title: J/K and two-electron integrals

findings.title: Hessian: ip1ip2 and ipvip1 compute twice the rows that ej/ek ever read (atoms B > A are discarded)
findings.evidence: Code: pyscf/pyscf/hessian/rhf.py:142 builds shls_slice=(A shells, all, all, all) for int2e_ip1ip2 (rhf.py:147) and int2e_ipvip1 (rhf.py:157). The results are only read in the loop at rhf.py:171, `for j0, ja in enumerate(atmlst[:i0+1])`, through vj1[:,:,q0:q1] and vk1[:,:,q0:q1] with q in atom B <= A. Those rows are the k index of ip1ip2 ('ji->s1kl', 'li->s1kj', 'lj->s1ki') and the j index of ipvip1 (its outputs are transposed into vj1/vk1). So every quartet with k (ip1ip2) or j (ipvip1) on an atom after A only feeds rows that are discarded. Each unordered atom pair is therefore computed twice. The same pattern is in hessian/uhf.py:158-203, in the RSH long-range loops of hessian/rks.py:89-116, and in hessian/uks.py:90-126. Measured with /tmp/claude-1000/-home-danny-Chemistry-my-pyscf/3d2aa02f-ca12-40eb-b5fd-b099754f302d/scratchpad/swarm/jk/hess_tri.py, 1 thread, ip1ip2 k range and ipvip1 j range cut to shells [0, max shl1 of atmlst[:i0+1]): benzene/SVP _partial_hess_ejk went from 33.12 s to 21.26 s (ipip1's unchanged 8 s included). ej and ek are bitwise identical (max diff 0.0), also with with_k=False and with a reversed atmlst. Ethylene went from 1.17 s to 0.79 s, also identical. Per-class 1-thread budget (hess_jk_parts.py) on benzene: ipip1 8.0, ip1ip2 16.3, ipvip1 8.3, make_h1 ip1 4.1 s, so ip1ip2+ipvip1 is 67%. Caffeine, extrapolated from per-atom timings of atom 9 (C) and atom 23 (H) (hess_screen_atom.py, ipip1_screen.py, h1_screen.py): ip1ip2 312, ipvip1 155, ipip1 147, make_h1 69, total 683 s at 1 thread. Caffeine atom 9 with screening on, before and after the cut: ip1ip2 13.40 to 7.96 s, ipvip1 6.94 to 4.06 s. Profile: summary.txt hess_caffeine_svp_b3lyp nr_direct_drv 107.761 s over 73 calls (1 ipip1 + 24 ip1ip2 + 24 ipvip1 + 24 make_h1). hess_benzene_svp_b3lyp nr_direct_drv 11.337 s over 37 calls.
findings.current_cost: hess_caffeine_svp_b3lyp: ip1ip2+ipvip1 ≈ 0.68 × 107.8 = 73 s of 181.2 s wall (40%). hess_benzene_svp_b3lyp: ≈ 0.67 × 11.34 = 7.6 s of 17.87 s (43%). hess_benzene_svp_pbe: ≈ 6.5 s of 15.64 s. caffeine r2SCAN Hessian (It13: J/K 92 s of 199 s): about 60 s.
findings.proposal: In _partial_hess_ejk (hessian/rhf.py, uhf.py) and the omega != 0 loops of hessian/rks.py and uks.py, set bsh1 = max(aoslices[ja][1] for ja in atmlst[:i0+1]) and nb = ao_loc[bsh1]. Pass shls_slice=(shl0,shl1,0,nbas,0,bsh1,0,nbas) to int2e_ip1ip2 and (shl0,shl1,0,bsh1,0,nbas,0,nbas) to int2e_ipvip1. vj1/vk1/veff then have shape (3,3,nb,nao): vj1[:,:,p0:p1] += vjk2[0].transpose(0,2,1)*.5 and vk1 += vjk2[1].transpose(0,2,1), as before. The max over atmlst keeps it correct for any atom list; it saves work for the default ordered list. About 15 changed lines per file; a working prototype is ejk_tri() in hess_tri.py.
findings.expected_gain: −47% of ip1ip2+ipvip1 work. Benzene measured 25.1 to 13.3 s at 1 thread. By bra-ket and i-j symmetry each atom pair is kept once: 1/2 plus half the diagonal pairs. Caffeine B3LYP Hessian: 0.47 × 467 s of the 683 s 1-thread budget = 32% of direct J/K, about −35 s of 181 s wall at 10 threads. Benzene B3LYP Hessian: about −3.6 s of 17.9 s, or more together with jk-par-blocks. Pure-functional Hessians save about the same share (J scripts only). It applies unchanged to UKS and RSH Hessians.
findings.exactness_notes: The skipped quartets only fed discarded rows. Verified bit-identical ej/ek at 1 thread (benzene, ethylene; with_k True/False; reversed atmlst). At 10 threads, CVHFnr_direct_drv already writes back blocks in dynamic order, so run-to-run rounding is unchanged in kind.

findings.title: Hessian derivative-integral J/K runs unscreened: _make_vhfopt is dead code (hasattr on an unsuffixed symbol), and make_h1 has no vhfopt
findings.evidence: pyscf/pyscf/hessian/rhf.py:190-192: `if not hasattr(libcvhf, vhf_intor): return None` uses 'int2e_ip1ip2', 'int2e_ipip1ipip2' and 'int2e_ipvip1ipvip2'. Only the _sph/_cart names exist. hasattr is False in this tree and in pyscf-base (checked: all three _make_vhfopt calls return None). So ipip1, ip1ip2 and ipvip1 all run with CVHFnoscreen. make_h1 (rhf.py:236, rks.py:155-176, uks.py:158-191) never passes a vhfopt. The path was never exercised: given a vhfopt, direct_bindm (scf/_vhf.py:792) calls _VHFOpt.set_dm on the ragged dm list [dm0[:,p0:p1], dm0[:,p0:p1], dm0], and numpy.asarray (_vhf.py:234) raises on that list (reproduced). The C prescreens already exist and match the scripts: hessian_screen.c:218 CVHFip1ip2_prescreen, :262 CVHFipip1_prescreen, :391 CVHFipvip1_prescreen. Measured at 1 thread on caffeine/SVP with a minao dm, dm_cond computed once from dm0 (hess_screen.py make_vhfopt_fixed, hess_screen_atom.py, ipip1_screen.py, h1_screen.py), unscreened vs screened: ip1ip2 atom 23 (H) 5.64→3.30 s, atom 9 (C) 18.25→13.40 s. ipvip1 2.94→2.04 s and 8.98→6.94 s. ipip1 (i on the atom) 2.94→2.01 s and 8.38→6.42 s. make_h1 int2e_ip1 with a conservative Schwarz×max|D| screen 1.45→0.98 s and 3.88→3.00 s. Max element change of these J/K matrices: 1.2e-13 to 7.4e-13. Benzene: 32.30 vs 33.78 s (nothing screened; +4.6% prescreen overhead). Quartet volume kept by q_ij·q_kl·max|D| > 1e-14 (screen_frac.py): benzene 0.99, caffeine 0.73-0.77, n-C20H42/SVP 0.19.
findings.current_cost: hess_caffeine_svp_b3lyp: all 73 direct J/K calls unscreened, 107.8 s of 181.2 s wall (59%). Hessians of 40-60 atom molecules: 80% or more of their derivative-integral quartets are ones that this screening would drop.
findings.proposal: (1) rhf.py:192: test hasattr(libcvhf, mol._add_suffix(vhf_intor)). (2) In _make_vhfopt, compute dm_cond once from the dms the scripts use: dm0 for RHF; [dm0, dm0a, dm0b] for UHF, since |dm0a| can exceed |dm0a+dm0b| off-diagonal. Then set vhfopt._dmcondname=None so direct_bindm's set_dm is a no-op. (3) Give make_h1 (rhf/rks/uhf/uks) a _VHFOpt for int2e_ip1 with q_cond from grad.rhf._calc_q_cond and a new 10-line prescreen in hessian_screen.c that tests D_ji, 2D_lk, D_li, D_ki, D_jk and D_jl (its four s2kl scripts). CVHFgrad_jk_prescreen misses D_ji and D_li: it gave 3.5e-11 errors here. (4) Build the same vhfopts under with_range_coulomb(omega) for the RSH calls. Optional: skip whole blocks by q_ij·max q_kl to recover the 4% prescreen cost on compact molecules.
findings.expected_gain: Caffeine, weighting the per-atom savings by the 1-thread class budget: ip1ip2 −29.5%, ipvip1 −24%, ipip1 −25%, make_h1 −25%. That is −27% of direct J/K alone (about −29 s of 181 s), or −18% (about −19 s) on top of jk-hess-tri, ±30% (two sample atoms). Together with jk-hess-tri the caffeine Hessian goes from 181 to about 127 s. For n-C20H42-size molecules the derivative-integral work drops about 4-5× (19% of the volume kept). No change for benzene.
findings.exactness_notes: This is a screening change, not new physics: it restores the Schwarz×density screen at direct_scf_tol=1e-14 that upstream wrote for these integrals (the same threshold the gradient uses). Measured deviations of the J/K matrices are ≤ 7.4e-13 (caffeine), so Hessian elements should move by roughly 1e-11, against validate.py's Hessian tolerance of 1e-7. Validate against pyscf-base before adopting it.

findings.title: CVHFnr_direct_drv has too few parallel tasks for small molecules and per-atom calls (64-AO blocks): benzene gradient J/K runs at 2.7x on 10 threads
findings.evidence: pyscf/pyscf/lib/vhf/nr_direct.c:398-430 parallelizes `omp for schedule(dynamic,1)` over (j,k,l) blocks of AO_BLOCK_SIZE=64 (nr_direct.h:22), with the i blocks inside each task. Benzene/SVP (nao 114) has 2 blocks per index, so 8 tasks, 6 non-empty under s2kl. I timed every task at 1 thread by restricting shls_slice to its blocks (task_balance.py) and simulated the dynamic schedule on 4 Zen 5 cores plus 6 Zen 5c at 0.72 relative speed. Benzene gradient int2e_ip1: 6 tasks, the largest 0.957 s of 3.577 s; predicted 1.33 s at 10 threads (2.69×), measured 1.298 s (summary.txt grad_benzene_svp_b3lyp nr_direct_drv). Benzene Hessian (per-class 1-thread times from hess_jk_parts.py, per-call speedups from the model): predicted 11.5 s, measured 11.34 s. With 32-AO blocks: gradient 40 tasks, largest 0.154 s, predicted 0.50 s (7.27×), with only +1.8% total 1-thread work. Per-atom ip1ip2 rises from 4.0× to 8.1× and make_h1 from 2.8× to 7.7×. Caffeine gradient: 7.45× at 64-AO blocks, 8.31× at 32 (modelled 6.10→5.54 s). Per-atom caffeine calls are already 7.5-8× at 64, and 32 adds per-task overhead there, so the choice should be adaptive. nr_direct.c:262 sizes keys_cache as size_limit/(AO_BLOCK_SIZE²·ncomp); with smaller blocks that bound must use the actual block size (or nblock²).
findings.current_cost: grad_benzene_svp_b3lyp: J/K 1.30 of 1.46 s wall (89%) at 2.7× parallel speedup. hess_benzene_svp_b3lyp: direct J/K 11.34 of 17.87 s (63%) at about 3.2× (36.8 s at 1 thread). grad_caffeine_svp_b3lyp: J/K 7.48 of 8.14 s at about 7.5×.
findings.proposal: In CVHFnr_direct_drv and CVHFnr_direct_ex_drv, pick the block size per call. Start at 64 and halve, down to 16, while the number of non-empty (j,k,l) tasks (k>=l blocks only for s2kl) is below about 4×omp_get_max_threads(). Pass the size to CVHFshls_block_partition and to CVHFallocate_JKArray, and size keys_cache from it.
findings.expected_gain: Benzene gradient 1.46 → about 0.66 s (J/K 1.30 → about 0.50 s). Benzene B3LYP Hessian direct J/K 11.3 → about 5.0 s (−6.3 s of 17.9 s); with jk-hess-tri, about 3.5 s. Caffeine gradient −0.6 s (−8%). Caffeine Hessian −2 to 3 s, from the all-atom ipip1 call and keeping the short early-atom calls of jk-hess-tri parallel.
findings.exactness_notes: Only the partition, and with it the order of the block write-backs, changes. That order is already dynamic (omp critical in completion order).

findings.title: In-core UKS SCF: two symmetric dms take the BLAS batch path at 2.7x the cost of the fused one-pass single-dm kernel
workloads: in-core UKS/ROKS hybrid SCF (nao up to about 370 at 20 GB)
findings.evidence: summary.txt: scf_caffeine+_svp_b3lyp_uks _incore_s8_batch 5.502 s over 25 calls = 220 ms per call. scf_caffeine_svp_b3lyp: 1.392 s over 17 calls = 82 ms per call. Same nao and the same ERIs. dft/uks.py:98 calls get_jk with _dm of shape (2,nao,nao) and dft/uks.py:103 sums vj[0]+vj[1]. scf/_vhf.py:509-520 takes CVHFnrs8_incore_jk_1dm (nr_incore_batch.c:282, one pass over the ERIs) only when n_dm == 1. Two dms go to CVHFnrs8_incore_vj_batch (nr_incore_batch.c:45: tile copies plus dgemm with m=2) and CVHFnrs8_incore_vk_batch (nr_incore_batch.c:126: each packed row memcpy'd into a square M plus 2 dsymm with 2 columns). That is two passes plus copies. 1-thread microbenchmark (uks_incore.py, benzene/SVP, 0.17 GB ERIs): 1 dm fused J+K 13.6 ms; 2 dms batch 43.2 ms (J 10.5 ms, K 32.3 ms); even 2 × fused would be 27.3 ms.
findings.current_cost: scf_caffeine+_svp_b3lyp_uks: 5.50 s of 21.16 s wall (26%) in in-core J/K.
findings.proposal: Generalize CVHFnrs8_incore_jk_1dm to n ≤ 4 symmetric dms: loop over the dms inside _jk_1dm_row_body on the row already in cache, with J for each dm (or a J-of-sum flag, since UKS only needs vj[0]+vj[1]). Route sym_k batches with n_dm ≤ 4 to it from _incore_s8_batch. Interim: loop the existing 1-dm kernel per dm when n_dm ≤ 3, which saves about 1.4 s.
findings.expected_gain: One streaming pass over the 3.7 GB with twice the K FMAs is still close to bandwidth-bound (It7: J alone 43 ms, K alone 51 ms, J+K 56 ms). Estimated 100-120 ms per call instead of 220: −2.5 to 3.0 s of 21.2 s (−12 to 14%) for scf_caffeine+_svp_b3lyp_uks.
findings.exactness_notes: Same integrals and the same symmetric-K formulation as the 1-dm kernel. Only the summation order differs: 1-dm path vs batch path agree to about 5e-15 here.

findings.title: Gradient J/K: s8 driver with translational invariance (3 of 4 center derivatives) and contraction straight to dE/dR
findings.evidence: grad/rhf.py:191-205: direct_mapdm on int2e_ip1, s2kl, with 'lk->s1ij' and 'jk->s1il'. The s2kl loop evaluates (i'j|kl) for (ij|kl), (ji|kl), (kl|ij) and (lk|ij): 4 ip1 calls per s8 orbit, where 3 plus ∂l = −(∂i+∂j+∂k) suffice. Fewer are needed when shells share an atom. 1-thread native profile native_grad_caffeine_svp_b3lyp.txt (104.7 s including the SCF): CVHFnr_direct_drv 55.9%, int2e_ip1_sph 45.1% (so integrals are about 81% of gradient J/K), contraction kernels nrs2kl_jk_s1il 5.4% + nrs2kl_lk_s1ij 3.8% (about 16%). The RKS gradient only contracts vhf with dm0 rows per atom (grad_elec), so the JKArray matrices are not needed. Already listed in NOTES 'Next iterations' item 1; not done or rejected. Re-quantified here on the It13 tree.
findings.current_cost: grad_caffeine_svp_b3lyp: J/K 7.48 of 8.14 s (92%). grad_c20h42_svp_b3lyp: 26.55 of 28.26 s (94%). grad_benzene_svp_b3lyp: 1.30 of 1.46 s.
findings.proposal: New C driver (nr_direct.c or a new file) used by grad_elec when only the energy gradient is needed. Loop over s8 shell quartets with the existing CVHFgrad_jk_prescreen-style screen. Evaluate int2e_ip1 for (i,j,k,l), (j,i,k,l) and (k,l,i,j), and drop the evaluation of the center whose derivative is most expensive (highest l) or that shares an atom. Get the 4th center by translational invariance. Contract each with Γ = D_ij D_kl − (hyb/4)(D_ik D_jl + D_il D_jk), with s8 weights, into thread-private de[natm,3]. No JKArray.
findings.expected_gain: −25% of integral evaluations (more where two shells sit on one atom) plus part of the contraction: about −21 to 27% of gradient J/K. Caffeine −1.6 to 2.0 s of 8.1 s; n-C20H42 −5.6 to 7.2 s of 28.3 s.
findings.exactness_notes: Same integrals; the 4th derivative is obtained from translational invariance, which holds analytically and in qcint to about 1e-14 relative. qcint's SGX invariance is 7e-12 (NOTES), so check gradients to 1e-10. validate.py's gradient tolerance is 1e-8.

findings.title: Hessian/gradient JKArray contractions cost 21-28% of each derivative J/K call, about 0.15 s per script on a 1.9 s call; fuse the scripts of a call
findings.evidence: script_cost.py, benzene C atom, int2e_ip1ip2, 1 thread: 1 script (ji) 1.559 s, +li 1.698 s, +lj 1.730 s, all 3 1.870 s. Each script costs about 0.15 s, so contraction is about 25% of the call. hess_jk_parts.py: ipvip1 2 vs 1 script 1.005 vs 0.899 s (≈21%), make_h1 int2e_ip1 4 vs 1 script 0.495 vs 0.392 s (≈28%), ipip1 7.99 vs 7.14 s (≈21%). Each script does 1.87e8 multiply-adds in 0.15 s, about 1.25 GFMA/s. That is overhead-bound: per quartet and per script, LOCATE in JKArray (nr_direct_dot.c:180-206) plus 9-component nests over 1-5 wide dims (DEF_NRS1_CONTRACT, nr_direct_dot.c:207-224), with no restrict. Native benzene Hessian profile: nr_direct_dot.c kernels sum to 9.5% of 93 s = 8.8 s, against 47.7 s in CVHFnr_direct_drv (18%).
findings.current_cost: hess_caffeine_svp_b3lyp: about 23% of 107.8 s ≈ 25 s (about 12 s after jk-hess-tri and jk-hess-screen). hess_benzene_svp_b3lyp: about 2.6 s of 11.3 s. grad_caffeine: about 16% of 7.48 s.
findings.proposal: Add fused JKOperators for the fixed script sets of the Hessian and gradient: ip1ip2 (ji->s1kl, li->s1kj, lj->s1ki), ipvip1 (lk->s1ij, li->s1kj), ipip1 (lk->s1ij, jk->s1il), make_h1 (4 scripts) and gradient (lk->s1ij, jk->s1il). Each LOCATEs its output blocks once per quartet, hoists the dm values, and runs one loop nest per component doing all FMAs on the integral just loaded, with restrict pointers. hessian/rhf.py would request the fused script names.
findings.expected_gain: Contraction from 21-28% to about 10% of each call: about −12% of Hessian direct J/K (caffeine −12 s now, −6 s after tri+screen) and −5% of gradient J/K (caffeine −0.4 s). This is an estimate; no prototype was built.
findings.exactness_notes: If each output keeps its current loop order within a quartet, sums are bit-identical. A reordered loop nest gives rounding-level differences.

ruled_out:
All timings are at 1 thread (scripts under /tmp/claude-1000/-home-danny-Chemistry-my-pyscf/3d2aa02f-ca12-40eb-b5fd-b099754f302d/scratchpad/swarm/jk/) unless 10-thread profile numbers from bench/results/profile-it13 are cited.

(1) Contracting derivative integrals in the Cartesian basis to skip c2s: c2s_sph_2e1 + d_ket_cart2spheric + dcopy_iklj are 7.7% of the 1-thread caffeine-gradient run, about 17% of int2e_ip1's 45% inclusive time. Tried it with D_cart = C D C^T, V = C^T V_cart C (cart_contract.py): benzene gradient J/K 3.483 s spherical vs 3.535 s Cartesian, identical to 6e-14. No gain.

(2) In-core ERI fill (fill_nr_s8.c): store_ij copy plus zero fill is about 1.7% of the 1-thread caffeine SCF (0.8 s of 46.9 s), and getints4c is 0.9 s at 10 threads, roughly scaling. Not worth it.

(3) Semi-direct read path: _batch_k_body_s 24.6% and _batch_j_body_s 14.5% of the 1-thread alkane SCF, about 5.7 s of 18.8 s at 10 threads for its 10 cache-reading calls. It9 already tried inlining and transposed accumulation. My count is about 10 memory ops per element, roughly 80-150 cycles per 14-integral quartet, so the kernels are op-bound rather than branch-bound. Sorting stored quartets by shape is possible only for complete caches (the uncached loop is skipped at nr_direct_batch.c:563-565). Untested, so no confident gain.

(4) In-core long-range ERIs for RSH: CAM-B3LYP LR-K is semi-direct at 2.585 s / 15 calls (172 ms vs about 55 ms for the in-core K-only kernel). Net about 1 s of 10.7 s after the build, for 3.7 GB more RAM; bigger only for RSH-TDDFT, which is not benchmarked.

(5) TDA/TDDFT in-core K: tda_caffeine_svp_b3lyp _incore_s8_batch is 0.55 s/call, near the BLAS-3 bound (about 0.4 s of flops for 20 non-symmetric dms). TDA needs hermi=0. A sym/antisym split for RPA keeps the same K flops (w=1+1 vs 2).

(6) CPHF in-core J/K in Hessians: 8.6 s over 8 calls of up to 72 symmetric dms, at BLAS-3 rate. An MO-basis or low-rank K would need an O(N^5) transform (about 3.6e12 flops), which costs more.

(7) UKS direct/semi-direct batch pads 2 dms to npad=4: 4-wide vectors give the same instruction count as 2 lanes. Nothing to gain.

(8) ipip1 xy=yx duplicate components: about 1/3 of that class's gout and contraction, roughly 3% of Hessian J/K. Needs a qcint change. Low priority.

(9) A combined second-derivative integral (one g-array for ipip1/ipvip1/ip1ip2/ip1) could be large but is an L-effort qcint autocode plus driver project.

(10) 3-of-4 translational invariance for make_h1 is feasible but would need scatter into 4 atoms' matrices. Deferred.

(11) DF J is 0.28 s in scf_caffeine_tzvp_dfpbe; nothing left. Semi-direct index/histogram setup is 0.5 s (caffeine TZVP) and 2.0 s (alkane TZVP), about 1%.

(12) Partial-cache TZVP SCFs (scf_caffeine_tzvp_b3lyp 68.8 s and scf_c20h42_tzvp_pbe 136 s in _direct_s8_batch) are bound by qcint evaluation of the uncached quartets. No exact lever beyond integral speed and the memory budget. Float32 storage of small integrals would be an approximation.

(13) The SCF conv_check extra cycle is semantics; not touched.

(14) Out of my area but large and exact: hessian/rhf.py hess_elec einsums with optimize=False. 'xpq,pi,qj->xij' takes 0.247 s × 24 atoms (vs 0.0014 s with optimize=True), 'ypi,qi,i->ypq' 5.6 ms × 300, 'ypi,qi->ypq' 2.6 ms × 300. That is about 8.4 s of the 14.9 s c_einsum in hess_caffeine_svp_b3lyp; flagged for the Hessian/numpy analyst.

(15) Gradient prescreen and block size for the alkane: 288 tasks, already balanced.

verdicts.checked: Read hessian/rhf.py:139-182. ip1ip2 outputs ('ji->s1kl', 'li->s1kj', 'lj->s1ki') have k as the row index that is later sliced as vj1[:,:,q0:q1]. ipvip1 outputs are transposed, so j becomes that row index. Only atoms B in atmlst[:i0+1] are read. The same loops exist in uhf.py:158-203, rks.py:89-116 and uks.py:90-126. Checked hasattr: the per-atom calls run with vhfopt=None. I ran the analyst's ejk_tri myself at 1 thread on a 6-atom H2O+CH2 molecule: original 1.08 s, triangle 0.73 s; ej and ek differ by exactly 0.0 with the default, permuted ([2,0,5,1,4,3]) and subset ([3,1]) atom lists. I also wrote a 10-thread model (jk-verify/tri_model.py): it times every (j,k,l) 64-AO task of every per-atom call at 1 thread and runs the analyst's 4 fast + 6 slow dynamic-schedule simulation on them. The model reproduces the measured 11.3 s benzene J/K. Benzene ip1ip2+ipvip1 at 1 thread: 23.57 -> 13.15 s (-44%). Modelled at 10 threads: 6.74 -> 5.26 s, only -1.5 s. Tri does not shrink the largest 64-AO task of the C4/C5/H calls (task counts stay 8/6), so with few tasks the 1-thread saving does not reach wall time. With 32-AO blocks the same pair goes 3.09 -> 1.81 s. Profile numbers recomputed: caffeine 107.761 s over 73 calls = 1+24+24+24; benzene 11.337 s over 37 calls.
verdicts.comment: Real and bitwise exact. It is not in NOTES. The 10-thread gain is overstated for small molecules: benzene B3LYP and PBE Hessians save about 1.3-1.5 s (-8%), not 3.6 s. They save the full share only together with jk-par-blocks. Caffeine lists its 14 heavy atoms first, so the early (expensive) calls drop to about 16 tasks; I estimate -28 to -33 s of 181 s (the analyst's -35 s needs good balance in those short calls). The r2SCAN caffeine Hessian saves about the same share of its 92 s J/K. Use the max over atmlst as proposed; I verified it with a non-ordered subset list.
verdicts.cost_seconds: hess_caffeine_svp_b3lyp: about 73 s (0.68 x 107.8) in ip1ip2+ipvip1. hess_benzene_svp_b3lyp: about 6.7 s modelled at 10 threads. hess_benzene_svp_pbe: about 6 s.
verdicts.gain_estimate: Caffeine B3LYP Hessian -28 to -33 s of 181 s (-16 to -18%). Caffeine r2SCAN about -25 s. Benzene B3LYP/PBE Hessians -1.3 to -1.5 s (-8 to -9%) alone, or -1.3 s on top of jk-par-blocks.

verdicts.checked: Ran hasattr on libcvhf myself. 'int2e_ip1ip2', 'int2e_ipip1ipip2' and 'int2e_ipvip1ipvip2' are all False, while 'int2e_ip1ip2_sph' and CVHFip1ip2/ipvip1/ipip1_prescreen exist, and _make_vhfopt returns None. pyscf-base has the same code (rhf.py:182), so upstream Hessians also run unscreened. Read the set_dm path: _vhf.py:225-245 calls numpy.asarray on the dm list, so the ragged list would fail; direct_bindm:792. The grad get_jk uses CVHFgrad_jk_prescreen at the same direct_scf_tol. The analyst's timings used a minao dm, so I tested whether that inflates the gain. On caffeine atoms 23 and 9, ip1ip2 screened with a Huckel (molecular, more delocalized) dm took 2.64 s and 9.23 s, against 3.24 s and 11.03 s with minao in my run, so the gain does not come from minao's atom-local density. The analyst's unscreened references were 5.64 s and 18.25 s.
verdicts.comment: The bug and the speed-up are real. Exactness: this adds screening that upstream does not apply in practice. The policy allows a screening change only if results stay within tolerance. Restoring the intended Schwarz x density screen at direct_scf_tol=1e-14 gives J/K changes of 1e-13 to 7e-13, so Hessian elements should move by about 1e-11; energies are untouched. That is within the policy, provided it is validated against pyscf-base on all Hessian cases and documented as a deviation from upstream's actual behaviour. Design corrections: (a) the +4.6% prescreen cost on benzene should be avoided by default, for example by skipping the vhfopt when the kept-volume estimate is near 1, or by block-level skips; it is not optional; (b) make_h1 needs the new C prescreen (CVHFgrad_jk_prescreen misses D_ji and D_li, with 3.5e-11 errors); (c) UHF needs dm_cond over dm0, dm0a and dm0b. The gain estimates (+-30%, from two sample atoms) are reasonable. Per-atom calls already scale 7.5-8x, so the 1-thread percentages carry over to 10 threads.
verdicts.cost_seconds: hess_caffeine_svp_b3lyp: 107.8 s of unscreened direct J/K (73 calls). hess_benzene_*: about 11 s with nothing to screen.
verdicts.gain_estimate: Caffeine B3LYP Hessian about -25 to -29 s alone, or about -15 to -20 s after jk-hess-tri. Similar shares for the r2SCAN caffeine Hessian. Benzene 0 (must not regress by about 0.5 s). Large for molecules over 40 atoms.

verdicts.checked: Read nr_direct.c:398-470: a dynamic,1 omp for over nblock_j*nblock_k*nblock_l with the i blocks inside each task, AO_BLOCK_SIZE=64 (nr_direct.h:22). keys_cache is sized at :262 as size_limit/(64^2*ncomp), so it must change with smaller blocks. The write-back is under omp critical in completion order, so this is rounding-only. CVHFdot_nrs2kl calls CVHFdot_nrs1 for k>l blocks. My own task model (all per-atom ip1ip2/ipvip1 tasks of benzene timed at 1 thread, simulated on 4+6 cores) gives ip1ip2+ipvip1 at 10 threads: 6.74 s (64-AO blocks) -> 3.09 s (32-AO blocks), with 1-thread work up 2-3%. The same model reproduces the measured 11.3 s benzene Hessian J/K at 64. Measured profile: grad_benzene_svp_b3lyp nr_direct_drv 1.298 s of 1.46 s; hess_benzene_svp_b3lyp 11.337 s of 17.87 s.
verdicts.comment: NOTES It7 records only that 32/16-AO blocks gained 3-5% on the caffeine direct SCF. That was measured but not adopted or rejected, and it is consistent with the analyst's point that the gain is concentrated in small-task-count calls, hence the adaptive choice. The model's numbers support the analyst's benzene estimates (Hessian J/K about 11.3 -> about 5 s; with tri about 3.5 s). Real hardware will be a little worse than the ideal schedule, so I expect -5 to -6 s on the benzene Hessian. Caffeine per-atom calls already scale 7.5-8x, so the gain there is small except for the short early-atom calls after jk-hess-tri.
verdicts.cost_seconds: grad_benzene_svp_b3lyp 1.30 s of 1.46 s; hess_benzene_svp_b3lyp 11.34 s and hess_benzene_svp_pbe 9.71 s direct J/K; grad_caffeine_svp_b3lyp 7.48 s
verdicts.gain_estimate: Benzene B3LYP/PBE Hessians -5 to -6 s of 17.9/15.6 s (about -30 to -35%). Benzene gradient -0.6 to -0.8 s of 1.46 s. Caffeine gradient about -0.5 s. Caffeine Hessian -1 to -3 s.

verdicts.checked: summary.txt: scf_caffeine+_svp_b3lyp_uks _incore_s8_batch 5.502 s / 25 calls = 220 ms; scf_caffeine_svp_b3lyp 1.392 s / 17 = 82 ms. Read _vhf.py:509-560: the fused CVHFnrs8_incore_jk_1dm is taken only when n_dm == 1. Otherwise J goes through CVHFnrs8_incore_vj_batch and K through the dsymm batch path, two passes. dft/uks.py:98-103 passes the (2,nao,nao) dm and sums vj[0]+vj[1]. The 1-thread native RKS profile shows _jk_1dm_row_body at 19% of the SCF. NOTES It7 A/E built these paths with no note on a UKS variant.
verdicts.comment: Exact up to summation order (rounding). One C-level pass with J of the summed dm (or J per dm) and K for both dms in the row body. The 82 ms 1-dm call is about 56 ms of kernel plus Python overhead (pack_tril, symmetry check, unpack, z+z.T), so a 2-dm call should land near 110-130 ms. The interim per-dm loop (2 x 82 ms) saves about 1.4 s, as stated. The pure-functional UKS (scf_benzene+_svp_r2scan_uks) J-only n_dm=2 call could likewise use the 1-dm J kernel on the summed dm, but that workload is small.
verdicts.cost_seconds: scf_caffeine+_svp_b3lyp_uks: 5.50 s of 21.16 s
verdicts.gain_estimate: -2.3 to -2.8 s of 21.2 s (-11 to -13%); interim per-dm loop -1.4 s

verdicts.checked: grad/rhf.py:191-205: direct_mapdm on int2e_ip1 with s2kl and scripts ('lk->s1ij', 'jk->s1il'), so the loop over all i, all j and k>=l visits 4 ip1 evaluations per general s8 orbit. Native 1-thread profile: get_jk 56.0%, CVHFnr_direct_drv 55.9%, int2e_ip1_sph 45.1% inclusive (81% of J/K), nrs2kl_jk_s1il 5.4% + nrs2kl_lk_s1ij 3.8% (16%). CVHFdot_nrs1 shows under the gradient because CVHFdot_nrs2kl delegates its k>l blocks to it. summary.txt: grad_caffeine J/K 7.482 of 8.14 s, alkane 26.554 of 28.26 s, benzene 1.298 of 1.46 s. NOTES 'Next iterations' item 1 lists exactly this (-25%, needs a driver that contracts inside the loop): proposed, neither done nor rejected.
verdicts.comment: Exact up to rounding: translational invariance of the analytic 4-center integrals holds to about 1e-14 relative in qcint (the 7e-12 NOTES item is SGX grid response, not this). Per-orbit instead of per-ordering screening is a screening-level difference that should be validated, though the gradient prescreen is already Schwarz x density. Extra savings are available where centers share an atom ((ii|kl) needs 2 of 3, same-atom pairs fewer) and from skipping one-atom quartets. Effort L: grad_elec/RKS get_veff must take a dE path, RSH LR-K needs its own pass, and the hybrid weight goes into Gamma. Gains are slightly below the analyst's upper bound, because the contraction into Gamma is not free.
verdicts.cost_seconds: grad_caffeine_svp_b3lyp 7.48 s; grad_c20h42_svp_b3lyp 26.55 s; grad_benzene_svp_b3lyp 1.30 s
verdicts.gain_estimate: About -20 to -25% of gradient J/K: caffeine -1.5 to -1.8 s of 8.1 s; n-C20H42 -5.3 to -6.5 s of 28.3 s; benzene about -0.25 s.

verdicts.checked: Read nr_direct_dot.c:180-224. LOCATE runs per output per quartet, and DEF_NRS1_CONTRACT does v[...] += eri*dm with possible aliasing and no restrict, so the accumulator is stored on every inner iteration. Native benzene Hessian profile (1 thread): the nr_direct_dot kernels sum to about 9.5% (nrs2kl_lk_s1ij 2.2, nrs1_lj_s1ki 1.8, nrs1_li_s1kj 1.6, nrs2kl_jk_s1il 1.4, nrs2kl_li_s1kj 1.4, nrs1_ji_s1kl 1.1), against 51.3% in CVHFnr_direct_drv, which is 18.5% of direct J/K. The analyst's 21-28% comes from marginal-script timings, which also include LOCATE and cache effects. Gradient contraction is 16% (native caffeine gradient). There is no NOTES entry on these kernels.
verdicts.comment: A real but smaller lever than claimed, with no prototype. The contraction is about 18-24% of Hessian direct J/K. Fusing plus restrict could plausibly halve it, not cut it to 10% on every class. A first, cheaper step is restrict pointers and register-held accumulators in the existing per-script kernels: with the same loop order this is bitwise identical, and it gets most of the store traffic out. Full fusion that reorders loops is rounding-only. The gain shrinks proportionally once jk-hess-tri and jk-hess-screen cut the quartet count.
verdicts.cost_seconds: hess_caffeine_svp_b3lyp: about 19-25 s of contraction in 107.8 s of direct J/K (about 11-14 s after tri+screen); hess_benzene_svp_b3lyp about 2.1-2.6 s; grad_caffeine about 1.2 s
verdicts.gain_estimate: Caffeine Hessian -6 to -10 s now, -3 to -5 s after tri+screen. Benzene Hessians -0.7 to -1.1 s. Caffeine gradient -0.3 to -0.5 s. Low confidence.

title: XC integration in SCF and the direct grid pipeline

findings.title: numpy's and scipy's bundled OpenBLAS pools busy-spin for 134 ms after every threaded call and compete with PySCF's OpenMP XC kernels; the per-block numpy.dot(den, exc) in nr_rks/nr_uks re-arms them every block
workloads: (likely also tda/tddft/hess: their solvers call numpy BLAS between OpenMP kernels)
findings.evidence:
Mechanism, from source. In OpenBLAS driver/others/blas_server.c:405-430, a pthread worker waits for work in a loop whose YIELDING is 8 nops on x86_64 (common.h:393-397). It keeps spinning until rpcc()-last_tick > thread_timeout = 1<<28 (blas_server.c:160-164). With the 1996.25 MHz TSC (kernel log) that is 134 ms of spinning per worker. kernel/x86_64/ddot.c:174-177 threads every ddot with n > 10000. numpy's bundled libscipy_openblas64_ (0.3.34.106, pthreads) and scipy's libscipy_openblas (0.3.31.dev) are separate pools; `strings` shows both read OPENBLAS_THREAD_TIMEOUT and OMP_NUM_THREADS, so each has 10 threads. Profile config N sets no OPENBLAS_* variable (results JSON meta), and the run started at loadavg 2.17. PySCF's own OpenBLAS is the OpenMP build and shares libgomp.
Triggers. numint.py:1312 (fused nr_rks), 1339-1340 (fused nr_uks), 1940, 2069-2070 and 2206 call numpy.dot(den, exc) on 26k-67k points once per block (5 blocks per cycle on caffeine, about 60 ms apart). Every cycle, scipy eigh, make_rdm1 (scf/hf.py:867, numpy dgemm) and DIIS (lib/diis.py:228/326, ddot over nao^2) arm both pools just before get_veff calls nr_rks: 10 OpenMP threads plus 18 spinners on 20 logical CPUs. The grid case calls np.dot(exc*rho0, weights) on every 50k-point chunk (bench/cases.py grid_case).
Anomalies in the profiles (summary.txt):
- scf_caffeine_svp_pbe: get_overlap_cond takes 0.277 s / 54 calls = 5.1 ms per call, vs 0.138 ms at 1 thread (probe1); condense takes 0.237 s / 36 = 6.6 ms vs 0.048 ms. In UKS they take 4.4 and 4.8 ms. Both are tiny OpenMP regions that run right after eigh and make_rdm1.
- libxc _eval_xc inside the SCF: B3LYP 0.672 s / (17 x 294,800 points) = 134 ns/pt; PBE 166; r2SCAN 223. micro_libxc in the same run, at 10 threads with no numpy BLAS in its loop: 36 / 56 / 79 ns/pt. At 1 thread (probe1, probe3): 171 / 200 / 424-460 ns/pt, with real and random densities costing the same. So inside the SCF, libxc gets only 1.3-2x from 10 threads.
- 1-thread native SCF profile: nr_rks is 62.7% of 46.87 s = 29.4 s, vs ~6.6 s at 10 threads (4.5x). getints4c, which is compute-bound and runs mostly outside the spin windows, goes from 7.1 s to 0.95 s (7.5x).
- grid_caffeine_svp: eval_gto takes 1.70 s at 10 threads vs ~3.6 s at 1 thread (2.1x). probe2 measured 0.093 / 0.136 / 0.242 s per 50k-point chunk for deriv 0/1/2, i.e. 6x0.093 + 12x0.136 + 6x0.242. eval_rho's GEMMs run at ~188 GFLOP/s vs 257 GFLOP/s for the same shape in micro_gemm, and its libxc is 2.6x slower than micro_libxc.
findings.current_cost:
Not separable without a 10-thread A/B. Excess visible in the profiles:
- caffeine/SVP B3LYP: libxc 0.49 s; get_overlap_cond and condense 0.48 s; the XC loop (~6.6 s of 10.03 s) scales 4.5x vs ~7x expected.
- PBE: libxc excess 0.58 s. r2SCAN: 0.68 s.
- caffeine+ UKS: libxc 1.52 s, setup calls 1.02 s, xc_kernels 9.87 s of 21.16 s.
- benzene+ UKS r2SCAN: libxc 1.085 s of 4.09 s.
- grid_caffeine_svp: most of its 3.64 s runs inside the windows (eval_gto 1.70 s, GEMM 1.32 s, libxc 0.15 s).
findings.proposal:
(a) Configuration, no code. Export OPENBLAS_THREAD_TIMEOUT in scripts/pyscf-env.sh, document it for user scripts, and add it to bench/common.py worker_env, which currently drops every OPENBLAS_* variable. Both bundled copies read it: the minimum is 4 (16 ticks); about 18-20 (0.13-0.5 ms) keeps back-to-back calls, e.g. inside eigh, warm.
(b) Code, defense in depth for users who do not set it. Replace numpy.dot(den, exc) in the per-block loops (numint.py:1312, 1339-1340, 1940, 2069-2070, 2206) with a non-BLAS reduction such as numpy.einsum('i,i->', den, exc), or accumulate in C. nr_rks/nr_uks and the J/K that follows then run without re-armed spinners.
Verify with: run_bench.py --tag spin --reps 2 --cases scf_caffeine_svp_b3lyp,scf_caffeine+_svp_b3lyp_uks,scf_benzene+_svp_r2scan_uks,grid_caffeine_svp A=pyscf:PYSCF_MAX_MEMORY=20000 B=pyscf:PYSCF_MAX_MEMORY=20000,OPENBLAS_THREAD_TIMEOUT=4. Optionally add C=...OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS=1 as a bound.
findings.expected_gain:
Assuming the XC loop reaches the ~6.5-7x scaling that getints4c shows in the same runs:
- caffeine/SVP PBE, B3LYP, r2SCAN SCF: -1.5 to -2.5 s each (15-25%).
- caffeine+ UKS: -3 to -4.5 s (15-20%).
- benzene+ UKS r2SCAN: -0.8 to -1.3 s (20-30%).
- grid_caffeine_svp: -1.0 to -1.5 s (25-40%). eval_gto would move toward ~0.7 s, the GEMM toward the micro rate, libxc toward ~0.06 s.
- The J/K that runs right after nr_rks and the TDA/Hessian solvers should gain too (not quantified).
The mechanism is certain; the magnitude is inferred.
findings.exactness_notes: (a) changes thread scheduling only, so results are bitwise identical. (b) changes the summation order of excsum by ~1e-16 relative; it is energy-only, does not feed the Fock matrix, and is no longer thread-count dependent.

findings.title: GGA densities on the MO path take 4 GEMMs per group where 2 suffice (Z = C·v0, as It13's low-rank kernel already does); the MO/dm path choice is a pair-mask heuristic, not a flop count
findings.evidence:
nr_numint_fused.c:455-482: for each 224-point group, VXCfused_eval_rho_mo computes v0 = ao0·C (dgemm ng x nocc x ns). For GGA it then runs three more GEMMs, v1 = ao_c·C for c = 1..3, only to form grad rho_c = 2 sum_o v0·v1.
With Z = C·v0 (one GEMM of the same size), grad rho_c = 2 sum_n ao_c[n,k]·Z[n,k] (the existing _contract_group). This is the trick It13 B uses in VXCfused_eval_rho_lowrank.
probe2, caffeine/SVP SCF grid: 1317 groups, ns mean 154 (max 231), nocc 51. Density GEMMs cost 18.6 GFLOP/cycle now and 9.3 with Z; the dm path would cost 14.9; the GGA Vxc GEMM costs 14.9. Total XC GEMM work drops from 33.5 to 24.2 GFLOP/cycle (-28%).
_rho1_preferred (numint.py:1016-1024) chooses the MO path for caffeine/SVP because the pair-mask ratio is 4.046 against a threshold of 4 (probe1), i.e. by a hair.
1-thread native SCF profile: VXCfused_eval_rho_mo is 29.4% inclusive (13.8 s). About 9.5 s of it is BLAS (BLAS inclusive 37.6% minus the dot_wv GEMM), ~3 s is _eval_group and 0.7 s is _contract_mo.
eval_rho2's GGA branch (numint.py:408-414) has the same 4-GEMM pattern.
findings.current_cost: _rho_kernel at 10 threads: caffeine/SVP PBE 2.83 s, B3LYP 2.50 s, CAM-B3LYP 1.81 s; DF-TZVP 3.97 s (of 14.96 s); caffeine+ UKS 4.58 s (of 21.16 s).
findings.proposal:
In VXCfused_eval_rho_mo, for nderiv == 1, after v0 and rho0:
- one dgemm('N','N', ng, ns, nc, v0, ng, cbuf, nc) gives Z[ns,ng];
- rho_c = 2·_contract_group(aobuf + c·ns·ng, Z) for c = 1..3.
Meta-GGA stays unchanged, because tau needs every ao_c·C.
For the fused path, replace _rho1_preferred with a flop test summed over groups, as lowrank_cheaper does: MO+Z costs 4·ng·ns·nocc and the dm path 2·ng·ns^2. Alternatively choose per group inside one kernel that receives both cmo and dm.
Apply the same rewrite to eval_rho2's GGA branch. test_fused_xc asserts bit-for-bit equality between the fused and block_loop paths, so change both identically or move those asserts to ~1e-13.
findings.expected_gain:
Halves the density GEMM flops for GGA and hybrid-GGA RKS/UKS. The extra contraction (3·ns·ng per group, read from L2) gives back ~10-15%.
- caffeine/SVP PBE: -0.7 s; B3LYP: -0.65 s (6.5-7%).
- DF-TZVP (ns ~290): -1.2 to -1.6 s (8-11%).
- caffeine+ UKS: -1.0 to -1.3 s (5-6%).
No gain for meta-GGA or for the SVP alkane, where ns ~159 ~ 2·nocc. Absolute savings shrink by ~30% if xc-blas-spin lands first.
findings.exactness_notes: The summation order changes (sum over n of ao_c·(C C^T ao0) instead of sum over o of (ao0 C)(ao_c C)); expect differences of ~1e-15 relative in rho.

findings.title: VV10 (NLC) runs an O(N^2) pair loop with three divisions per pair over the full level-3 grid every SCF cycle: ~17-20 s per cycle for caffeine
workloads: VV10 functionals (wB97M-V, wB97X-V, B97M-V, SCAN-rVV10) in SCF, gradients and Hessians (not in the bench set)
findings.evidence:
VXC_vv10nlc (nr_numint.c:549-583, identical to pyscf-base) loops over every outer x inner point pair. Each pair costs three divisions, and the F/U/W accumulations are scalar FP reductions that GCC -O2 -msse3 cannot vectorize without reassociation.
nr_nlc_vxc (numint.py:2153-2221) calls it every cycle with the full nlcgrids as both sets. RKS.nlcgrids defaults to level 3, like the main grid (rks.py:357-359, no __config__ override).
probe4 (caffeine/def2-SVP, wB97M-V, minao density, 1 thread): 294,800 NLC points, of which 275,681 have rho >= 1e-8, giving 7.6e10 pairs. At 1.70 ns/pair, one call takes 129 s at 1 thread, which is ~17-20 s at 10 threads.
The gradient and Hessian VV10 kernels (nr_numint.c:585-660) have the same O(N^2) structure.
findings.current_cost: caffeine/SVP with a VV10 functional: ~17-20 s per SCF cycle at 10 threads, ~250-300 s per SCF. That is 20-30x the rest of a caffeine SVP SCF (~10 s).
findings.proposal:
1. One division per pair: inv = 1/(g·gp·gt); T = RpW·inv; 1/g + 1/gt = gp·(g+gt)·inv.
2. Store coordinates as [3,N] (SoA) and use #pragma omp simd reduction(+:F,U,W). Compile this file's VV10 kernels with -mavx2 -mfma, or with target_clones adding an AVX-512 variant.
3. In nr_nlc_vxc the inner and outer sets are the same points, and W0/K are bitwise equal to W0p/Kp (same expressions on the same rho). So g_i·g_j·(g_i+g_j) is symmetric: evaluate each unordered pair once in (i-tile, j-tile >= i-tile) blocks, add to both i and j, and reduce per-tile partials in tile order so the result is deterministic.
Apply the same to VXC_vv10nlc_grad and the Hessian kernel.
findings.expected_gain: One division plus 4-8-wide SIMD gives ~2-2.5x; symmetry gives another ~2x; together 3-5x per call. That is -11 to -16 s per SCF cycle on caffeine/SVP: a 15-cycle wB97M-V SCF would go from ~250-300 s to ~60-100 s. The saving grows as N^2 for larger molecules.
findings.exactness_notes: Summation order and the algebraic rewrite of the reciprocals change the last bits; expect differences of ~1e-14 relative in the NLC energy and potential.

findings.title: nr_rks/nr_uks run the pair-mask setup (get_overlap_cond, condense_to_shell) 3-5 times per call, and the fused path uses none of it except one ratio
findings.evidence:
In nr_rks, numint.py:1918 calls _gen_rho_evaluator, whose _rho_setup does get_overlap_cond plus one condense_to_shell per dm (numint.py:3689-3693). numint.py:1945 calls mol.get_overlap_cond() again for pair_mask. Both run before the fused path is chosen at 1948-1950, and that path uses neither result. _FusedXC.rho_evaluator then calls _rho_setup a third time (numint.py:1116-1117).
nr_uks does the same at 2044-2045, 2074 and 1320 (dma and dmb).
Per call that is 3 get_overlap_cond + 2 condense for RKS and 5 + 4 for UKS, exactly the profile counts: 54/36 calls in 18 PBE cycles, 125/100 in 25 UKS cycles.
For plain dms (fxc/TDA), rho1_rho2_ratio is 0, so the per-dm condense calls (320 in tda_caffeine) feed nothing on the fused path.
Per call at 10 threads: get_overlap_cond 4.4-5.1 ms and condense 4.8-6.6 ms, vs 0.138 and 0.048 ms at 1 thread (probe1). The inflation comes from xc-blas-spin.
findings.current_cost:
get_overlap_cond + condense per run:
- scf_caffeine_svp_pbe 0.514 s (5.0% of 10.22 s); b3lyp 0.479 s (4.8%); r2scan 0.506 s (4.3%).
- dfpbe 0.545 s (3.6%).
- caffeine+ UKS 1.019 s (4.8%); benzene+ UKS r2SCAN 0.301 s (7.4%).
- c20h42 b3lyp 0.276 s; r2scan 0.364 s.
- tda_caffeine 0.25 s; tddft_benzene 0.13 s.
findings.proposal:
In nr_rks and nr_uks, call _fused_xc first, and build make_rho and pair_mask only on the fallback path.
Cache mol.get_overlap_cond() per molecule, e.g. on _GridAOData, which already checks mol content on every call, or keyed on _atm/_bas/_env.
In _rho_setup, skip condense_to_shell when no mo_coeff is attached, since the ratio is then unused; keep pair_mask for non-fused callers.
Once xc-rho-mo-gga-z's flop-based path choice exists, the ratio and the remaining condense can go too.
findings.expected_gain: At today's per-call cost: -0.35 to -0.45 s per RKS caffeine SCF (3.5-4.5%), -0.8 to -0.9 s for UKS (4%), -0.25 s for benzene+ UKS (6%), -0.2 s for caffeine TDA. If xc-blas-spin lands first, these calls cost ~0.05-0.2 ms each and the saving falls to 10-30 ms per SCF.
findings.exactness_notes: Only removes work whose results are discarded on the fused path.

findings.title: The xc_deriv transforms after libxc are single-threaded (xc_deriv.c has no OpenMP; numpy fancy-index gathers and adds) and dominate eval_xc_eff at deriv 2-3 on 10 threads
findings.evidence:
xc_deriv.c contains no OpenMP pragma (grep count 0) in any of its kernels: VXCunfold_sigma_spin0 (106-136), VXCunfold_sigma_spin1 (138+), VXCud2ts/VXCts2ud (69, 86) and VXCfg_to_direct_deriv (28). In xc_deriv.py, _unfold_gga (489-516) also materializes xc_val[idx.ravel()], and transform_xc (539+) adds the sigma terms with numpy fancy-index +=. All of this runs on one thread while LIBXC_eval_xc is OpenMP.
probe3 (1 thread, 200k points), share of the transforms in eval_xc_eff: 2-3% at deriv 1, 7-18% at deriv 2, 29-50% at deriv 3. Examples: spin=1 PBE d3 is 1683 ns/pt in libxc and 1707 ns/pt in the transforms; spin=0 B3LYP d3 is 304 vs 198.
At 10 threads libxc scales and the transforms do not: micro_libxc (summary.txt) spends 0.761 s in xc_post (_unfold_gga 0.581 s, transform_xc 0.178 s) vs 0.931 s in libxc, of 1.74 s wall.
findings.current_cost: micro_libxc: 0.76 s of 1.74 s (44%). Direct eval_xc_eff at 10 threads (estimated): the transforms are ~40-45% of a deriv-2 call and 75-87% of a deriv-3 call. SCF at deriv 1: 0.03 s RKS, 0.12 s UKS (caffeine+ _unfold_gga 0.117 s / 125 calls).
findings.proposal:
Add `#pragma omp parallel for` over grid points, collapsed with ncounts, in VXCunfold_sigma_spin0/1, VXCud2ts/ts2ud and VXCfg_to_direct_deriv. These are elementwise, so results stay bitwise identical.
Pass the unique-index list to the first unfold pass instead of materializing xc_val[idx].
Replace transform_xc's per-diagonal numpy `xc_tensor_1[diag_idx] += xc_sub` loops with one C/OpenMP kernel that adds the sigma terms per point in the same order.
findings.expected_gain: micro_libxc: -0.5 to -0.6 s (30-35%). Direct calls at 10 threads: ~1.5-2x faster at deriv 2 and 2-4x at deriv 3 (the deriv-3 UKS GGA tensor is 512 doubles/point, so the parallel version becomes memory-bound). SCF: <= 0.1 s.
findings.exactness_notes: Elementwise operations with the per-element accumulation order unchanged.

findings.title: AO evaluation uses scalar glibc exp for every primitive and point, with -msse3 -O2 code; a SIMD exp and per-file AVX2 flags would roughly halve eval_ao
findings.evidence:
GTOcontract_exp0/1 (lib/gto/deriv1.c:31-55 and 225+) and GTOprim_exp (grid_ao_drv.c:158) call scalar exp() for every primitive and grid point, with no cutoff. They are compiled with -msse3 -O2 (lib/CMakeLists.txt:54-57).
With non0tab=None, as in the direct eval_ao API, every shell is evaluated at every point: ~218 primitive exponentials per point for caffeine/SVP.
grid_caffeine_svp native profile (1 thread, 13.19 s):
- eval_ao 34.1% (4.5 s).
- Exponential code (GTOcontract_exp1 9.9%, GTOcontract_exp0 4.1%, GTOprim_exp 4.7% inclusive, including exp 14.6% plus unresolved libm frames): ~2.5 s, ~55% of eval_ao.
- Polynomial and c2s: ~2.0 s (GTOshell_eval_grid_cart_deriv2 8.0%, deriv1 3.3%, d_ket_cart2spheric 2.4%).
probe2: eval_ao takes 0.093 / 0.136 / 0.242 s per 50k points (deriv 0/1/2) at 1 thread.
The fused SCF kernels avoid exp only through the deriv <= 1 radial cache. The deriv 2/3 kernels (gradient dot_terms 0.50 s on caffeine, 1.23 s on the alkane; Hessian terms) compute it.
NOTES It3: -march=native for all of PySCF made the XC passes 20-35% faster but J/K 4-6% slower, so the flags must be per file.
findings.current_cost: grid_caffeine_svp: eval_gto 1.70 s of 3.64 s at 10 threads. grad_caffeine: dot_terms 0.50 s; grad_c20h42: 1.23 s. In SCF at 1 thread, AO polynomial plus libdft loops are ~7.7 s of nr_rks's 29.4 s.
findings.proposal:
Compile lib/gto/grid_ao_drv.c, deriv1.c, deriv2.c and libdft's nr_numint_fused.c/nr_numint.c with -O3 -mavx2 -mfma -ffp-contract=off, or use target_clones for AVX2 and AVX-512. Leave libcvhf and the integral drivers at stock flags.
Vectorize the exp loops with a <= 1-4 ulp SIMD exp: glibc libmvec (_ZGVdN4v_exp / _ZGVeN8v_exp via `#pragma omp declare simd` + -fopenmp-simd + -lmvec) or SLEEF.
With -ffp-contract=off, everything except exp stays bitwise identical.
findings.expected_gain:
eval_ao 1.8-2.2x faster at 1 thread (exp 4-6x cheaper, polynomial ~1.3x).
- grid_caffeine_svp: -0.4 to -0.8 s of 3.64 s (11-22%) at today's cost; -0.3 to -0.5 s if xc-blas-spin lands.
- Gradients: -0.1 to -0.3 s (1-2%).
- SCF: -2-3% from the polynomial and libdft loops.
findings.exactness_notes: The SIMD exp differs from glibc's scalar exp by up to 1-4 ulp for some arguments, so AO values change at ~1e-16 relative. Vectorized elementwise code with -ffp-contract=off is otherwise bitwise identical.

findings.title: Dense eval_rho writes an N x nao temporary per GEMM and re-reads it from DRAM for every component; fusing the GEMM and contractions per point block roughly halves the traffic
findings.evidence:
On the dense path, eval_rho (numint.py:179-247) computes c0 = _dot_ao_dm(...) via lib.dot (numint.py:781), writing an F-ordered N x nao array. _contract_rho (848-871, VXC_dcontract_rho) then re-reads ao_c and c0 from DRAM for each of the 4 GGA components. Meta-GGA needs 4 GEMMs and 7 contractions.
grid_caffeine_svp: _contract_rho takes 0.405 s for 96 calls, i.e. 4.2 ms per 2 x 98 MB, ~47 GB/s, which is DRAM-bound. _dgemm takes 1.316 s for 42 calls.
probe2 (1 thread, 50k points): GEMM 0.110 s (55 GFLOP/s); each contraction 6 ms.
findings.current_cost: grid_caffeine_svp: 0.405 s of contractions, plus the c0 write/read traffic inside the 1.316 s of GEMMs (together 47% of 3.64 s).
findings.proposal:
Add a C kernel for dense eval_rho with hermi=1 (and eval_rho2) that processes point blocks of ~256-1024 in parallel. Each thread runs a single-threaded dgemm of its block into a cache-resident buffer, then does every contraction while ao_c of the block is still hot, writing rho directly.
This removes the N x nao temporaries (98 MB per GEMM here) and cuts a GGA chunk's DRAM traffic from ~1.0 GB to ~0.4 GB.
findings.expected_gain: grid_caffeine_svp: -0.3 to -0.45 s (8-12%). Most of the 0.405 s of contractions goes, plus the c0 write. User scripts also allocate less.
findings.exactness_notes: A point-blocked GEMM normally keeps each element's k-summation order, so results are likely bitwise identical, but OpenBLAS may pick different kernels for different M.

findings.title: The XC-matrix kernels use a static round-robin group schedule on 4 Zen 5 + 6 Zen 5c cores; a chunked, order-fixed dynamic schedule keeps reproducibility and recovers the imbalance
findings.evidence:
VXCfused_dot_wv (nr_numint_fused.c:562) and VXCfused_dot_terms (824) use schedule(static,1), so that each thread sums a fixed set of groups and results are reproducible. The rho kernels use dynamic scheduling.
In the profile run, Zen 5 cores averaged 4.4 GHz and Zen 5c cores 3.3 GHz, so the static schedule waits for the Zen 5c threads.
NOTES It6 measured the XC-matrix kernel at 18.5-18.8 ms with static round-robin vs 17.3-17.6 ms with dynamic (-6.5%).
findings.current_cost: dot (VXCfused_dot_wv) at 10 threads: caffeine/SVP 2.66 s (B3LYP) to 4.78 s (r2SCAN); DF-TZVP 6.92 s; caffeine+ UKS 5.30 s; c20h42 r2SCAN 8.45 s; tda_caffeine 9.35 s; tda_c20h42 14.05 s.
findings.proposal:
Cut the groups into a fixed number of contiguous chunks that does not depend on the thread count (e.g. 64). Threads take chunks dynamically and accumulate each chunk into a compact buffer over the union of its shells, or into a per-chunk matrix when nset·nao^2·nchunk fits a memory budget. Chunk results are added into vmat in chunk order (ticketed).
The result is deterministic and also thread-count independent. Fall back to static when the buffers do not fit.
findings.expected_gain: ~6% of dot time: caffeine/SVP -0.15 to -0.3 s; DF-TZVP -0.4 s; caffeine+ UKS -0.3 s; caffeine TDA -0.55 s; alkane TDA -0.8 s.
findings.exactness_notes: The summation order changes but stays fixed, so results are deterministic and no longer depend on the thread count.

findings.title: Each SCF block evaluates every group's AO values twice (density kernel, then Vxc kernel) with libxc in Python in between; a one-pass group kernel with libxc called from C saves one AO pass per cycle
findings.evidence:
For each block, _FusedXC.nr_rks (numint.py:1295-1315) calls VXCfused_eval_rho_mo, then ni.eval_xc_eff in Python, then VXCfused_dot_wv. Both kernels rebuild every group's AO values with _eval_group from the radial cache.
In the 1-thread native SCF profile, _eval_group is 12.6% inclusive (5.9 s), half of it in the second pass.
Between the two kernels, the block's rho and wv go through numpy (the numpy category is 0.25-0.31 s per SCF) and through LIBXC_eval_xc's static equal split of points (libxc_itrf.c:977-1000) over heterogeneous cores.
findings.current_cost: One AO-evaluation pass per cycle is ~3 s per SCF at 1 thread, ~0.4-0.5 s per caffeine/SVP SCF at 10 threads, and ~0.6-0.8 s for DF-TZVP. Per-block numpy and the libxc imbalance come on top.
findings.expected_gain: -0.4 to -0.6 s per caffeine/SVP SCF (4-6%); -0.6 to -0.9 s for DF-TZVP. It also removes the per-block numpy.dot behind xc-blas-spin and libxc's static split.
findings.exactness_notes: libxc is pointwise, so exc and vxc are bitwise unchanged; only the nelec/excsum summation order changes. Vxc is unchanged if the dot order is kept.

ruled_out:
Checked and not proposed (or folded into a finding):
- LIBXC_eval_xc interface (libxc_itrf.c:968-1024): static equal point split, nfn+3 parallel regions per call, serial exc merge (886-893), one parallel region per term in the UKS axpy (869-878). Once xc-blas-spin is fixed, libxc should be ~0.18-0.37 s per caffeine SCF (micro rates 36-79 ns/pt). Fixing the Zen 5c imbalance would then save only ~20-30% of that (0.05-0.1 s); folded into xc-onepass-scf.
- libxc cost depending on the density: real minao densities and random densities cost the same per point at 1 thread (B3LYP 171 vs 182, PBE 200 vs 213, r2SCAN 460 vs 462 ns/pt; probe1). The SCF slowdown is therefore not a density effect.
- Exact-zero screening for direct eval_rho without non0tab: on caffeine 50k-point chunks only 9.2% of (block, shell) pairs are exactly zero (AO-weighted 81% nonzero; probe2). Gathered GEMMs could skip at most ~34% of flops, and a mask pass plus less efficient gathered GEMMs would eat most of that. The cutoff screen index (54% nonzero) changes AO values and is therefore an approximation.
- eval_ao page faults from fresh arrays in user scripts: deriv-1 chunk 0.136 s fresh vs 0.120 s with a reused buffer at 1 thread (12%). The allocation is on the user side and cannot be removed without aliasing the returned arrays.
- Grid construction: Becke partition (gen_grid_partition) takes 0.10-0.12 s per caffeine SCF and 0.37 s for the alkane (grids category 0.42 s of 18.8 s), once per geometry. The original Becke scheme has no exactly-0/1 factors, so pair screening would be approximate, and an AVX2 build would gain <= 0.2 s.
- The argsort per cycle (0.17-0.41 s in the SCF profiles) is scf/_vhf.py:350, which is J/K, not XC.
- Dense path for small molecules: benzene/SVP and larger take the fused kernels (_FusedXC.dot/_rho_kernel in the benzene profiles); only water-sized systems stay dense.
- cache_xc_kernel: once per TD/Hessian run (tda_caffeine: _eval_xc 0.067 s, transform 0.007 s).
- xc_deriv transforms at deriv 1 in SCF: 2-3% of eval_xc_eff (0.03 s RKS, 0.12 s UKS); covered by xc-deriv-omp.
- Per-call checks in _fused_xc/_grid_ao_data: array_equal 0.025 s and count_nonzero 0.009 s per SCF.
- Flop count of the GGA Vxc GEMM: already minimal (one GEMM plus hermi_sum). The meta-GGA tau term already uses dsyrk. The meta-GGA MO-path density needs all 4 GEMMs, because tau needs every ao_c·C.
- xc-rho-mo-gga-z on the SVP alkane: ns ~159 ~ 2·nocc (81), so the dm path (already chosen) costs the same as MO+Z; no gain there.
- Group size (GEMM_NBLK): NOTES It6 found no difference for 2/4/8 blocks.
- -march=native for all of PySCF: NOTES It3 found J/K 4-6% slower, hence the per-file proposal in xc-ao-simd-exp.
- Not measured here because the rules forbid multithreaded runs: the 10-thread magnitude of xc-blas-spin. The run_bench A/B command for it is given in that finding.
Probe scripts are under /tmp/claude-1000/-home-danny-Chemistry-my-pyscf/3d2aa02f-ca12-40eb-b5fd-b099754f302d/scratchpad/swarm/xc/: probe1.py (libxc per point, setup overheads), probe2.py (grid pipeline, group sizes and flops), probe3.py (libxc vs transforms), probe4.py (VV10).

verdicts.checked: Source: OpenBLAS blas_server.c:160-164 (THREAD_TIMEOUT 28 gives 1<<28 TSC ticks, about 134 ms at 2 GHz) and 405-430 (nop spin loop); common.h:393-397 (YIELDING is 8 nops on x86_64); kernel/x86_64/ddot.c (threads when n > 10000); blas_server.c:572-576 (env clamped to 4..30). `strings` on both bundled libs (numpy libscipy_openblas64_ 0.3.34.106, scipy libscipy_openblas 0.3.31.dev, both pthreads) shows OPENBLAS_THREAD_TIMEOUT and OMP_NUM_THREADS. Triggers are real: numint.py:1312 and 1339-1340 (excsum += numpy.dot(den, exc) per fused block, about 59k points, 5 blocks per cycle), hf.py:867 (make_rdm1 ndarray.dot, a threaded dgemm), diis.py:228/326 (numpy.dot), and the grid case's np.dot per 50k chunk. bench/common.py worker_env drops OPENBLAS_*, but cfg.env is applied afterwards, so the proposed A/B config works. Profile numbers match summary.txt: get_overlap_cond 0.261 s/51 calls = 5.1 ms (B3LYP), condense 6.4 ms, libxc 0.672 s/(17 x 294,800 points) = 134 ns/pt against micro_libxc's B3LYP_d1 36 ns/pt (JSON values), and 1-thread nr_rks 62.7% of 46.87 s = 29.4 s. Two caveats. (1) File timestamps show the 1-thread native scf_caffeine profile (finished 18:09:59) overlapped the start of the 10-thread run (18:09:28), so the PBE case was contaminated; B3LYP and UKS show the same per-call inflation, so the anomaly is robust. (2) NOTES' AO-cache test shows dense eval_ao at 10 threads is bound by writing its block, and the grid case also page-faults 11 GB of fresh AO arrays, so eval_gto's 2.1x scaling is not mainly spin.
verdicts.gain_estimate: Mechanism is confirmed; the magnitude is overstated. The '~7x expected' scaling ignores static schedules on Zen 5c cores (ceiling about 10 x 3.3/5.0 = 6.6x), memory-bound parts, and libxc reaching only 4.75x even in micro. Realistic: caffeine/SVP RKS SCFs -0.5 to -1.5 s each (5-15%); caffeine+ UKS -1 to -3 s; benzene+ UKS r2SCAN -0.3 to -1.0 s; grid_caffeine_svp -0.2 to -0.6 s (eval_gto is mostly memory and page-fault bound). Part (a), the timeout of about 18-20 in pyscf-env.sh, is the real fix. Part (b) alone gains little, because make_rdm1, DIIS and eigh re-arm both pools immediately before every nr_rks. The magnitude must come from the proposed run_bench A/B; also consider an OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS=1 arm, though it would slow scipy eigh at nao ~500 (eigh is 0.82 s in DF-TZVP).
verdicts.cost_seconds: Not separable from the profiles. Visible excess on caffeine/SVP B3LYP: libxc ~0.49 s, get_overlap_cond plus condense 0.48 s; per-region stalls of the OMP kernels are unquantified. UKS: libxc 1.52 s and setup 1.02 s.
verdicts.comment: Part (a) is bitwise (scheduling only). Part (b) changes excsum by rounding (~1e-16 relative), not bitwise as the exactness label says. The finding is worth an A/B run first, since it changes how every other XC estimate should be read. NOTES It3 already saw a related symptom: scipy eigh went from 0.4 to 3.0 s with 20 threads, from pool contention.

verdicts.checked: nr_numint_fused.c VXCfused_eval_rho_mo (about lines 386-500): one dgemm for v0, then for nderiv==1 three more dgemms (aobuf+c*ns*ng)·C into v1, each followed by _contract_mo. The Z = C·v0^T identity is correct: sum_o v0[k,o]·v1_c[k,o] = sum_n ao_c[n,k]·Z[n,k]. The proposed dgemm('N','N', ng, ns, nc, v0, ng, cbuf, nc) produces Z in the [ns][ng] layout of aobuf. It13 B uses the same trick in rho_lowrank (NOTES), and it was never applied to the SCF MO path. _rho1_preferred (numint.py:1016-1024) uses thresholds of 4 (GGA) and 1 (otherwise). The 1-thread native SCF profile confirms the MO path is taken: VXCfused_eval_rho_mo 29.4% inclusive = 13.8 s. Recomputed the BLAS split: sgemm_* self time 36.8% = 17.2 s, split by flops 18.6:14.9 gives about 9.6 s for rho and 7.7 s for dot_wv. That is consistent with dot_wv's 13.45 s inclusive (7.7 s BLAS + 2.06 s omp body + 0.66 s scatter + about 2.95 s _eval_group). Flop arithmetic 8·224·154·51·1317 = 18.5 GFLOP/cycle checks out. eval_rho2's GGA branch (numint.py:406-413) has the 4-GEMM pattern.
verdicts.gain_estimate: At 1 thread: -4.75 s of GEMM, plus about 1 s of extra contractions (3 reads of ns·ng instead of nc·ng; aobuf plus Z ≈ 1.4 MB per group exceeds the 1 MB L2), net about -3.7 s of 13.8 s (27% of _rho_kernel). At 10 threads: caffeine/SVP B3LYP -0.6 to -0.7 s, PBE -0.6 to -0.75 s, CAM-B3LYP -0.45 s (5-7%); DF-TZVP -0.8 to -1.4 s (5-9%); caffeine+ UKS -1.0 to -1.2 s (5%). No gain for meta-GGA or LDA.
verdicts.cost_seconds: _rho_kernel at 10 threads: PBE 2.83 s, B3LYP 2.50 s, CAM-B3LYP 1.81 s, DF-TZVP 3.97 s, caffeine+ UKS 4.58 s (summary.txt; matches).
verdicts.comment: Do the flop-based path choice too: with Z the MO path costs 4·ng·ns·nocc against the dm path's 2·ng·ns², which also helps any case that now takes the dm path with ns > 2·nocc. The density changes only by rounding. test_fused_xc's bit-for-bit block_loop comparison needs both paths changed together or a 1e-13 tolerance.

verdicts.checked: nr_numint.c VXC_vv10nlc: an O(N_out x N_in) pair loop with three divisions per pair (RpW/(g·gp·gt), 1./g, 1./gt), scalar reductions, schedule(static), and the stock -msse3 -O2 flags. The kernel is unchanged from pyscf-base apart from new code elsewhere in the file. rks.py:356-358: nlcgrids.level defaults to the Grids default (3). In _vv10nlc the inner and outer sets use the same rho, the same 1e-8 threshold and the same expressions (R**2 squares exactly like Rp*Rp), so W0 = W0p and K = Kp bitwise and the symmetric kernel holds. I re-ran the analyst's probe4 single-threaded: 294,800 NLC points, 275,681 above threshold, 1.77 ns/pair, 134 s per full call at 1 thread (7.6e10 pairs). NOTES lists NLC as still on the old path, with nothing tried.
verdicts.gain_estimate: Per call: ~134 s at 1 thread, ~18-20 s at 10 threads (the static schedule is bound by the Zen 5c cores). One division plus 4-wide SIMD gives ~2-3x; the symmetric pair loop gives ~1.6-1.9x after the extra scatter and multiplies; together 3-5x. That is -11 to -16 s per SCF cycle on caffeine/SVP with wB97M-V, ~150-250 s per SCF, and the saving grows as N². Using a dynamic or chunked schedule for the outer loop adds ~10%.
verdicts.cost_seconds: ~18-20 s per SCF cycle at 10 threads for caffeine/SVP with any VV10 functional (~250-300 s per SCF). Not in the bench set.
verdicts.comment: This is the largest saving in this set, but only for VV10 users, and the bench has no VV10 case. Add one (e.g. scf_caffeine_svp_wb97mv) before implementing. Changing the order of the 7.6e10-term sums moves the NLC energy by ~1e-14 relative, far inside the 1e-9 Eh gate. The gradient and Hessian VV10 kernels have the same structure.

verdicts.checked: In nr_rks: _gen_rho_evaluator → _rho_setup (numint.py:3689-3692: get_overlap_cond plus one condense_to_shell per dm), then pair_mask = mol.get_overlap_cond() at 1945, both before _fused_xc at 1948. _FusedXC.rho_evaluator calls _rho_setup again (1116-1117) and uses only mo_coeff, mo_occ and rho1_rho2_ratio; it ignores pair_mask. nr_uks does the same twice (2044-2045) plus 2074, plus [dma, dmb] in rho_evaluator. Counts match exactly: PBE 54/36 over 18 cycles, B3LYP 51/34 over 17, UKS 125/100 over 25. Both GTOoverlap_cond (fill_int2c.c:177, omp static) and NPcondense are OpenMP regions, so their 5 ms per-call cost (against 0.14 and 0.05 ms at 1 thread) is per-region stalling from xc-blas-spin. Removing regions removes their per-region penalties; the stall does not shift elsewhere. In TDA the calls cost only 0.7 ms each (condense 320 calls 0.226 s, get_overlap_cond 30 calls 0.026 s).
verdicts.gain_estimate: Today: -0.3 to -0.45 s per caffeine/SVP RKS SCF (3-4.5%), -0.8 to -0.9 s for caffeine+ UKS (4%), -0.2 to -0.25 s for benzene+ UKS r2SCAN (5-6%), -0.25 s for tda_caffeine (1%). After xc-blas-spin lands, only tens of ms.
verdicts.cost_seconds: get_overlap_cond plus condense: PBE 0.514 s, B3LYP 0.479, r2SCAN 0.506, DF-TZVP 0.545, caffeine+ UKS 1.019, benzene+ UKS 0.301, tda_caffeine 0.25 (summary.txt; matches).
verdicts.comment: Trivial, bitwise change; do it regardless of the spin fix. Keep _rho_setup's pair_mask for non-fused callers and compute condense only where the MO/dm ratio is needed (MO-tagged dms).

verdicts.checked: xc_deriv.c has no OpenMP: the only 'omp' match is in the license header. VXCunfold_sigma_spin0/1, VXCud2ts/ts2ud and VXCfg_to_direct_deriv are serial elementwise loops. xc_deriv.py _unfold_gga materializes xc_val[idx.ravel()] with numpy fancy indexing into a fresh array. transform_xc adds sigma terms by numpy fancy-index +=, also single-threaded. micro_libxc in summary.txt: _unfold_gga 0.581 s, transform_xc 0.178 s, libxc 0.931 s, wall 1.74 s. The JSON values show deriv 3 dominating (PBE_d3 0.223 s, B3LYP_d3 0.216 s, SCAN_d3 0.449 s). In the SCF _unfold_gga is 0.03 s (RKS) and 0.117 s (caffeine+ UKS); cache_xc_kernel in TDA costs 0.007 s of transforms.
verdicts.gain_estimate: micro_libxc -0.45 to -0.55 s (25-32%). The kernels and copies are memory-bound, so 10 threads give ~3-5x, not 10x. Direct eval_xc_eff calls at deriv 2 and 3 run ~1.5-3x faster. SCF and TD gain less than 0.1 s (<1%).
verdicts.cost_seconds: micro_libxc 0.76 s of 1.74 s; SCF 0.03-0.12 s.
verdicts.comment: Its only value is for direct-API and functional-development scripts, which per the user's profile are a real use. Bitwise as long as each element's accumulation order in transform_xc is kept. Also parallelize the first touch of the fresh xc_tensor and buf arrays.

verdicts.checked: deriv1.c GTOcontract_exp0 (31-55) and grid_ao_drv.c GTOprim_exp (158+) call scalar exp() per primitive and point with no cutoff. CMakeLists.txt adds only -msse3 to the stock flags. Native grid profile (13.19 s): eval_ao 34.1% = 4.5 s; exp inclusive 14.6% = 1.93 s plus contract_exp and prim_exp self time, about 2.4 s (~55%) of exponential code at 1 thread. However, NOTES' AO-cache test and Next-iterations item 5 found that dense eval_ao at 10 threads is bound by writing its block: GGA zero-writes come within 1-3% of a full evaluation. The grid case writes about 11 GB of fresh AO arrays (LDA 0.6, PBE 2.4, SCAN 2.4, PBE d2 5.9 GB) and page-faults all of it, a memory floor of roughly 0.6-0.9 s of the 1.70 s eval_gto. So halving compute does not halve eval_gto at 10 threads. In the SCF the fused kernels use the radial cache (no exp) for deriv ≤ 1. Polynomial and libdft loops are ~16% of the 1-thread SCF; It3's 20-35% XC gain from -march=native was measured on the pre-It6 kernels, which were dominated by dot loops. NOTES It3 rejected only the whole-tree -march=native; per-file flags were never tested.
verdicts.gain_estimate: grid_caffeine_svp -0.15 to -0.4 s (4-11%), not -0.4 to -0.8 s. Gradients: -0.05 to -0.15 s on caffeine (<2%; dot_terms 0.50 s); alkane gradient <1%. SCF -1 to -3% from per-file AVX2/FMA flags on libdft and the GTO polynomial code; measure, since the GEMMs, which dominate the XC time, are OpenBLAS and unaffected.
verdicts.cost_seconds: grid_caffeine_svp eval_gto 1.70 s at 10 threads (largely memory and page-fault bound); exp code ~2.4 s at 1 thread. grad dot_terms 0.50 s (caffeine), 1.23 s (alkane).
verdicts.comment: A SIMD exp (libmvec ≤ 4 ulp) changes AO values only by rounding, so it is allowed under the policy. Note that glibc declares the vector exp variants only under __FAST_MATH__, so call _ZGVdN4v_exp directly or use SLEEF. Use -ffp-contract=off to keep the rest bitwise. Split into two experiments: per-file -O3 -mavx2 -mfma for libdft and libcgto (cheap; worth measuring on SCF), and SIMD exp (helps the 1-thread and gradient deriv-2/3 paths more than the 10-thread grid case).

verdicts.checked: numint.py eval_rho (179-247). The perf tree already symmetrizes the dm for GGA and meta-GGA, so it is hermi=1 with one GEMM for GGA and four GEMMs plus seven contractions for meta-GGA. Each _dot_ao_dm writes a fresh 50000 x 246 array (98 MB), which _contract_rho reads back. Call counts match the grid case: 6 + 24 + 42 + 24 = 96 contractions and 6 + 6 + 24 + 6 = 42 GEMMs. summary.txt: _contract_rho 0.405 s for 96 calls = 4.2 ms per 196 MB ≈ 47 GB/s, DRAM-bound. _dgemm 1.316 s for 42 calls = 31 ms against about 24 ms at micro_gemm's 257 GFLOP/s for the 67200 x 246 x 246 shape (JSON). The 7 ms gap per call is partly the c0 write and its page faults. A GGA chunk moves about 1.08 GB now against about 0.4 GB fused; meta-GGA about 2.2 GB against about 0.4 GB.
verdicts.gain_estimate: grid_caffeine_svp -0.25 to -0.4 s (7-11%): most of the 0.405 s of contractions (they then read only hot ao_c), plus the c0/c1 writes and faults (about 4 GB, about 0.1-0.2 s). Little gain elsewhere: only water-sized SCFs stay on the dense path.
verdicts.cost_seconds: grid_caffeine_svp: 0.405 s of contractions plus about 0.15-0.3 s of temporary write and fault traffic inside the 1.316 s of GEMMs.
verdicts.comment: Per-block single-threaded dgemm inside an omp region (as the fused kernels do) can pick OpenBLAS' small-matrix kernels for small M, so results change by rounding and are not guaranteed bitwise. That is fine under the policy, but say so. It benefits only direct-API users (grid_caffeine), which matches the user's profile.

verdicts.checked: VXCfused_dot_wv uses a static round-robin schedule ('static: each thread sums a fixed set of groups'); the rho kernels use schedule(dynamic,4). NOTES It6 measured static contiguous 19.4-20.3 ms, round-robin 18.5-18.8 ms and dynamic 17.3-17.6 ms on one alkane block, and kept round-robin for reproducibility. Plain dynamic was therefore rejected for that reason; the chunk-ordered deterministic design is new. The ideal heterogeneous-core gain for compute-bound work is 33/37.4 ≈ 12%; It6 measured 6.5%. Costs match summary.txt: dot B3LYP 2.66 s, r2SCAN 4.78 s, DF-TZVP 6.92 s, UKS 5.30 s, alkane r2SCAN 8.45 s, tda_caffeine 9.35 s, tda_c20h42 14.05 s. NOTES' Next iterations already flag the nthreads·nset private nao² matrices and their reduction as a cost for many dms (about 6 s of 44 s on the alkane fxc).
verdicts.gain_estimate: ~4-6% of dot time at best, with overhead: caffeine/SVP -0.1 to -0.25 s (1-2.5%), DF-TZVP -0.3 to -0.4 s (2-3%), alkane r2SCAN -0.3 to -0.45 s (~2%). For TDA, fixed 64-chunk buffers would make the reduction worse: 64 chunk matrices against today's 10 private ones, per set, at nset = 5-40. The gain holds there only if the chunk buffers are compact over the chunk's shell union and the chunk count is ~2-3x the thread count; otherwise ≤ 0.
verdicts.cost_seconds: VXCfused_dot_wv (dot) at 10 threads: 2.66-4.78 s on caffeine/SVP SCFs, 6.92 s DF-TZVP, 9.35 s tda_caffeine, 14.05 s tda_c20h42.
verdicts.comment: Borderline at the ~2% threshold. Combine it with the planned fix for the per-block private nao² matrices; group-ordered accumulation as in It12's VXCdot_sets_aow_ao_sparse is a ready model. On its own it is not worth an M-effort iteration.

verdicts.checked: _FusedXC.nr_rks (numint.py:1295-1315): _rho_kernel (VXCfused_eval_rho_mo), then eval_xc_eff in Python, then _dot_wv (VXCfused_dot_wv); both kernels call _eval_group per group. 1-thread native SCF: _eval_group 12.6% inclusive = 5.9 s, about half per pass. NOTES' AO-cache test measured a fused pass with the radial cache at 0.012 s (caffeine/SVP, deriv 1, 10 threads), about 0.2 s per 17-cycle SCF. The 1-thread figure scaled by ~6.5x gives ~0.45 s, so one pass costs 0.2-0.45 s per SCF. Not recorded in NOTES as done or rejected; It10 B noted the double AO evaluation, and It11 mitigated it with the radial cache.
verdicts.gain_estimate: -0.2 to -0.45 s per caffeine/SVP SCF from the saved AO pass (2-4.5%), plus ≤ 0.1-0.2 s from per-block numpy and libxc's static split, which is mostly gone if xc-blas-spin is fixed. Total about 3-5% on caffeine/SVP and about 3-4% on DF-TZVP, for effort L.
verdicts.cost_seconds: One AO-evaluation pass: about 0.2-0.45 s per caffeine/SVP SCF at 10 threads (about 3 s at 1 thread).
verdicts.comment: The gain is real but small for the effort and risk: libxc called per 224-point group from inside OpenMP, the wv recipes reimplemented in C for every xctype, and one shared schedule for the rho and Vxc halves. exc and vxc stay bitwise because libxc is pointwise; nelec and excsum change by rounding. Do xc-rho-mo-gga-z and xc-blas-spin first, then re-profile to see whether this still clears ~3%.

findings.proposal:
1. scf/_response_functions.py, singlet (:159-196) and triplet (:198-222) branches: do what the CPHF branch got in It13 (:135-157).
   - Precompute fxc_st = fxc[0,:,0] +/- fxc[0,:,1] once.

findings.title: One-pass factored fxc kernel for TD/CPHF: ao*C_o computed once (B = Q) or cached across Davidson iterations, all sets of a group in one GEMM, wv in C
findings.evidence:
Duplicated per-pass work in rks_fxc_mo (numint.py:1262-1293):
- With B = Q = C_o (TD and CPHF), rho_lowrank computes tb[c] = ao_c*B (nr_numint_fused.c:951-956) and dot_ao_mo computes the identical fq[c] = ao_c*Q (:1120-1125), for 4 components with GGA/MGGA.
- Each pass also re-evaluates the AO values (_eval_group).
- The Python loop (numint.py:1276-1291) round-trips rho1 and wv through memory and runs one numpy einsum per set.

Per-pass share of the model (c_pass = 8):

| case | GF per pass | GF per set | share of a call |
|---|---|---|---|
| caffeine | 37.14 | 18.57 | 11.1% of a 16-set call |
| benzene | 4.65 | 2.32 | 11.1% |
| alkane | 142.76 | 71.38 | 13.3% at 13 sets |

GEMM shapes (scratch gemm_shapes.py, 1 thread, the linked OpenBLAS 0.3.34), per set -> one GEMM over 16 sets, GF/s:

| system | TA | Z | vQ (two GEMMs) |
|---|---|---|---|
| caffeine | 52.6 -> 61.1 | 55.1 -> 58.7 | 51.1 -> 59.3 |
| benzene | 49.5 -> 59.0 | | 40.0 -> 52.5 |
| alkane | 55.9 -> 61.5 | | 50.3 -> 56.8 |

- On caffeine shapes that is 284 -> 250 us of GEMM per set and group.
- The dm path gains <= 5% from the same batching.
- The per-set einsum costs 0.451 s (caffeine TDA), 0.436 s (benzene TDDFT) and 0.560 s (alkane) at 10 threads.
findings.current_cost:
After td-factored-response the factored XC is about:

| workload | factored XC (s) |
|---|---|
| caffeine TDA | 14 |
| benzene TDDFT | 3.9 |
| benzene TDA | 1.4 |

The alkane stays on the dm path at 25.07 s, because the per-pass cost tips its flop ratio above 1.
findings.proposal:
New kernel VXCfused_fxc_lowrank(vq, A, B, fxcw, nset, xctype, ...) behind rks_fxc_mo's API. Per 224-point group:
1. Evaluate the AO values once.
2. Compute TB_c = ao_c*B_g once and use it for rho1 and for v*Q. Optionally keep TB of all groups across the calls of a TD run (4*ngrids*nocc doubles: benzene 96 MB, caffeine 481 MB, alkane 1.8 GB), under max_memory.
3. TA for all sets in one GEMM (m=ng, n=nset*r, k=ns); Z for all sets in one GEMM (n=nset*ns, k=r).
4. rho1 contractions as now.
5. wv = fxcw*rho1 in C, with fxcw = fxc*weight built once per response function.
6. v*Q for all sets as two GEMMs: ao0^T[ket0_k] and [S_k]^T TB0.
7. Scatter into the private vq matrices.

lowrank_cheaper drops c_pass when TB is cached.
findings.expected_gain:
- **caffeine TDA:** the cache saves 11% of the factored flops, the batching ~12% of the GEMM time, the einsum ~0.4 s and one AO evaluation per group ~1%. Total -2 to -3 s on top of td-factored-response (XC ~14 -> ~11-12 s).
- **benzene TDDFT:** -0.7 to -1.0 s.
- **alkane:** with the cache the GGA flop ratio drops from 1.10-1.18 to 0.98. With batching and the 6x smaller private memory (nao*nq instead of nao^2) the factored path may win 0-15% at 10 threads (It13: a factored flop costs 0.74-0.91x on the alkane): 0 to -3 s, to be measured.
- Overlaps td-fxc-wv-kernel on the factored path.
findings.exactness_notes: Sharing or caching TB is bitwise, since it is the same dgemm on the same inputs. Batched GEMMs and the precomputed fxc*w change rounding only.

findings.title: One grid block per fxc call: stop allocating and reducing nthreads*nset private nao^2 matrices 11 times per alkane call
findings.evidence:
Block sizes:
- _fused_fxc_blksize (numint.py:2231-2242) keeps block_loop's 1200*BLKSIZE cap and its AO-array term, although the fused kernels hold no AO arrays.
- rks_fxc_mo caps at 300 groups (numint.py:1274-1275).
- Blocks per call: alkane 11 (694,296 points; dot 66 calls / rks_fxc 6), caffeine 5 (50/10), benzene 3 (51/17).

Per-block cost:
- Each VXCfused_dot_wv call callocs nset*nao^2 doubles per thread (nr_numint_fused.c:544), reduces them (:679) and adds them to vmat.
- At nset 20, nao 490 and 10 threads that is 384 MB of fresh pages per block.
- NOTES It13 A measured 0.59 s per block for 186 dms at nao 490, i.e. ~3.2 ms per dm and block.

Cross-check: at 10 threads the alkane's dot takes 14.05 s against 11.02 s for _rho_kernel. At 1 thread the two are equal (14.61 vs 14.18 s, measured with tda_factored.py c20 12 PBE). That leaves ~2.7 s of excess that only appears at 10 threads, from these private matrices plus the static schedule.

- **alkane PBE TDA:** ~1.5-2.6 s of 36.79 s (4-7%).
- **caffeine TDA:** ~0.3-0.5 s of 25.25 s.
- **benzene:** <0.1 s.
findings.proposal: Size the fused fxc blocks (_fused_fxc_blksize, rks_fxc_mo) only by the existing rule that rho1 and wv fit in a quarter of max_memory. For 20 GGA sets on all alkane points that is 2*20*4*694k*8 B = 0.89 GB, so usually one block per call. The alternative is to keep the private matrices across blocks.

- **caffeine:** -0.3 to -0.5 s.

findings.title: Hybrid TD with in-memory ERIs: exchange of the trial vectors from (ij|ab) built once, instead of an AO K for every trial vector
findings.evidence:
Current cost:
- tda_caffeine: _incore_s8_batch 5.554 s for 10 calls (160 dms with hermi=0, which take the non-symmetric formulation, w=2, _vhf.py:546-563).
- native: CVHFnrs8_incore_vk_batch 13.2% against vj_batch 4.3%, so K is ~4.2 s and J ~1.4 s at 10 threads.
- TDA needs only C_v^T K[D] C_o = 2 sum_jb (ab|ij) Z_jb.

Measurement (scratch mo_jk.py; benzene, 1 thread, core-Hamiltonian orbitals):
- AO J/K of 16 dms: 0.21 s.
- One-time ao2mo.incore.general: (ij|ab) 0.25 s, (ia|jb) 0.35 s.
- MO contraction of 16 dms: 0.019 s.
- MO vs AO agree to 1.1e-12 relative.

Scaling to caffeine:
- The (ij|ab) transform is 3.4e11 flops (55.7x benzene): ~14 s at 1 thread, ~2 s at 10 threads.
- The contraction is 2*nocc^2*nvir^2 = 2e8 flops per dm, against ~6.6e9 for the AO K.

| workload | K or J/K (s) | wall (s) |

| caffeine TDA | K ~4.2 | 25.25 |
| benzene TDDFT | J/K 0.56 | 8.52 |

findings.proposal:
Where mf._eri is in memory and the functional is a global hybrid:
1. The singlet/triplet response builds (ij|ab) once, s4 = 203 MB for caffeine.
2. Exchange: K_ia = 2 sum_jb (ij|ab) Z_jb as a GEMM, added in the MO basis (vind_lowrank of td-factored-response).

findings.title: Compute wv = fxc*rho1*w for all trial vectors in one parallel pass, instead of a numpy einsum per set and block
findings.evidence:
Code:
- numint.py:1362 (rks_fxc) and :1286 (rks_fxc_mo) call numpy.einsum('yg,xyg,g->xg') per set and block.
- It runs single-threaded and re-reads the fxc slice (16*ng doubles = 8.6 MB per 67,200-point block) for every set.
- uks_fxc does two einsums per set (numint.py:1381-1385).

Profiles, c_einsum:

| workload | time (s) | calls | fxc einsums |
|---|---|---|---|
| caffeine TDA | 0.451 | 811 | 800 = 160 dms x 5 blocks |
| benzene TDDFT | 0.436 | 960 | ~840 = 280 x 3 |
| benzene TDA | 0.154 | 320 | |
| alkane | 0.560 | 887 | 880 = 80 x 11 |

That is ~0.56 ms per call, about 2 GFLOP/s.
findings.current_cost:
| workload | time (s) | share of wall |
|---|---|---|
| caffeine TDA | 0.45 | 1.8% |
| benzene TDDFT | 0.38-0.44 | 5% |
| benzene TDA | 0.15 | 5% |
| alkane TDA | 0.56 | 1.5% |
findings.proposal:
A small OpenMP C kernel that reads fxc[:,:,g] once per point and applies it to all sets: wv[k,x,g] = sum_y fxc[x,y,g]*rho1[k,y,g]*w[g].
- Bitwise variant: keep einsum's product order and y order.
- Rounding-only variant: precompute fxc*w once per response function.
- Use it in rks_fxc, rks_fxc_mo and uks_fxc. It is subsumed by td-lowrank-single-pass on the factored path, but still needed on the dm path.
findings.expected_gain:
5-10x less time, from reading fxc once per block instead of nset times and from 10 threads:
- **caffeine:** -0.4 s.
- **benzene TDDFT:** -0.35 s (4%).
- **benzene TDA:** -0.13 s (4%).
- **alkane:** -0.5 s.
