ruled_out:
**Davidson/eigensolver work: <= 2% everywhere.**

| case | items | total | share |
|---|---|---|---|
| caffeine TDA | _qr 0.090 s + scipy/lr eigh 0.036 + ndarray.dot 0.099 + vstack 0.044 + norm 0.009 | ~0.28 s of 25.25 | 1.1% |
| benzene TDDFT | real_eig incl. inv 0.047, _lu 0.021, eigh 0.037 | ~0.15 s of 8.52 | 1.8% |
| alkane | _qr 0.108 + eigh 0.018 | 0.14 s of 36.79 | 0.4% |
| native caffeine | eigh 81.4% vs vind 81.3% inclusive | | |

**J/K shares.**
- caffeine TDA: 5.56 s (22%; in-memory, 160 hermi=0 dms; K ~3/4).
- benzene TDA: 0.22 s (7%).
- benzene TDDFT: 0.56 s (6.6%).
- alkane PBE TDA: 10.09 s (27%; semi-direct J only, 80 dms in 6 calls).
- The kernels themselves are the J/K area's. TD-specific checks:
  - J already uses the symmetrized dm (pack_tril(dm+dm^T), dm_sum).
  - TDA's K needs both the symmetric and antisymmetric parts (A-type exchange (ab|ij)Z), so there is no hermi trick.
  - Low-rank K via M*C_o costs 2i^2*nocc per ERI row against 2i^2*2*n_dm now, which is worse for n_dm < nocc/2.
  - An MO-basis (ia|jb) for J breaks even at ~280 dms on caffeine, against 160 used.
  - For the direct alkane the AO->MO transform is ~9e12 flops.

**Algorithm changes (approximation class, not proposed).**
- _lr_eig adds up to MAX_SPACE_INC=20 vectors per iteration, mostly residuals of non-target Ritz vectors: caffeine 160 dms in 10 iterations for 5 roots; benzene TDDFT 280 in 17; alkane 80 in 6.
- Adding only target-root vectors could cut the dms per iteration up to 4x. But it changes the Krylov space, the iteration count, and the energies at the conv_tol level (~1e-9 Eh).
- Coarser second_grids, small_rho_cutoff and frozen core are user choices. Frozen core would favour the factored path: alkane nocc 81 -> 61 gives a GGA ratio of ~0.74.

**Other formulations.**
- Orbitals on the grid (ao*C_v, ao*C_o) instead of AO factors: costs 2*ng*nvir*nocc per set, and nvir >= ns (195 vs 163, 409 vs 165, 93 vs 99).
- The full MO XC kernel matrix: ~5.8e13 flops for caffeine.
- Localized occupied orbitals have no exact zeros, so exact-only gains nothing.
- The factored path for the alkane GGA as is: measured 0.93x (29.0 vs 31.2 s, 12 sets, 1 thread); the model correctly keeps the dm path.

**Small items.**
- Batching the dm path's per-set GEMMs: <= 5% (rho 58.6 -> 58.5, dot 58.8 -> 61.7 GF/s).
- Dynamic instead of static scheduling for the dot kernels on Zen 5/5c: ~6.5% (It6) but loses reproducibility. This is a known trade-off and was kept.
- nr_rks_fxc runs _rho_setup twice (hermi_sum, per-dm condense, overlap cond): ~0.28 s (1.1%) in caffeine TDA; the factored path skips it.
- nr_rks_fxc_st rebuilds fxc[0,:,0] +/- fxc[0,:,1] per call: 0.06 s.
- The vind einsum projections (BLAS): ~0.1 s.

Scratch scripts and builds: /tmp/claude-1000/-home-danny-Chemistry-my-pyscf/3d2aa02f-ca12-40eb-b5fd-b099754f302d/scratchpad/swarm/td/ (group_stats.py, tda_factored.py, gemm_shapes.py, simd_fxc.py, mo_jk.py, build/).

findings.title: Hessian 2e terms: compute int2e_ip1ip2 / int2e_ipvip1 only for the atom pairs _partial_hess_ejk actually reads
findings.evidence:
Code: for each atom A, hessian/rhf.py:142-158 calls ip1ip2 (s1) and ipvip1 (s2kl) with shls_slice=(A, all, all, all). The pair loop at rhf.py:171-180 reads only the vj1/vk1 rows of atoms in atmlst[:i0+1]: the k index for ip1ip2, and the j index for ipvip1 through the transposes at 159/162. Blocks with B > A are filled by transposition (182-185), so the k>A part (ip1ip2) and the j>A part (ipvip1) are computed and thrown away. The same pattern is in uhf.py:155-180, in the RSH long-range K loops of rks.py:91-107 and in uks.py:91-113.
Measured at 1 thread (hess_jk_split.py):
- benzene, all 12 atoms: ip1ip2 15.86 -> 8.85 s; ipvip1 8.43 -> 4.71 s.
- caffeine ip1ip2: atom O6 15.78 -> 6.60 s; atom H23 5.62 -> 5.61 s.
- caffeine ipvip1 (atoms C0/C9/O6/H15/H23): 9.04/8.37/9.27/3.12/3.40 -> 0.55/4.66/3.78/2.70/3.44 s.

findings.title: Hessian 2e diagonal blocks from translational invariance: drop int2e_ipip1 and the A=A blocks of ip1ip2/ipvip1
findings.evidence:
Code: hessian/rhf.py:121-126 evaluates int2e_ipip1 (9 components, J and K) over all shells, only for ej[A,A] and ek[A,A] (rhf.py:166-168). The per-atom calls also compute the k in A (ip1ip2) and j in A (ipvip1) blocks, which feed only the diagonal.
Translational invariance: sum over B of dA dB (ij|kl) = 0, so e2[A,A] = -sum over B != A of e2[A,B], for ej and ek separately.
Measured on the tree's _partial_hess_ejk (ti_check.py):
- TI residual 1.8e-12 (water ej), 7.1e-12 (benzene ej, |ej| up to 22.5), 1.2-1.3e-12 (ek).
Prototype (ejk_pairs.py: deriv-hess-pairs with k/j < A, plus TI diagonal), benzene RHF at 1 thread:
- 32.34 -> 10.76 s (3.0x);
- off-diagonal blocks bitwise identical, e1 identical, diagonal blocks within 7.1e-12 (ej) and 1.2e-12 (ek).
Caffeine ipip1 on single-atom i slices: O6 9.19 s, H23 3.19 s, which puts the full call at about 157 s at 1 thread.
findings.current_cost: caffeine B3LYP: ipip1 about 157 s at 1 thread (24% of the 657 s of 2e J/K), about 26 s at 10 threads. The A=A blocks of the per-atom calls are another 2.5% of their work (about 11 s at 1 thread). benzene: ipip1 8.43 s at 1 thread, about 3.1 s at 10 threads (6 tasks, modelled efficiency 0.38).

On top of deriv-hess-pairs:

- benzene: about 4.1 s at 10 threads by the task model; together with deriv-hess-pairs about 5.6 s (31% of 17.9 s).

The diagonal blocks then differ from the directly computed ones by the TI residual of the analytic derivative integrals: 7e-12 absolute, 3e-13 relative on benzene. findings.title: hess_elec post-CPHF contraction: replace 3-operand numpy einsums and per-pair recomputed dm1 with GEMMs
findings.evidence:
Code:
- hessian/rhf.py:73 computes s1oo = numpy.einsum('xpq,pi,qj->xij', s1ao, mocc, mocc) per atom. numpy.einsum defaults to optimize=False, so this runs a 5-index loop of 3*nao^2*nocc^2 iterations.
- rhf.py:79 and 81 recompute dm1 and the 3-operand energy-weighted dm1 for every pair (i0,j0), although both depend only on ja.
- uhf.py:80-90 does all of this once per spin.
Measured (hess_elec_loop.py: this exact loop on caffeine and benzene shapes with synthetic mo1/h1ao, 1 thread):

findings.title: CVHFnr_direct_drv gives gradient/Hessian calls on ~100-AO molecules only 6-8 parallel tasks: smaller or adaptive task blocks
findings.evidence:
Code:
- nr_direct.h:22 sets AO_BLOCK_SIZE 64; nr_direct.c:398-401 partitions with it.
- nr_direct.c:429-430 runs omp for schedule(dynamic,1) over the j, k and l blocks only; the i blocks of the sliced atom are looped inside each task.
- benzene (nao 114) has 2 blocks per index, hence 8 tasks per s1 call and 6 non-empty ones per s2kl call (CVHFdot_nrs2kl returns early for k<l blocks).
- The SCF's batched driver (nr_direct_batch.c) does not use AO_BLOCK_SIZE.
Task model (task_model.py: greedy dynamic schedule, cost proportional to AO quartets), 10-thread efficiency:
- with 64-AO blocks: benzene 0.62 (ip1ip2) and 0.38 (ipvip1, ipip1, make_h1 ip1, gradient get_jk); caffeine 0.91-0.93;
- with 32-AO blocks: benzene 0.95-0.96; caffeine 1.00.
The model matches the measured scaling:
- benzene Hessian 2e J/K: 36.7 s at 1 thread (hess_jk_split.py) vs 11.34 s at 10 threads (profile-it13), 3.2x; model 10.7 s.
- benzene gradient J/K: 3.36 s vs 1.298 s, 2.6x; model 1.25 s.
- direct SCF J/K scales 6.6x (NOTES It7: 7.16 -> 1.08 s), and NOTES It3 found the benzene gradient 8% slower at 20 threads.
findings.current_cost:
- hess_benzene_svp_b3lyp: nr_direct_drv 11.34 s of 17.87 s.
- grad_benzene_svp_b3lyp: 1.298 of 1.46 s.
- hess_caffeine_svp_b3lyp: 107.8 s, at modelled efficiency about 0.92.
- grad_caffeine_svp_b3lyp: 7.48 s, at about 0.91.
findings.proposal: In CVHFnr_direct_drv and CVHFnr_direct_ex_drv, choose the j/k/l block size per call so that the number of non-empty tasks is at least about 8x the thread count (64, then 32, then 16), or simply use 32: NOTES It7 found 32- or 16-AO blocks 3-5% faster even for SCF direct J/K. Size keys_cache (nr_direct.c:262) from the block size actually used. This touches the J/K driver (overlap with the J/K analyst), but the cause is the per-atom call structure of gradients and Hessians.
findings.expected_gain:
- benzene Hessian J/K: 11.3 -> about 5.6 s (-5.7 s, 32% of wall) with today's call structure; it also keeps the deriv-hess-pairs/ti gains at 10 threads (combined, benzene 2e J/K about 11.3 -> 2.4 s).
- benzene gradient: 1.30 -> about 0.5 s (-0.8 s, about 55%).
- caffeine Hessian: about 7-8% of the J/K (about 8 s now, about 4 s after deriv-hess-pairs/ti).
- caffeine gradient: about 0.6 s (8%).
- n-C20H42 gradient: none (288 tasks already).
findings.exactness_notes: The per-thread JKArray partial sums are grouped differently. The dynamic schedule already makes the summation order nondeterministic.

findings.title: Hessian 2e-derivative J/K run unscreened: _make_vhfopt is dead code and make_h1 passes no vhfopt
findings.evidence:
Code:
- rhf.py:192 returns None from `if not hasattr(libcvhf, vhf_intor)`. It tests 'int2e_ip1ip2', 'int2e_ipip1ipip2' and 'int2e_ipvip1ipvip2' without the _sph/_cart suffix, and those symbols do not exist. check_vhfopt.py confirms it returns None in both pyscf and pyscf-base.
- So ipip1, ip1ip2 and ipvip1 get vhfopt=None, which means CVHFnoscreen (nr_direct.c:59-78).
- make_h1 never passes a vhfopt (rhf.py:236, rks.py:154-176, uhf.py:229, uks.py:160-191), unlike grad/rhf.py get_jk, which uses CVHFgrad_jk_prescreen.
Enabling it as written would break in two places:
- _VHFOpt.set_dm stacks dms of different shapes, which raises ValueError in numpy 2.
- CVHFnr_int2e_pppp_q_cond (hessian_screen.c:309-331) reads components at offsets (a*16+a)*iijj of an 81-component integral, where the diagonal is at a*10. Five of its nine reads fall past the computed data.
Measured with a working opt (pp q_cond plus dm_cond of the full dm0), 1 thread:
- caffeine ip1ip2 (k<=A): O6 6.60 -> 4.83 s, H23 5.61 -> 3.45 s (0.68); max abs diff 9e-14.
- caffeine make_h1 ip1: 4.23/1.55 -> 2.77/0.96 s (0.65); max abs diff 1.4e-11.
- benzene: 0.97-0.99 (compact molecule).
findings.current_cost: caffeine: all of the 107.8 s of 2e-derivative J/K at 10 threads runs unscreened, and about 32-35% of its quartet work falls below the 1e-14 threshold. benzene: 1-3%.
findings.proposal:
- Fix the hasattr test (use mol._add_suffix).
- Give the vhfopt a dm_cond from the full dm0 (for UHF, the max over dm0a, dm0b and dm0) and set dmcondname=None.
- Fix the pppp q_cond offsets to a*9+a; this is needed only for ipvip1 once deriv-hess-ti drops ipip1.
- Add a make_h1 prescreen that tests all four of its dm patterns (ji, lk, li, jk). The gradient's prescreen omits ji and li.
- Make it opt-in (e.g. hessobj.direct_scf_tol, default None = today's behavior), or the default if the user accepts the gradient's level of screening.
findings.expected_gain:
- caffeine B3LYP: about 211 s at 1 thread (about 34 s at 10 threads) without deriv-hess-pairs/ti; about 90 s (about 14-15 s, 8%) after them.
- Much more for elongated molecules: only 17% of the n-C20H42/SVP s8 quartets are Schwarz-significant (NOTES It9).
- benzene: 3% or less.
findings.exactness_notes: New Schwarz/density screening at 1e-14, as in the gradient. Measured absolute deviations of the J/K matrices: 9e-14 for ip1ip2 and 1.4e-11 for make_h1 with the gradient prescreen. The end-to-end effect on the Hessian was not measured; it is expected to be 1e-10 or less, against a 1e-7 tolerance.

findings.title: lib.krylov (CPHF solver) orthogonalizes and builds its subspace matrix one vector at a time
findings.evidence:
Code (lib/linalg_helper.py):
- 1319-1322: one GEMV plus one rank-1 update per previous vector, in Python, every cycle.
- 1349-1357: nd^2 separate dot calls to build h.
- 1365: g, also vector by vector.
Profile, hess_caffeine_svp_b3lyp: krylov 0.912 s self, _qr 0.259 s, _outprod_to_subspace 0.142 s.
Synthetic test (krylov_cost.py, 1 thread, 72 RHS x 12546, the caffeine CPHF shape, 10 cycles, 650 vectors):
- lib.krylov 3.29 s, of which aop 0.06 s;
- the same classical Gram-Schmidt done with 2 GEMMs per cycle, and h and g with one GEMM each: 0.71 s (mostly _qr);
- same cycle count, max |dx| 1.9e-13 for |x| = 5.3.
The real benzene CPHF runs 6 cycles with 36, 36, 35, 33, 32, 13 vectors (cphf_trace.py).
findings.current_cost: caffeine: about 1.3 s (0.7% of 181 s). Grows as nd^2*ndim: extrapolated to about 30 s for a 60-atom, 490-AO Hessian (186 RHS, about 1100 vectors).
findings.expected_gain: About 1 s on caffeine, and about 75% of the solver overhead for larger systems.
findings.exactness_notes: Same classical Gram-Schmidt, different summation order. A vector whose norm sits exactly at the lindep/tol mask threshold could in principle flip.

findings.title: UHF/UKS make_h1 contracts the Coulomb part separately with dm0a and dm0b
workloads: UKS Hessians of medium molecules (target, not benchmarked)
findings.evidence:
Code: uks.py:160-167 and 188-192, and uhf.py:229-236, pass 'ji->s2kl' and 'lk->s1ij' once with -dm0a and once with -dm0b, then form vj1 = vj1a+vj1b and vj2 = vj2a+vj2b. J is linear in the dm, so passing dm0a+dm0b once gives the same result.
Each dm adds a contraction pass over every quartet, about 9-10% of the integral time for 3-component ip1:
- benzene: make_h1 with 4 dms takes 4.00 s vs 3.46 s (unscreened equivalent) for the 2-dm gradient get_jk, i.e. 0.27 s per dm on 2.92 s of integrals;
- native_grad_caffeine: the nrs2kl_* contraction kernels take 9.2% for 2 dms, vs 45.1% for int2e_ip1_sph.
findings.current_cost: UKS is not in the profile. The RKS caffeine make_h1 J/K is about 73 s at 1 thread (about 12 s at 10 threads); a UKS hybrid make_h1 has 8 dms instead of 4, so roughly 1.8/1.4 of that.
findings.proposal: Pass 'ji->s2kl' with -(dm0a+dm0b)[:,p0:p1] and 'lk->s1ij' with -(dm0a+dm0b) once, in uks.make_h1 (both branches) and uhf.make_h1.
findings.expected_gain: About 11% of the UKS hybrid make_h1 J/K (8 -> 6 dms) and about 13% for pure functionals (4 -> 2): about 1.5-2 s for a caffeine-size UKS Hessian.

ruled_out:
Where the einsum time goes. The caffeine Hessian's 14.87 s of c_einsum (12229 calls) splits into:
- about 11.2 s in the hess_elec loop (deriv-hesselec-blas);
- about 3.2-3.7 s in the per-atom XC terms (_make_dR_rho1, the wv einsum, _atom_pair_sum; deriv-xc-onepass);
- about 0.2-0.3 s in the per-pair einsums of _partial_hess_ejk, partial_hess_elec and vxc_dm. Too small to pursue.

Checked and not worth pursuing (or exact gains not available):
1. HDF5/chkfile traffic: none in this tree. h1ao, mo1 and mo_e1 stay in in-memory lists (rhf.py:232-247, 324-353; uhf.py is the same), and the cases set mf.chkfile=None.
2. Replacing the post-Krylov fvind(mo1) in cphf.solve_withs1 (cphf.py:136-139) with the Krylov vectors' cached responses.
   - It is 1 of 7 response builds on benzene: 36 vectors, 3.06 of 21.3 s of fx time at 1 thread (cphf_trace.py).
   - But the reset of the occupied block (cphf.py:134) puts mo1 outside their span by 6.1e-7 relative (measured), so results would move at CPHF-tolerance level, not rounding.
3. Fewer CPHF iterations: benzene takes 6+1 response builds and caffeine 7+1 (8 _incore_s8_batch calls). Cutting them needs a looser tol or a level shift, i.e. an approximation.
4. solve_mo1 back-transformation einsum (rhf.py:345): 0.05 s on caffeine (0.01 s with lib.einsum).
5. The left-to-right reduce(numpy.dot, (C^T, v, mocc)) association in vind_mo and gen_vind: about 0.2-0.4 s per caffeine Hessian.
6. hcore_deriv(ia, ja) recomputing rinv derivative integrals for each atom pair (rhf.py:509-559).
   - On caffeine: get_hcore 0.251 s over 300 calls, getints2c 0.218 s over 1187, make_cintopt 0.072 s.
   - Computing them once per center would save 0.4 s or less.
7. Translational invariance for make_h1's 2e part (skip the most expensive atom's ip1 call): about 5% of make_h1 J/K, about 0.6 s on caffeine.
8. Sharing fxc between cache_xc_kernel and the deriv1/deriv2 passes: libxc takes 0.04 s in the whole caffeine Hessian.
9. Gradients.
   - The single, already screened int2e_ip1 J/K call is 92% of grad_caffeine (7.48 of 8.14 s) and 94% of the alkane gradient (26.55 of 28.26 s). XC is 0.57 s (done in It12).
   - The 3-of-4 translational-invariance trick with the contraction inside the integral loop is already in NOTES 'Next iterations' and is J/K-kernel work.
   - A fused ip1/ipip1/ip1ip2/ipvip1 qcint kernel that shares Rys roots would be a deep qcint change.
   - The only structural lever left here is the task decomposition (deriv-jk-tasks).
10. Belongs to other analysts:
    - CPHF J/K: _incore_s8_batch 8.57 s over 8 calls on caffeine (J/K analyst).
    - CPHF XC: rho_lowrank + dot_ao_mo 36.2 s (XC/It13).
    - UKS CPHF has no vind_mo yet (NOTES 'Next iterations').
11. gen_hop has the same einsum patterns, but kernel() does not use it.
12. DF Hessians have their own 3-center _partial_hess_ejk, so only deriv-hesselec-blas applies to them.

All scripts are in /tmp/claude-1000/-home-danny-Chemistry-my-pyscf/3d2aa02f-ca12-40eb-b5fd-b099754f302d/scratchpad/swarm/deriv/. Timings are single-threaded. The 10-thread conversions use the measured ratio (caffeine 2e J/K about 657 s at 1 thread vs 107.8 s at 10 threads) or the task model.

title: UKS and density fitting

findings.title: UKS in-core J/K: the two spin densities take the slow small-batch kernels, costing 0.22 s per call against 0.082 s for the RKS single-dm call
workloads: any UKS/UHF/ROKS hybrid SCF whose ERIs fit in memory (nao up to ~370 at PYSCF_MAX_MEMORY=20000)
findings.evidence:
Profile (bench/results/profile-it13/summary.txt):
- scf_caffeine+_svp_b3lyp_uks: scf/_vhf.py:509(_incore_s8_batch) takes 5.502 s over 25 calls, 0.220 s per call. That is 26% of the 21.16 s wall time.
- RKS scf_caffeine_svp_b3lyp: the same function takes 1.392 s over 17 calls, 0.082 s per call.
- In It9, semi-direct UKS at 4000 MB cost 6.1 s / 25 = 0.244 s per call and RKS 3.8 s / 17 = 0.224 s.
- So in-core RKS is 2.7x faster than semi-direct RKS, but in-core UKS is barely faster than semi-direct UKS. The UKS 'jk' category at 20 GB is 6.43 s, ERI build included.

Code:
- The fused one-pass kernel CVHFnrs8_incore_jk_1dm is only used for n_dm == 1 (pyscf/scf/_vhf.py:518).
- UKS passes 2 dms (pyscf/dft/uks.py:98), so the path is:
  - CVHFnrs8_incore_vj_batch (nr_incore_batch.c:45): tile copies plus a dgemm with N=2;
  - CVHFnrs8_incore_vk_batch (nr_incore_batch.c:126-185): every packed ERI row is memcpy'd into an mdim x mdim buffer, then two dsymm calls with only 2 columns.
- uks.py:103 then keeps only vj[0]+vj[1].

Measured at 1 thread (scratchpad swarm/uks_df/incore_uks_jk.py and incore_crossover.py), naphthalene+/def2-SVP, ERIs 1.06 GB:
- current 2-dm call: 281.5 ms (J 75, K 217);
- 1-dm kernel once per spin: 168 ms;
- J(Da+Db) and K(Da) in one 1-dm pass, then a K-only pass for Db: 125 ms;
- benzene+: 45.5 ms with the current call, 21.5 ms with the last variant;
- batch path per dm: 132 ms (2 dms), 107 (3), 79 (4), 51 (8), against 84 ms for the 1-dm kernel. The crossover is at about 4 dms.
findings.current_cost: 5.50 s of 21.16 s (26%) in scf_caffeine+_svp_b3lyp_uks at 10 threads. That is about 0.14 s per SCF cycle more than an ideal one-pass kernel would take.
findings.proposal:
Three options, in increasing order of effort:
- (a) Python only, API unchanged: in _incore_s8_batch, when the dms are symmetric (sym_k) and n_dm <= 3, call CVHFnrs8_incore_jk_1dm once per dm.
- (b) In dft/uks.py get_veff (hybrid branch), compute J of the spin-summed density. The 1-dm kernel already takes separate dmtri (for J) and dm (for K) arguments. Pass tri(Da+Db) with Da, then make a K-only call with Db; only vj[0]+vj[1] is ever used. Expose this as a private _vhf helper used when mf._eri is set.
- (c) In C, generalize _jk_1dm_row_body (nr_incore_batch.c:226) to n <= 4 dms: each packed ERI row is read once, K is formed for each dm and J for their sum. Use the same AVX2 dispatch. This covers UHF, ROHF/ROKS and 2-4-dm callers.
findings.exactness_notes: Measured against the current path: J (summed) to 7.5e-15 relative and K to 6.1e-15 relative (naphthalene+). J is linear, so J(Da+Db) = J(Da)+J(Db) up to rounding.

findings.title: DF exchange of response densities (TDA/TDDFT/CPHF with DF hybrids) costs O(naux*nao^3) per dm; the factored form costs nocc/nao of that
workloads: DF hybrid TDA/TDDFT, RKS and UKS (e.g. caffeine/SVP or TZVP DF-B3LYP TDA)
DF hybrid Hessians and CPHF (hess_water_svp_b3lyp_df; caffeine-size DF Hessians)
findings.proposal:
- The response code tags the dms with their factors:
  - TDA (tdscf/rhf.py and uhf.py vind): L_k = Cvir X_k^T and R = Cocc;
  - RPA: one such term for X and one for Y;
  - CPHF (hessian rhf/uhf gen_vind, It13's vind_mo): L_k = C x_k, R = Cocc, plus the transpose.
- df_jk.get_jk gets a factored branch, next to the existing mo_coeff branch: per aux block, unpack B once and form BR = B R once; per dm, form BL = B L_k and add BL^T BR to vk[k] as GEMMs.
- In the existing non-factored branch, hoist the unpack_tril out of the k loop.
- In the SCF MO branch, use dsyrk for the symmetric lib.dot(buf1.T, buf1) (line 403). That removes 25% of the DF-SCF K flops.
- A further step for TDA: MO-basis K_ov = sum_P B^vv_P X^T B^oo_P, 2*naux*nocc*nvir*nmo flops per dm (12x fewer for caffeine/SVP).
findings.exactness_notes: Same DF approximation and the same _cderi; only the order of the products changes. The prototype agrees to 5-9e-15 absolute on |K| up to 5. Nothing is truncated: the factors come from the code that builds the dms.

findings.title: UKS CPHF and UKS Casida TDDFT XC response have no factored path (It13 covers RKS only); UKS pays 2.15x the RKS dm-path cost
workloads: UKS Hessians (hess_water+_svp_*_uks suite; caffeine+-size UKS Hessians)
UKS Casida TDDFT for pure functionals (tdscf/uks.py CasidaTDDFT, hermi=1)
UKS TDA/TDDFT, once the RKS TD factoring exists
findings.evidence:
Code:
- _gen_uhf_response (pyscf/scf/_response_functions.py:234-325) attaches no vind_mo.
- hessian/uhf.py:313-337 gen_vind builds dm1 and calls vresp(dm1). That goes to nr_uks_fxc, then _FusedXC.uks_fxc (numint.py:1366-1389): the dm path for 2*nset dms.
- The RKS counterpart is _response_functions.py:135-157 with rks_fxc_mo (numint.py:1262-1293).

Measured at 1 thread (swarm/uks_df/cphf_xc_uks_vs_rks.py), benzene/SVP B3LYP, 36 sets:
- RKS dm path 4.98 s;
- RKS factored 2.98 s (relative difference 5.7e-15);
- UKS benzene+ dm path 10.71 s for 2x36 sets, 2.15x the RKS dm path.

It13 RKS caffeine/SVP numbers:
- per call: SVWN 6.22 to 2.21 s, B3LYP 8.36 to 5.93 s, r2SCAN 25.3 to 11.6 s;
- CPHF XC over a whole Hessian: B3LYP 53.2 to 35.9 s, r2SCAN 147.7 to 66.3 s.
findings.exactness_notes: It13 measured the RKS factored path to agree to 8.1e-15 relative or better; the UKS version uses the same kernels with one set of factors per spin.

findings.title: hess_elec does single-threaded 3-operand numpy einsums per atom and per atom pair: 8 s in the RKS caffeine Hessian, about 16 s for UKS, growing as natm*nao^2*nocc^2
findings.evidence:
Code:
- pyscf/hessian/uhf.py:80-81 computes s1ooa and s1oob per atom with numpy.einsum('xpq,pi,qj->xij'). Without optimize, numpy runs this as a naive 3*nao^2*nocc^2 loop.
- uhf.py:85-93 computes dm1a/dm1b and the energy-weighted einsums for every (ia, ja) pair, although they depend only on ja. RHF has the same pattern at hessian/rhf.py:73,79,81.

Measured at 1 thread (swarm/uks_df/wv_einsum.py and s1oo_einsum.py), at caffeine sizes (nao 246, nocc 51):
- s1oo einsum: 0.259 s per call, against 0.4 ms as a matmul and 1.5 ms with optimize=True;
- RKS pair body: 6.8 ms, against 0.022 ms per pair in MO form plus 0.7 ms per atom (relative difference 3.4e-15).

numpy einsum is serial, so these times hold at 10 threads. In hess_caffeine_svp_b3lyp, c_einsum takes 14.87 s over 12229 calls (8% of 181.18 s). About 6.2 s of that is s1oo (24 atoms) and about 2.0 s is the pair loop (300 pairs).
findings.current_cost:
- RKS caffeine/SVP Hessian: about 8.2 s (4.5% of 181 s).
- UKS caffeine+: about 16.4 s (two s1oo per atom, twice the pair work).
- Scaled to n-C20H42/SVP (nao 490, nocc 81, 62 atoms): about 2.6 s per atom, about 160 s for s1oo plus about 80 s for the pairs, per RKS Hessian.
findings.proposal:
- s1oo = mocc.T @ s1ao @ mocc, as a matmul or lib.einsum.
- Once per atom ia: h1mo[ia] = h1ao[ia] @ mocc and s1mo[ia] = s1ao[ia] @ (mocc*e_occ).
- Per pair: three 3x(nao*nocc) GEMMs with mo1[ja] and mo_e1[ja].
- In uhf.hess_elec, do the same once per spin.
- Also switch solve_mo1's numpy.einsum('pq,xqi->xpi') to lib.einsum.
findings.expected_gain: -8.2 s on the RKS caffeine Hessian (4.5%) and about -16 s on a UKS caffeine+ Hessian. The remaining cost is about 0.04 s.
findings.exactness_notes: The MO form agrees to 3.4e-15 relative (pair terms) and 1.7e-14 (s1oo).

findings.title: UKS computes J separately for the alpha and beta densities and only uses their sum (response, gradients, Hessian make_h1)
findings.evidence:
Code:
- pyscf/scf/_response_functions.py:289-290, 293, 306 and 310: J of all 2*nset dms, of which only vj[0]+vj[1] is used.
- grad/uhf.py:93-94 and grad/uks.py:79-87: direct_mapdm contracts four jobs per quartet (J and K for each spin); only vj[0]+vj[1] is used.
- hessian/uks.py:158-167 and uhf.py:225-236 (make_h1): four J scripts on dm0a/dm0b, then vj1 = vj1a + vj1b.

Measured at 1 thread (swarm/uks_df/incore_jshare.py), naphthalene/SVP in-core, 20 dms:
- J is 23% of J+K at hermi=0 and 34% at hermi=1;
- J of 10 sums instead of 20 dms saves 11% (hermi=0) and 17% (hermi=1) of J+K.

Derivative J/K (native_hess_benzene_svp_b3lyp.txt): the nr_direct_dot.c contraction functions take about 9.5% of the 1-thread time, about 20% of nr_direct_drv.
findings.current_cost:
- UKS caffeine+ Hessian, in-core CPHF J/K: about 17 s (2x the RKS 8.57 s in _incore_s8_batch); a sixth of that is spent on redundant J.
- UKS TDA, in-core J/K: about 11-14 s; a tenth is redundant.
- Pure-functional UKS response: half of the response J. For a caffeine+ PBE Hessian that is about 0.44 s per CPHF call (1.3e11 flops of J per 72 dms).
- UKS gradient: 1 of 4 contraction jobs.
findings.proposal:
Compute J of the summed dms:
- In-core and DF backends: call get_j(dm1[0]+dm1[1]) and get_k(dm1) separately. Both backends already do J and K in separate passes for many dms, so no extra pass is added.
- Direct and semi-direct: add an optional J-only dm set to CVHFnr_direct_jk_batch (C), so that J and K stay in one pass.
- Gradients and make_h1: give direct_bindm/_get_jk the J scripts on dm0a+dm0b (Python only).
- The UKS SCF case is covered by uks_df-incore-2dm-jk.
findings.exactness_notes: J is linear in the density matrix, so only the summation order changes.

findings.title: The response potentials wv are built per set with single-threaded numpy einsum in uks_fxc (4x the RKS work per set), rks_fxc and rks_fxc_mo
findings.evidence:
Code:
- numint.py:1379-1386 (_FusedXC.uks_fxc): per set, two einsum('xg,xbyg->byg') calls plus w *= weight.
- numint.py:1286 (rks_fxc_mo) and :1362 (rks_fxc): einsum('yg,xyg,g->xg').

Measured at 1 thread (swarm/uks_df/wv_einsum.py), per set on a 67200-point block (the block size of these loops for caffeine): UKS GGA 1.91 ms, UKS MGGA 3.17 ms, RKS GGA 0.66 ms, RKS MGGA 1.07 ms. A numpy-broadcast batching was slower (341 vs 138 ms per 72 sets), so this needs a C pass.

Call counts (hess_caffeine_svp_b3lyp): 35 rho_lowrank calls, i.e. 7 CPHF calls x 5 blocks, with up to 72 sets each. The benzene+ DF-UKS TDA had 140 trial vectors.
findings.current_cost:
- UKS caffeine+ Hessian CPHF: about 3-5.5 s for GGA, 5-9 s for MGGA.
- UKS caffeine+ TDA: about 1.3 s.
- RKS caffeine B3LYP Hessian: about 1 s.
The share grows once uks_df-ucphf-lowrank-xc makes the GEMM kernels faster, because the wv cost per set is the same on both paths.
findings.proposal: Add one OpenMP C kernel per block for all sets: fw = fxc*weight once per block, then wv[k] = contraction of fw with rho1[k] (RKS: 4x4 or 5x5; UKS: 2x4x2x4). Alternatively, let VXCfused_dot_wv/dot_ao_mo take rho1 and fw directly.
findings.expected_gain: Bandwidth-bound at 10 threads: about 6 ms per 72-set block instead of 138 ms (UKS GGA). That saves about 3-5 s (GGA) and 5-9 s (MGGA) on a UKS caffeine+ Hessian, about 1.2 s on the UKS caffeine+ TDA, and about 1 s on the RKS caffeine Hessian.
findings.exactness_notes: Only the order of summation over the density components changes; measured differences are at most 3.5e-16 relative.

ruled_out:
Checked and not worth pursuing (or outside UKS/DF):

**UKS SCF XC: at parity with RKS.** In scf_caffeine+_svp_b3lyp_uks, dot takes 42 ms and _rho_kernel 37 ms per block, against 31 and 29 ms for RKS. Alpha and beta already share one fused kernel call (It11), and the remaining 1.3x is the second set's GEMMs. Merging the alpha/beta GEMMs in VXCfused_dot_wv/eval_rho_mo would only change GEMM shapes (est. <10% of those kernels, not measured).

**libxc spin-polarized cost: inherent.** It is 1.54x per point for B3LYP (12.2 vs 7.9 ms per block call) and about 3x for r2SCAN (1.085 s, 26% of scf_benzene+_svp_r2scan_uks). The cost is inside libxc, not on the PySCF side.

**UKS cycle count: chemistry.** 25 cycles against 17 for RKS; the exactness policy rules out changing it.

**get_overlap_cond/condense in nr_uks: a threading symptom, not work.** They cost 1.02 s at 10 threads (125 + 100 calls, 4.8% of the UKS SCF), but only 0.13 and 0.08 ms per call at 1 thread (swarm/uks_df/ovlp_cond.py), against 4.4 and 4.8 ms at 10 threads. That is thread contention, most likely numpy/scipy pthread OpenBLAS threads still spinning after eigh and dot, not compute.
- 3 of the 5 get_overlap_cond calls and 2 of the 4 condense calls per nr_uks are dead when the fused path runs: _gen_rho_evaluator is called twice and pair_mask is built before _fused_xc. The same pattern exists in nr_rks and nr_uks_fxc.
- Removing them may only move the wait to the next OpenMP region, so I did not count it. Handed to whoever covers threading.

**Direct/semi-direct UKS J/K: at parity.** Padding 2 dms to npad=4 vectors issues the same instructions as a 2-wide kernel. Semi-direct UKS costs 0.244 s per call against 0.224 s for RKS (It9), so a dedicated kernel would gain under 5%.

**UKS Hessian XC terms: at parity, apart from small einsums.** _get_vxc_diag, _get_vxc_deriv1 and _get_vxc_deriv2_dm already use It12's dot_terms, _dot_sets_aow_ao and _atom_pair_dot. The only UKS extra is the per-atom wv einsum: 7.4 ms per atom per block against 1.3 ms for RKS (swarm/uks_df/dR_wv_einsum.py), about 1.8 s per caffeine+ Hessian.

**UKS derivative-integral K scripts: small.** The alpha and beta K scripts double the K contraction. In native_hess_benzene_svp_b3lyp the nr_direct_dot.c functions are about 9.5% of the 1-thread time, so this adds about 7% of an RKS Hessian; batching alpha/beta per quartet would recover only part of it.

**nr_uks_fxc dense-path batching (Next iterations #3): little left.** Caffeine-size and benzene molecules take the fused path, so only tiny molecules (water) or cartesian basis sets still reach the per-dm loop.

**UKS gradient XC: done.** It12's get_vxc_grad already covers it.

**DF-PBE SCF (caffeine/TZVP): nothing DF-specific remains.**
- J/K is 0.28 s and the tensor build 0.6 s, out of 14.96 s.
- XC per call equals the conventional TZVP B3LYP SCF (0.605 vs 0.60 s).
- DF J streams the 1.2 GB _cderi twice per call (numpy dot 0.536 s over 18 calls); a fused single pass saves at most 0.25 s.

**DF-UKS gradients: small but free.** df/grad/rhf.py:171-227 builds rhok_oo and vkaux for all (i,j) spin pairs, but UHF/UKS use only the trace (df/grad/uhf.py:53, uks.py:97). That wastes about 4e10 flops, about 0.1-0.15 s per caffeine+/TZVP hybrid gradient. The fix needs an opt-in flag, because CASSCF/CCSD use the off-diagonal terms. The rest of the DF gradient (GEMV J, MO-factored K) is already efficient.

**DF Hessian _partial_hess_ejk/make_h1: not measured.**
- HDF5 temporaries: rho_ip1 alone is 3*nao^2*naux doubles (about 1.5 GB for caffeine/SVP), and rhok_ip1 is stored twice.
- int3c2e_ip1 is evaluated twice in make_h1.
- I did not measure this: there is no profile, and a 1-thread benzene run exceeds the 2-minute limit.
- Its CPHF K is covered by uks_df-df-k-response-lowrank.

verdicts.checked: Recomputed from summary.txt: _incore_s8_batch takes 5.502 s over 25 calls (0.220 s per call, 26% of 21.16 s) in scf_caffeine+_svp_b3lyp_uks, and 1.392 s over 17 calls (0.082 s per call) in RKS scf_caffeine_svp_b3lyp. Read scf/_vhf.py:509-580: the fused CVHFnrs8_incore_jk_1dm is only taken for n_dm==1 with sym_k or no K. Two dms go through CVHFnrs8_incore_vj_batch and vk_batch. dft/uks.py get_veff passes _dm (2 dms) to get_jk and keeps vj[0]+vj[1]; incremental_jk is off when _eri is set, so full dms are used. NOTES It7 A/E records the batch kernels 'from 2 dms' and the 1-dm fused kernel, but no 2-dm comparison and no rejection. Did not rerun the analyst's 1-thread timings.
verdicts.gain_estimate:
At 10 threads, priced with the profile's measured 0.082 s per 1-dm pass rather than It7 E's 0.056 s:
- (a) 2 x 0.082 = 0.164 s per call, about -1.4 s over 25 cycles (6.6%).
- (b) is also two ERI streams (J+K for Da, then K-only for Db). K alone is about as bandwidth-bound as J+K (0.051 vs 0.056 s in It7 E), so (b) comes to about 0.155-0.16 s per call, about -1.5 s. The analyst's -2.3 to -3.0 s is overstated: it mixes It7's 0.056 s per pass with the profile's 0.220 s baseline.
- (c) one stream with K for 2 dms: about 0.09-0.10 s per call (the K compute doubles and passes the streaming bound), about -2.5 to -3.0 s (12-14%).
verdicts.cost_seconds: 5.50 s of 21.16 s in scf_caffeine+_svp_b3lyp_uks; the excess over two 1-dm passes is about 1.4 s and the excess over one ideal pass about 3 s
verdicts.comment: The premise and code facts hold, and (a) is a few lines of Python. At 10 threads (a) and (b) are nearly equivalent: both stream the ERIs twice, so (b) buys little over (a). Only (c) captures the larger saving. There is no gain at the 4000 MB default, where caffeine+ is semi-direct.

verdicts.checked: Read df/df_jk.py:303-431. Untagged dms take the else branch: per dm, an AO2MOnr_e2_drv half transform with the full nao x nao dm (2*naux*nao^3) and lib.dot(buf1.T, buf2) (2*naux*nao^3). unpack_tril(eri1) is inside the k loop. The mo_coeff branch uses lib.dot(buf1.T, buf1), not dsyrk. tdscf/uhf.py:99-100 and rhf build dms as Cvir z^T Cocc^T, so the factors are available at build time. Recomputed flops: caffeine/SVP 4*1242*246^3 = 7.4e10 per dm, TZVP (nao 494) 6.0e11. The factored form costs 4*naux*nao^2*nocc, a ratio of nocc/nao = 0.21 and 0.10. The analyst's 1-thread rates (49-53 GFLOP/s) are consistent with these flop counts. NOTES has no DF-K response work (only It7 D, DF J-only), and Next iterations does not list it. No profiled DF hybrid TDA or Hessian case exists in bench.
verdicts.cost_seconds: 29-30% of a 1-thread benzene DF-B3LYP TDA (measured by the analyst); estimated 17-31 s for a caffeine/SVP DF-B3LYP TDA and about 55 s of DF-K in a caffeine/SVP DF-B3LYP Hessian at 10 threads

The CPHF dms are L R^T + R L^T, so they need either both terms or a symmetrized single product. The tagging is cleanest as a factored-dm attribute set by tdscf and hessian gen_vind.

verdicts.checked: Read scf/_response_functions.py:234-325: _gen_uhf_response attaches no vind_mo, while the RKS branch (lines 135-157) attaches vind_mo through rks_fxc_mo. hessian/uhf.py:313-337 gen_vind.fx builds the full dm1a/dm1b and projects v1 back with C^T v Cocc. hessian/uks.py reuses uhf_hess solve_mo1 and gen_vind. _FusedXC.uks_fxc (numint.py:1366-1389) is the dm path over 2*nset dms. The existing rho_lowrank and dot_ao_mo kernels take per-spin A, B and Q, so only the spin-coupled wv step is new. Did not rerun the 2.15x benzene+ measurement.

About -150 to -185 s for r2SCAN. Per call for benzene+ B3LYP about -0.9 s at 10 threads.

verdicts.checked: Read hessian/rhf.py:73-83 and hessian/uhf.py:80-93: the 3-operand numpy.einsum('xpq,pi,qj->xij') runs once per atom (twice for UHF), and the pair loop rebuilds dm1 through 2- and 3-operand numpy einsums per (ia, ja). Timed at 1 thread at caffeine sizes (nao 246, nocc 51; verify/einsum_t.py): s1oo 255 ms with numpy.einsum vs 0.8 ms with lib.einsum. The pair body is 9.1 ms, versus the analyst's 6.8 ms. That gives 24 x 0.255 = 6.1 s plus 300 x 9.1 ms = 2.7 s, about 8.8 s of the 14.87 s c_einsum in hess_caffeine_svp_b3lyp (181.18 s). verdicts.cost_seconds: About 8.8 s of 181.18 s in hess_caffeine_svp_b3lyp (s1oo 6.1 s, pair loop 2.7 s); about 17 s for a UKS caffeine+ Hessian

verdicts.checked:
Code facts verified:
- _response_functions.py:289-310: get_j/get_jk of all 2*nset dms, of which only vj[0]+vj[1] is used.
- grad/uks.py:79-87 and grad/uhf.py:93: get_jk of both spins, only the J sum used.
- hessian/uks.py:158-167 and uhf.py:229-236 (make_h1): four J scripts per atom summed pairwise.
In-core J for many dms is a dgemm with N = n_dm (CVHFnrs8_incore_vj_batch), so the J flops halve. Splitting get_jk into get_j(sum) + get_k on the direct and semi-direct backends would stream the integrals twice; the analyst correctly proposes a J-only dm set in the batched C driver for those. Not in NOTES.
verdicts.gain_estimate:
Hybrid cases: about 1% of a caffeine+ UKS hybrid Hessian (-2.9 s of about 300 s), about 2-3% of a UKS hybrid TDA, about 2-3% of UKS gradients (contraction is only about 14% of gradient J/K) and about -1 s in make_h1.
The larger case is not listed by the analyst: pure-functional UKS TDA/TDDFT (non-hybrid branch, J only). Halving the J dms there halves the response J. J/K is 20-30% of an RKS PBE TDA (n-C20H42: 11 of 52 s after It9, mostly contraction), so a UKS PBE TDA should gain about 8-15%. A pure UKS Hessian gains about 1-2%.
verdicts.cost_seconds: Redundant J is about 1/6 of the in-core CPHF J/K for hybrids (about 2.9 s per caffeine+ Hessian) and half of all response J for pure functionals
verdicts.comment: The response-function part is a two-line Python change on in-core and DF backends (get_j of dm1[0]+dm1[1] in the non-hybrid branch) and should be done for pure UKS response. Hybrid savings are marginal (about 1-3%) unless the direct kernel gets a J-only set. Gradient and make_h1 savings are small because integral evaluation dominates there.

verdicts.checked: Read numint.py:1366-1386 (uks_fxc: two einsum('xg,xbyg->byg') per set plus a weight multiply), 1286 (rks_fxc_mo) and 1362 (rks_fxc): einsum('yg,xyg,g->xg') per set. Timed on a 67200-point block at 1 thread (verify/wv_t.py): RKS GGA 0.50 ms per set (analyst 0.66) and UKS GGA 3.3 ms (analyst 1.91). The profile caps the RKS side: c_einsum is 0.451 s total in tda_caffeine_svp_b3lyp (25.25 s). In hess_caffeine_svp_b3lyp, 7 CPHF calls x 5 blocks x up to 72 shrinking sets x 0.5-0.66 ms comes to about 1-1.6 s of 181 s.
verdicts.cost_seconds: RKS: 0.45 s in the caffeine TDA and about 1-1.5 s in the caffeine Hessian. UKS: about 1.3-2.2 s in a caffeine+ TDA and 3-9 s in a caffeine+ Hessian (estimated).
verdicts.comment: Real but small: below 2% for every RKS workload, and only 2-4% for unprofiled UKS TDA. Best folded into uks_df-ucphf-lowrank-xc, by computing wv inside the new UKS factored loop or a shared C helper, rather than pursued on its own.

title: Python and numpy overheads, memory traffic

findings.title: Hessian hess_elec: single-threaded 3-operand and per-atom-pair einsums (O(N^5)) can become per-atom GEMMs
findings.evidence: profile-it13/summary.txt, hess_caffeine_svp_b3lyp: {c_einsum} 14.869 s over 12229 calls; numpy category 15.16 s of 181.18 s wall. hess_benzene_svp_b3lyp: c_einsum 1.049 s over 3524 calls. I ran a 1-thread cProfile of the benzene Hessian (/tmp/claude-1000/-home-danny-Chemistry-my-pyscf/3d2aa02f-ca12-40eb-b5fd-b099754f302d/scratchpad/swarm/py/hess_prof2.out). Its einsum callers: hess_elec 402 calls 0.229 s, rks_fxc_mo 663 calls 0.316 s, _make_dR_rho1 936 calls 0.274 s, _atom_pair_sum 756 calls 0.141 s; all others under 0.04 s. Microbenchmark at caffeine shapes (nao 246, nocc 51, 24 atoms, 1 thread; scratch einsum_hess.py): s1oo = numpy.einsum('xpq,pi,qj->xij', s1ao, mocc, mocc) at pyscf/hessian/rhf.py:73 has no optimize, so it runs the naive 3*nao^2*nocc^2 = 4.7e8-term loop: 268 ms per atom, 6.43 s in total. The pair body at rhf.py:75-82 costs 6.77 ms per pair x 300 pairs = 2.03 s: dm1 einsum 2.07 ms, the 3-operand dm1e einsum 4.19 ms, three 'xpq,ypq->xy' at 0.17 ms each. dm1/dm1e of atom ja do not depend on i0 but are recomputed for every i0. 8.46 s from hess_elec plus about 4.4 s of XC terms and about 1.3 s of rks_fxc_mo accounts for the 14.87 s. The function is byte-identical to pyscf-base (diff empty). pyscf/hessian/uhf.py:80-94 repeats it per spin.
findings.current_cost: hess_caffeine_svp_b3lyp: about 8.4 s of 181.2 s (4.6%). hess_caffeine_svp_r2scan: the same 8.4 s of about 199 s (4.2%). hess_benzene_svp_b3lyp/pbe: 0.23 s of 17.9 s / 15.6 s (1.3-1.5%). Cost grows as natm*nao^2*nocc^2 + natm^2*nao^2*nocc; extrapolated from the same per-term rates, about 250 s single-threaded for a 62-atom C20H42/SVP Hessian.
findings.proposal: Replace the i0/j0 loop in hess_elec (pyscf/hessian/rhf.py:67-90), and per spin in pyscf/hessian/uhf.py:75-96, with per-atom intermediates and one GEMM per term over all atom pairs. For each atom i: h1mo[i] = h1ao[ia] @ mocc; s1mo[i] = s1ao_i @ mocc (s1ao_i is nonzero only in rows/columns p0:p1, so two thin GEMMs); s1oo[i] = mocc.T @ s1mo[i]. Stack M1 = mo1[ja] as (3natm, nao*nocc) and M1e = mo1[ja]*e_occ. Then with lib.dot: de2_full (3natm x 3natm) = 4 H M1^T - 4 S M1e^T - 2 SOO E1^T, where H and S stack h1mo and s1mo, and SOO and E1 stack s1oo and mo_e1. Keep the j0<=i0 entries and mirror them as now. This uses sum_pq h1[x,p,q] (mo1[y] mocc^T)[p,q] = sum_{p,i} (h1[x] mocc)[p,i] mo1[y,p,i], and the same identity for the e_occ-weighted s1 term. Also replace solve_mo1's numpy.einsum('pq,xqi->xpi') (rhf.py:345) with lib.einsum.
findings.expected_gain: About 8.4 s (4.6%) on the caffeine Hessians: the replacement is 24x3 GEMMs of 3x246x246x51 plus three 72x12546x72 GEMMs, and the numpy.dot equivalent measured 0.055 s in total, against 8.46 s. About 0.22 s (1.2%) on the benzene Hessians; twice as much on UKS. It removes an O(N^5) single-threaded term that would dominate larger Hessians.
findings.exactness_notes: Same products, summed in GEMM order instead of c_einsum order. Measured max |diff| 1.4e-11 on values of order 1e3 with random inputs (about 1e-14 relative). The lower triangle is mirrored as before.

findings.title: Hessian XC terms: per-atom einsums, a recomputation of t, and a duplicated grid pass in _get_vxc_deriv2_dm / _get_vxc_deriv1
findings.evidence: _get_vxc_deriv2_dm (pyscf/hessian/rks.py:556-594) and _get_vxc_deriv1 (rks.py:1292-1310; MGGA 1316-1335) each run block_loop(deriv=2) over the whole grid with the same dm0. Both do eval_ao, eval_rho2, eval_xc_eff(deriv=2) and 4 _dot_ao_dm calls (ao_dm0). Then, per atom, both call _make_dR_rho1 (13 single-threaded 'pi,pi->p' einsums for GGA) and numpy.einsum('xyg,sxg->syg', wf, dR_rho1). _get_vxc_deriv2_dm also builds t from 21 _atom_pair_sum calls (rks.py:578-586). I verified that every atom's dR_rho1 equals t with components 1-3 doubled, bitwise, for both GGA and MGGA on caffeine (scratch dr_from_t.py). The wv computed by the two functions is also the same (MGGA tau column scaled by 0.5). Timings at caffeine shapes with the real F-ordered AO layout (67,200-point deriv-2 blocks, 5 blocks per pass, 1 thread; scratch hess_xc_einsum2.py): _atom_pair_sum 12.8 ms per call, 1.35 s per Hessian; 24 x _make_dR_rho1 222 ms per block and the wv einsum 82 ms per block, 3.04 s for both functions. profile-it13, hess_caffeine: eval_gto 0.842 s over 10 calls (5 per function); _dot_ao_dm 1.186 s over 80 calls; _make_dR_rho1 240 calls. Benzene 1-thread cProfile: _make_dR_rho1 einsums 0.274 s, _atom_pair_sum 0.141 s. Pure-numpy rewrites of the pair sums are slower because of the ng*nao temporary: x*y followed by add.reduceat 35.9 ms, or a GEMM with an atom-indicator matrix 37.8 ms, against 12.8 ms now.
findings.current_cost: hess_caffeine_svp_b3lyp: about 4.4 s of single-threaded einsums plus about 0.9 s of duplicated pass work (eval_gto 0.42 s, ao_dm0 and eval_rho2 about 0.5 s), about 5.3 s of 181 s (2.9%). hess_benzene: about 0.49 s of einsums plus about 0.2 s duplicated, about 0.7 s of 17.9 s (3.9%). More for r2SCAN, where MGGA adds 9 einsums per atom per block.
findings.proposal: (a) In _get_vxc_deriv2_dm, build dR for all atoms from t (dR = t.copy(); dR[:,:,1:4] *= 2) instead of 24 _make_dR_rho1 calls per block, and compute wv with one einsum 'xyg,asxg->asyg'. (b) Compute _get_vxc_deriv1 in the same grid pass (same blocks, ao, rho, fxc, ao_dm0, and the same wv), keep its vmat[natm,3,nao,nao] (35 MB for caffeine) on the hessobj, and let make_h1 reuse it when mo_coeff/mo_occ are the same objects. (c) Add a threaded libdft kernel that forms all atom-pair sums of a block in one pass over the AO and ao_dm0 arrays (13 for GGA), replacing the 21 (GGA) or 30 (MGGA) single-threaded _atom_pair_sum calls. Apply the same to hessian/uks.py.
findings.expected_gain: (a) 1.1 s on the caffeine B3LYP Hessian, 0.14 s on benzene, bitwise identical. (b) A further about 2.4 s on caffeine: deriv1's eval_gto 0.42 s, ao_dm0/eval_rho2 about 0.5 s, dR+wv 1.52 s. (c) A further about 1.4 s on caffeine (1.35 s down to about 0.15 s; bandwidth-bound at about 40 GB/s). Total about 4.5-5 s (2.5-2.8%) on caffeine B3LYP/r2SCAN Hessians, about 0.6 s (3.4%) on benzene.
findings.exactness_notes: (a) is bitwise identical (verified). (b) is bitwise when the block partition is unchanged (deriv1 currently subtracts vmat's size from max_memory, which can change its blocks). (c) changes summation order, rounding only.

findings.title: Three thread pools: numpy's and scipy's bundled pthread OpenBLAS (10 threads each) busy-spin about 0.1 s after every call, alongside libgomp's 10
findings.evidence: Mechanism, from the OpenBLAS 0.3.34 source: on x86_64 YIELDING is 8 nops (OpenBLAS/common.h:392-396), and an idle pthread-server worker spins on it for thread_timeout = 2^28 TSC ticks before sleeping (driver/others/blas_server.c:160-164, 418-424); that is about 0.13 s if the TSC runs at the 2.0 GHz nominal clock. numpy bundles libscipy_openblas64_ (0.3.34) and scipy bundles libscipy_openblas (0.3.31); both are pthread builds that read OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS and OPENBLAS_THREAD_TIMEOUT. bench/common.py:46-55 and scripts/pyscf-env.sh set no OPENBLAS_* variable, so both pools take OMP_NUM_THREADS=10. PySCF's own OpenMP OpenBLAS ignores these variables (blas_omp_number_max comes from OMP_NUM_THREADS, blas_server_omp.c:143-148). Every SCF cycle runs eig (scipy eigh), then make_rdm1 (a numpy GEMM of 3.1e6 MACs, above the 64^3 threading threshold), then nr_rks's OpenMP kernels: up to 9+9 spinners plus 10 OpenMP threads on 20 logical CPUs. Symptoms, profile-it13 at 10 threads against my 1-thread timings: get_overlap_cond 5.1 ms vs 0.13 ms per call and condense 6.6 ms vs 0.04 ms (both tiny OpenMP regions at the start of nr_rks; scratch setup_cost.py). scipy eigh 10-12.8 ms per call vs 5.8 ms at 1 thread for n=246, 24 vs 34 ms for n=490, 65 vs 163 ms for n=872 (scratch eigh_cost.py), so threading barely helps and hurts at n=246. Scaling from 1-thread native profiles of the same session: the SCF's fused XC kernels reach 4.9-5.5x (VXCfused_eval_rho_mo 12.3-13.8 s down to 2.50 s; VXCfused_dot_wv 13.4 s down to 2.66 s). The TDA's kernels, which do not follow numpy/scipy BLAS calls, reach 7.6-8.2x (VXCfused_eval_rho 70.9 s down to 8.7 s), and getints4c 7.4x (7.03 s down to 0.95 s). It3 recorded eigh going from 0.4 to 3.0 s at 20 threads, where the pools also run 20 threads. Caveat: nset (1 vs about 10) also differs between the SCF and TDA kernel calls.
findings.current_cost: Not measurable without a multi-threaded A/B, which I may not run. On caffeine/SVP B3LYP SCF (10.03 s): lower bound about 0.5 s, from get_overlap_cond+condense spending 0.48 s on about 0.01 s of work plus eigh at 0.41 s vs 0.19 s single-threaded. Upper bound about 1.6 s if the XC kernels (5.16 s) are slowed only by this and would otherwise scale like the TDA's (about 3.6 s).
findings.proposal: A/B at 10 threads on scf_caffeine_svp_b3lyp, scf_caffeine+_svp_b3lyp_uks, scf_c20h42_svp_b3lyp and tda_caffeine with: OPENBLAS_THREAD_TIMEOUT=20 (2^20 ticks, about 0.5 ms: workers stay awake through eigh's back-to-back BLAS calls but stop spinning right after); =16; OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS=1; and GOMP_SPINCOUNT=10000 for libgomp's own post-region spin. Put the winner in scripts/pyscf-env.sh and bench/common.py worker_env. Optionally move PySCF's hot numpy dots (make_rdm1, DIIS, df_jk J, krylov) to lib.dot so less work lands in the pthread pools.
findings.expected_gain: At least 0.5 s (5%) on the caffeine/SVP SCFs; up to about 1.6 s (16%) if the SCF-vs-TDA scaling gap is mostly contention. Smaller relative gains where large kernels dominate (C20H42, TZVP). OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS=1 would make eigh faster at nao about 250 (5.8 vs 10 ms) but cost 2.2 s on scf_c20h42_tzvp_pbe (22 calls x (163-65) ms); the timeout knob keeps eigh threaded.
findings.exactness_notes: OPENBLAS_THREAD_TIMEOUT and GOMP_SPINCOUNT change only idle behaviour, so results are bitwise identical. The OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS=1 variant can change rounding in scipy's threaded LAPACK/BLAS (for example dsymv partial sums).

findings.title: nr_rks/nr_uks/fxc compute _gen_rho_evaluator and pair_mask that the fused path never uses (3-5 get_overlap_cond and 2-4 condense OpenMP regions per call)
findings.evidence: nr_rks calls ni._gen_rho_evaluator (pyscf/dft/numint.py:1918), which runs _rho_setup: get_overlap_cond plus condense_to_shell per dm (numint.py:3689-3691). It then computes pair_mask = mol.get_overlap_cond() (1945) before _fused_xc (1948). The fused path repeats _rho_setup in rho_evaluator (1117) and uses neither result. The same pattern is in nr_uks (2044-2045 twice, 2074, 2078), nr_rks_fxc (2367, 2388, 2396), nr_uks_fxc (2652-2653, 2677, 2685) and cache_xc_kernel (3516). The profile counts match exactly: scf_caffeine_svp_pbe has get_overlap_cond 54 calls (3 per cycle) 0.277 s and condense 36 calls (2 per cycle) 0.237 s; UKS caffeine+ has 125 (5 per cycle) 0.544 s and 100 (4 per cycle) 0.475 s. In the TDDFT benzene 1-thread cProfile (scratch td_prof.out), _rho_setup runs 34 times for 17 vind calls. Both routines open OpenMP regions (lib/gto/fill_int2c.c:177-186; lib/np_helper/condense.c:37-42). At 1 thread they cost 0.13 ms and 0.04 ms (caffeine/SVP) and 0.58 ms and 0.16 ms (C20H42/SVP) (scratch setup_cost.py), against 5.1 ms and 6.6 ms per call in the 10-thread profile.
findings.current_cost: Measured self time at 10 threads: scf_caffeine_svp_pbe 0.51 s (5.0%); b3lyp 0.48 s (4.8%); r2scan 0.51 s (4.3%); camb3lyp 0.37 s (3.4%); tzvp_dfpbe 0.55 s (3.6%); caffeine+ UKS 1.02 s (4.8%); benzene+ UKS r2SCAN 0.30 s (7.4%); c20h42_svp 0.28-0.36 s (1.5%); tda_caffeine 0.25 s (1.0%); tddft_benzene 0.13 s (1.6%).
findings.proposal: Call _fused_xc first, and build make_rho, pair_mask, ao_loc and nbins only when it returns None (nr_rks, nr_uks, nr_rks_fxc, nr_uks_fxc, cache_xc_kernel). Memoize mol.get_overlap_cond(), for example on grids._fused_ao_data, which already checks mol by content on every use, or keyed on the _atm/_bas/_env bytes. Run NPcondense and GTOoverlap_cond serially below about 1e5 shell pairs (#pragma omp parallel if(...)).
findings.expected_gain: Removes 2/3 (RKS) to 4/5 (UKS) of get_overlap_cond calls and half of condense calls. At the profiled per-call cost: about 0.39 s per caffeine RKS SCF (3.8%), about 0.77 s UKS (3.6%), about 0.22 s benzene+ UKS (5.4%), 0.07-0.15 s TDA/TDDFT. Only about 0.03 s per SCF if that per-call cost is contention that moves to the next region (see py-blas-spin).
findings.exactness_notes: Removes unused computations and caches a pure function of mol; serial condense and overlap_cond compute each element independently, with no reduction.

findings.title: Fused fxc paths form wv = fxc·rho1·w with a single-threaded 3-operand numpy.einsum per set and per block
findings.evidence: _FusedXC.rks_fxc (pyscf/dft/numint.py:1355-1363) and rks_fxc_mo (numint.py:1281-1290) run, for every set and grid block, wv[i] = numpy.einsum('yg,xyg,g->xg', rho1[i], _fxc, weight); uks_fxc (1380-1386) runs two einsums per set; the non-fused nr_rks_fxc loop (2382) does the same. In the 1-thread TDDFT benzene cProfile (scratch td_prof.out), 840 of 960 c_einsum calls and 0.342 of 0.344 s come from rks_fxc. In the 1-thread benzene Hessian, rks_fxc_mo makes 663 calls costing 0.316 s. profile-it13 c_einsum totals: tddft_benzene 0.436 s (960 calls), tda_benzene 0.154 s (320), tda_caffeine 0.451 s (811), tda_c20h42 0.560 s (887). Microbenchmark (scratch fxc_wv.py): 0.87 ms per set per 67,200-point GGA block. Numpy-only variants (weight folded into fxc and one 2-operand einsum, or broadcast loops) are only 1.4x faster: 12.6 ms vs 17.3 ms for 20 sets.
findings.current_cost: tddft_benzene about 0.43 s of 8.52 s (5.0%); tda_benzene 0.15 s of 3.03 s (5.1%); tda_caffeine 0.45 s of 25.25 s (1.8%); tda_c20h42 0.56 s of 36.8 s (1.5%); hess_benzene 0.32 s of 17.9 s (1.8%); hess_caffeine about 1.3 s of 181 s (0.7%; estimated as about 2210 calls x about 0.6 ms).
findings.proposal: Add one small OpenMP kernel to libdft, for example VXCfxc_contract(wv, rho1, fxc+ip0, weight+ip0, nset, nrho, ng, Ngrids), computing wv[k,x,g] = sum_y rho1[k,y,g]*fxc[x,y,g]*w[g]. Chunk over g so a chunk's nrho^2 fxc values stay in L1 while all sets are processed; add a UKS variant for 'xg,xbyg->byg'. Call it once per block from rks_fxc, rks_fxc_mo, uks_fxc and nr_rks_fxc. Keeping the (rho1*fxc)*w product order and the y order reproduces c_einsum's sum_of_products_three.
findings.expected_gain: The operation is bandwidth-bound (per set and point: 4-5 doubles read, 4-5 written), so about 8-10x on 10 threads, saving about 85% of the above: tddft_benzene about 0.37 s (4.3%); tda_benzene about 0.13 s (4.3%); tda_caffeine about 0.4 s (1.6%); tda_c20h42 about 0.48 s (1.3%); hess_benzene about 0.27 s (1.5%); hess_caffeine about 1.1 s (0.6%).
findings.exactness_notes: Bitwise if the kernel keeps c_einsum's per-element operation order; otherwise rounding only.

findings.title: Grids.build: arg_group_grids sorts structured rows via numpy.unique(axis=0); an integer box key gives the identical permutation 12-14x faster
workloads: all scf_* cases (grids are built inside the timed SCF)
findings.evidence: pyscf/dft/gen_grid.py:466-469 calls numpy.unique(box_ids, axis=0, return_inverse=True, return_counts=True). That views the (ngrids, 3) integer rows as a structured void dtype and argsorts with the generic VOID_compare (_unpack_field_index 0.8% and VOID_compare 0.6% in native_grid_caffeine_svp.txt); the counts are never used. It runs once per Grids.build (gen_grid.py:667-668). In profile-it13, the <method 'argsort'> entry is mostly this one call; the other calls are get_occ's on 246-872 energies. Its totals: 0.171 s over 19 calls (scf_caffeine_svp_pbe), 0.183 s (b3lyp), 0.174 s (tzvp_b3lyp), 0.170 s over 50 calls (caffeine+ UKS), 0.105 s (benzene+ UKS), 0.395 s over 13 calls (c20h42_svp_b3lyp), 0.413 s (r2scan), 0.409 s (tzvp_pbe). Measured at 1 thread (scratch group_grids.py): arg_group_grids 162 ms on caffeine (294,796 points) and 397 ms on C20H42 (694,296 points); the replacement 11.7 ms and 32.3 ms, with numpy.array_equal confirming the identical permutation.
findings.current_cost: 0.15-0.17 s per caffeine SCF (1.5-1.7%); 0.37-0.40 s per C20H42 SCF (2.0% of 18.8 s for SVP B3LYP, 1.8% of 22.7 s for r2SCAN); about 0.1 s on benzene+ UKS (2.4% of 4.09 s).
findings.proposal: After clipping box_ids to [-1, boxes], form key = ((ix+1)*(ny+2) + (iy+1))*(nz+2) + (iz+1) as int64 and return key.argsort(kind='stable'). Lexicographic row order equals the order of this key, and numpy.unique's inverse is the key's rank, so the stable argsort yields the same permutation.
findings.expected_gain: 0.15 s per caffeine SCF (1.5%), 0.37 s per C20H42 SCF (2.0%), about 0.09 s on benzene+ UKS (2.2%), and the same on every geometry step of an optimization.
findings.exactness_notes: Identical permutation, so identical grids (verified on caffeine and C20H42).

findings.title: CPHF lib.krylov uses per-vector numpy.dot loops (classical Gram-Schmidt, nd^2 subspace dots), and gen_vind builds dm1 per set
findings.evidence: pyscf/lib/linalg_helper.py:1318-1323 subtracts every previous vector one at a time (w = dot(axt, xs[i]); x1 -= xs[i]*w). All w use axt, so this is classical Gram-Schmidt and can be batched. Lines 1349-1358 build h with nd^2 one-dimensional numpy.dot calls and 1363-1365 build g the same way; _outprod_to_subspace (1434) and _qr (1411) loop per vector. pyscf/hessian/rhf.py:362-376 makes two numpy.dot calls per set to build dm1. profile-it13, hess_caffeine_svp_b3lyp: krylov tottime 0.912 s for 1 call (the C-level numpy.dot work is charged to it; in the benzene 1-thread cProfile krylov made 35,122 dot calls); _qr 0.259 s; _outprod_to_subspace 0.142 s; _functools.reduce 0.196 s over 1060 calls; 1.51 s in total. hess_benzene: 0.078 + 0.013 + 0.011 + 0.026 = 0.13 s.
findings.current_cost: hess_caffeine 1.5 s of 181 s (0.8%); hess_benzene 0.13 s of 17.9 s (0.7%). nd is about 3*natm*iterations, so the nd^2*nmo*nocc dot loop grows about as natm^4; estimated at over 10 s for a 62-atom alkane Hessian (186 roots, ndim 39,690).
findings.proposal: Keep xs and ax as growing 2-D arrays. Compute w = (axt @ X^H)/innerprod and x1 = axt - w @ X with lib.dot (the same classical Gram-Schmidt). Form h = X^H AX^T and g = X^H b as single GEMMs (hermi branch: full GEMM, then symmetrize), and _outprod_to_subspace as c^T X. In gen_vind.fx, build dm1 with lib.einsum('pa,kai,qi->kpq', mo_coeff, mo1*2, mocc) and add its transpose.
findings.expected_gain: About 1.3 s (0.7%) on the caffeine Hessians and about 0.1 s on benzene; much more for larger Hessians.
findings.exactness_notes: Mathematically identical (classical Gram-Schmidt is already used); only summation order changes. Rounding-level changes in the Krylov iterates could in principle shift a convergence check by one iteration.

findings.title: DF J-only builds stream the 3-center tensor from DRAM twice per cycle, through numpy's pthread BLAS
findings.evidence: pyscf/df/df_jk.py:357-360 runs vj += dmtril.dot(eri1.T).dot(eri1) for each auxiliary block of blockdim (240) rows. Each block is 240 x 122,265 x 8 B = 235 MB, so it is not cache-resident and both products read it from DRAM: about 1.56 GB per cycle for the 0.78 GB tensor (It7 D). profile-it13, scf_caffeine_tzvp_dfpbe: <method 'dot' of 'numpy.ndarray' objects> 0.536 s over 333 calls (3.6% of 14.96 s, in 'other'). Most of that is this J at about 50 GB/s, which is DRAM-bound; the rest is nao^3 GEMMs in DIIS/make_rdm1. The work runs in numpy's spinning pthread pool (see py-blas-spin). This overlaps the J/K analyst's area.
findings.current_cost: About 0.43-0.5 s of 14.96 s (about 3%) per caffeine/TZVP DF-PBE SCF.
findings.proposal: A small OpenMP kernel (or lib.dot on sub-blocks) over auxiliary rows: each thread takes rows P, computes rho_P = L_P·D and immediately vj_thread += rho_P·L_P while the 1 MB row is still in L2/L3, then reduce the per-thread vj (npair doubles each) in fixed order. That is one DRAM pass over the tensor instead of two.
findings.expected_gain: About 0.2-0.25 s per DF SCF (1.5%); grows with the tensor size.
findings.exactness_notes: Different summation order of rho and vj; deterministic for a fixed thread count.

findings.title: Fused dot kernels zero and reduce nthreads x nset private matrices once per grid block instead of once per call
workloads: CPHF dm path for many dms (C20H42 B3LYP)
findings.evidence: VXCfused_dot_wv (pyscf/lib/dft/nr_numint_fused.c:531-544, calloc(npriv*nn) per thread; :679 NPomp_dsum_reduce_inplace; :682-699 the add into vmat) and VXCfused_dot_ao_mo (:1071-1082, :1215) are called once per block by _FusedXC.dot / dot_ao_mo (numint.py:1149, 1224). The callers loop over blocks: rks_fxc uses 5 blocks for caffeine and 11 for C20H42, and tda_c20h42 makes 66 dot calls (6 rks_fxc calls x 11 blocks). With about 10 sets per call at 10 threads, each call zeroes and then reduces 10 x 10 x nao^2 x 8 B: 48 MB on caffeine, 192 MB on C20H42. NOTES ('Next iterations') puts the same cost at about 6 s of 44 s for 186 alkane dms. For the caffeine Hessian's dot_ao_mo (72 sets x 246 x 51 x 8 B = 7.2 MB per thread per call, 35 calls) it is only about 5 GB of traffic, about 0.15 s of 18.6 s.
findings.current_cost: Estimated, not measured: about 0.5-0.8 s of tda_c20h42 (1.4-2.2%; 66 calls x about 10 ms of zero/reduce traffic); about 0.15-0.25 s of tda_caffeine (0.6-1%); about 6 s for the 186-dm alkane dm-path CPHF.
findings.proposal: Keep the private matrices for a whole rks_fxc/nr_rks call: pass a per-call workspace (or an opaque handle) to VXCfused_dot_wv and VXCfused_dot_ao_mo so threads accumulate across blocks and the reduction runs once at the end. Alternatively, give the kernel all of a call's blocks in one invocation when wv for the whole grid fits (nset x nrho x ngrids x 8 B: 222 MB for 10 GGA sets on C20H42).
findings.expected_gain: Removes (nblocks-1)/nblocks of the zero/reduce traffic: about 0.5-0.7 s on tda_c20h42 (1.5%), about 0.15 s on tda_caffeine, about 5 s on the 186-dm alkane dm-path call.
findings.exactness_notes: Per-thread partial sums span blocks, which changes summation order; the result stays deterministic for a fixed thread count.

ruled_out:
All scripts and outputs are in /tmp/claude-1000/-home-danny-Chemistry-my-pyscf/3d2aa02f-ca12-40eb-b5fd-b099754f302d/scratchpad/swarm/py/. Every experiment ran at 1 thread through run_in.py.

- **Chkfile/HDF5 I/O.** dump_chk costs 0.49 ms per cycle at caffeine/SVP and 0.93 ms at C20H42/TZVP (nao 872) (chk_cost.py), so at most 0.02 s per SCF. The benchmarks set mf.chkfile = None, and the perf tree's Hessian passes chkfile=None (h1ao and mo1 stay in memory). TD and gradients do not write chk.
- **Logger, timers and ctypes glue.** time.process_time: 56 calls, 0.004 s. ctypes.cast: about 3000 calls, 0.008 s per SCF. _FusedXC._args: 0.006 s. Negligible.
- **Page faults of large numpy temporaries.** numpy madvises transparent huge pages (THP is in madvise mode). Fresh pages cost about 35 ms/GB: eval_ao at deriv 2 (984 MB) takes 221 ms fresh vs 186 ms with out= (fresh_pages.py). grid_caffeine allocates about 11 GB of AO arrays per run, so at most 0.39 s single-thread-equivalent, about 0.1 s (3%) at 10 threads. The fix is user-side (eval_ao(..., out=buf)); NumInt.block_loop already reuses its buffer.
- **libc memset/memmove at 1 thread** (raw py-spy stacks attributed to callers, attrib.py).
  - SCF caffeine: memset 1.1%, memmove 3.0% (1.1% in the ERI build's store_ij, about 1.5% in the fused group gathers).
  - grid_caffeine: memset 7.2%, of which 3.9% is GTOshell_eval_grid_cart_deriv2 zero-filling its output before accumulating primitives (AO-evaluation area) and 3.0% is OpenBLAS's beta=0 zero fill under NPdgemm.
  - Small, and mostly in other analysts' kernels.
- **Fused-kernel private matrices at medium size.** VXCfused_dot_ao_mo's calloc and reduction on caffeine come to about 0.15 s of 18.6 s. VXCfused_dot_wv in SCF (nset=1) uses 484 KB per thread per block. Both are negligible; only many sets with a large nao matter (finding py-fused-priv-blocks).
- **Pure-numpy rewrites.**
  - Atom pair sums via an x*y product plus add.reduceat, or a GEMM with an atom-indicator matrix: 36-38 ms vs 12.8 ms for the current einsum. The ng*nao temporary dominates, so this needs a C kernel.
  - The fxc contraction: numpy variants gain only 1.4x (12.6 vs 17.3 ms for 20 sets).
- **Smaller numpy items.**
  - TD Davidson: tda_caffeine _qr 0.09 s; 27,520 ndarray.dot calls 0.10 s.
  - solve_mo1's numpy.einsum('pq,xqi->xpi'): 3 ms on benzene, about 0.07 s on caffeine.
  - _GridAOData.matches array_equal: 0.4 ms per call (68 calls, 0.025 s).
  - Module imports during grad runs: about 0.02 s.
  - Grid _sparse_enough count_nonzero: 121 calls, 0.009 s.
- **argsort as contention evidence: dropped.** At first, get_occ's argsort looked like main-thread preemption at about 9 ms per call. It is in fact the single numpy.unique(axis=0) sort inside grid grouping (now finding py-grid-group-key); the per-cycle argsorts take microseconds.
- **OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS=1 as the default fix: rejected.** It makes scipy eigh single-threaded, which is faster at nao 246 (5.8 vs 10 ms) but slower at nao 872 (163 vs 65 ms, +2.2 s on scf_c20h42_tzvp_pbe). OPENBLAS_THREAD_TIMEOUT keeps eigh threaded.

The GEMM identity sum_pq h1[x,p,q](mo1[y] mocc^T)[p,q] = sum_pi (h1[x] mocc)[p,i] mo1[y,p,i] is correct, so only the summation order changes. NOTES has nothing on hess_elec.
