title: SCF driver, setup and linear algebra

findings.title: Oversubscription: numpy's and scipy's bundled OpenBLAS pools busy-spin for 134 ms after every threaded call, competing with PySCF's OpenMP threads in every SCF cycle
findings.evidence: MECHANISM (code). numpy 2.5.4 bundles OpenBLAS 0.3.34.106 (.venv/lib/python3.12/site-packages/numpy.libs/libscipy_openblas64_-f48b354e.so) and scipy bundles 0.3.31.dev (scipy.libs/libscipy_openblas-5f890258.so). Both are pthread builds: no USE_OPENMP in their config strings, and they carry the pthread-only 'Detect OpenMP Loop' warning. They are separate from PySCF's OpenMP OpenBLAS (install/openblas). Each pool takes its size from OMP_NUM_THREADS=10 (OpenBLAS/driver/others/init.c:835-838). Idle workers spin on 8 nops per iteration rather than sched_yield (OpenBLAS/common.h:393-397, since 0.3.27, commit 07b1c0bc1). They stop only after 2^THREAD_TIMEOUT = 2^28 TSC ticks (driver/others/blas_server.c:160-164, 424). The TSC runs at 1.996 GHz (lscpu BogoMIPS 3992.69), so the spin lasts 134 ms. The SCF loop re-arms both pools every cycle: SCF._eigh x.conj().T.dot(h).dot(x) and x.dot(c) (pyscf/scf/hf.py:1888, 1890; GEMMs above 64^3 run threaded, interface/gemm.c:225-255); scipy.linalg.eigh (hf.py:1889; dsymv is threaded from n=200, interface/symv.c:183-186; dsyr2k and dormtr GEMMs); make_rdm1 (hf.py:867); get_grad (hf.py:1208); DIIS error-vector dots of nao^2 elements (lib/diis.py:228); and, in every XC grid block, excsum += numpy.dot(den, exc) on 67,200 points (dft/numint.py:1312, 1339-1340, 1940, 2069-2070; ddot is threaded for n>10000, kernel/x86_64/ddot.c:174-177). numpy's 9 workers therefore spin through the whole XC phase and into J/K. scipy's 9 workers spin for 134 ms after each eigh, which covers the start of nr_rks. That is up to 18 spinners plus 10 GOMP threads on 20 logical CPUs. SYMPTOMS (profile-it13/summary.txt, scf_caffeine_svp_b3lyp, 10 threads) against my 1-thread timings of the same calls on caffeine/SVP (scratchpad/swarm/scf/percycle.py, grid_build.py): gto/mole.py:2097 get_overlap_cond 0.261 s/51 calls = 5.1 ms per call vs 0.13 ms; lib/numpy_helper.py:1226 condense 0.218 s/34 = 6.4 ms vs 0.05 ms; linalg/_decomp.py:311 eigh 0.411 s/32 calls, about 25 ms per Fock diagonalization (16 calls) vs 5.9 ms at 1 thread; dft/gen_grid.py:376 gen_grid_partition 0.121 s at 10 threads vs 0.126 s for all of get_partition at 1 thread; _dgemm 1.7 ms per 246^3 call; unpack_tril 2.2 ms per 246^2 call. The It3 thread sweep (bench/results/20261027-222823_it3-threads.json, scf_caffeine_svp_pbe/r2scan; per-call ranges at 8, 10 and 20 threads) shows these per-call costs rising with the total thread count (3 pools x OMP_NUM_THREADS), not falling: get_overlap_cond 2.4-3.6, 3.3-5.7 and 13-19 ms; eigh 5-7, 8-16 and 83-92 ms; condense 3.9-5, 5.9-7.8 and 21-29 ms. The large kernels show the effect as well. The same fused XC kernels speed up only 5.05x from 1 to 10 threads for VXCfused_dot_wv (13.45 s in native_scf_caffeine_svp_b3lyp.txt to 2.662 s) and 5.5x for the rho kernel (13.78 to 2.499 s) inside the caffeine SCF. In the caffeine TDA (no per-block numpy.dot) they speed up 7.7x and about 8x, and in the benzene Hessian 9.0-9.8x (dot_ao_mo 15.9 to 1.619 s). In-core J+K takes 82 ms per call in the SCF (_incore_s8_batch 1.392 s/17) against 56 ms standalone (NOTES It7 E).
findings.current_cost: Lower bound, the excess of the small calls over their 1-thread cost: scf_caffeine_svp_b3lyp 1.07 s of 10.03 s (10.7%): eigh 0.32, get_overlap_cond 0.25, condense 0.22, gen_grid_partition ~0.10, _dgemm ~0.09, ndarray.dot ~0.05, unpack_tril 0.04. scf_caffeine+_svp_b3lyp_uks ~1.85 s of 21.16 s (8.7%), including _dgemm 0.419 s for 177 calls; scf_caffeine_tzvp_dfpbe ~0.93 s of 14.96 s (6.2%); scf_benzene+_svp_r2scan_uks ~0.34 s of 4.09 s (8.3%); scf_c20h42_svp_b3lyp ~0.53 s of 18.77 s (2.8%). Not counted: the unmeasured slowdown of the XC kernels and in-core J/K themselves. The scaling gap above suggests up to ~1.7 s of the 5.2 s of XC kernel time in scf_caffeine_svp_b3lyp.
findings.proposal: Configuration only, no code change. Add export OPENBLAS_THREAD_TIMEOUT="${OPENBLAS_THREAD_TIMEOUT:-20}" to scripts/pyscf-env.sh. That is 2^20 ticks, about 0.5 ms: workers stay hot across the back-to-back BLAS calls inside one LAPACK routine, then sleep in pthread_cond_wait instead of spinning for 134 ms. Add the same variable in bench/common.py worker_env (lines 44-54 drop OPENBLAS_* from the inherited environment), so the benchmarks measure the user's setting. PySCF's own OpenMP OpenBLAS is not affected. Values to compare: 16, 20 and 24. Second variant: OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS=1, which removes the two extra pools entirely; numpy/scipy BLAS then runs single-threaded, and rounding changes because ddot and dsymv sums are no longer split. Code-level complement that does not depend on the environment (rounding-level): compute the per-block XC energy without BLAS ddot in _FusedXC.nr_rks/nr_uks and nr_rks/nr_uks (accumulate den*exc and sum once per call, or use numpy.einsum). Use lib.dot (PySCF's OpenMP BLAS) for the x^T F x and x C products in SCF._eigh, make_rdm1 and get_grad. Verification is one A/B run: run_bench.py A=pyscf:PYSCF_MAX_MEMORY=20000 B=pyscf:PYSCF_MAX_MEMORY=20000,OPENBLAS_THREAD_TIMEOUT=20 on scf_caffeine_svp_b3lyp, scf_caffeine+_svp_b3lyp_uks, scf_c20h42_svp_b3lyp, tda_caffeine_svp_b3lyp and hess_benzene_svp_b3lyp. If the diagnosis is right, get_overlap_cond falls to about 0.2 ms per call, eigh to at most ~6 ms per Fock diagonalization, and dot/_rho_kernel per call drop. Follow-up: re-test 20 OpenMP threads; the It3 20-thread runs had 38 spinners.
findings.expected_gain: At least the small-call excess: ~1.0 s (10%) on caffeine/SVP SCFs, ~1.8 s (9%) on the caffeine+ UKS SCF, ~0.9 s (6%) on caffeine/TZVP DF-PBE, ~0.5 s (3%) on n-C20H42/SVP. If the SCF's XC kernels regain the scaling they show in TDA (7.7-8x instead of 5.05-5.5x), a further ~1-1.7 s on caffeine/SVP SCFs, so 15-25% in total. TDA/Hessian gain less: the small-call excess is ~0.25 s in tda_caffeine.
findings.exactness_notes: The timeout only changes how long idle workers spin before sleeping. Thread counts and work partitioning stay the same, so results are bit-identical. The OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS=1 variant and the code-level complement change rounding only.

findings.title: Each fused XC call computes the shell-pair overlap bound 3-5 times and the dm shell bounds twice, and only the last results are used
findings.evidence: nr_rks first calls ni._gen_rho_evaluator (dft/numint.py:1918). That goes through _rho_setup, which calls mol.get_overlap_cond() (3689) and condense_to_shell(dm,'absmax') per dm (3691). nr_rks then computes pair_mask = mol.get_overlap_cond() (1945). Then _fused_xc (1948) runs fused.nr_rks, whose rho_evaluator calls _rho_setup again (1117) and repeats both. The first make_rho and pair_mask are read only by the non-fused branches. nr_uks makes two _gen_rho_evaluator calls (2044-2045), computes pair_mask (2074), then the fused path runs two _rho_setup calls: 5 get_overlap_cond and 4 condense per call. nr_rks_fxc (2367/2388/2396) and nr_uks_fxc (2652/2677/2685) follow the same pattern. In the fused fxc dm path (TDA trial dms carry no mo_coeff), _rho_setup's dm_cond and pair_mask are computed per dm and never read: only rho1_rho2_ratio uses them, and only when mo_coeff is set. get_overlap_cond depends only on mol._atm/_bas/_env, yet it is recomputed every cycle. The profile counts match: scf_caffeine_svp_b3lyp has 51 get_overlap_cond calls (3 x 17 nr_rks calls) and 34 condense calls (2 x 17); caffeine+ UKS has 125 (5 x 25) and 100 (4 x 25); tda_caffeine has 320 condense calls (2 per trial dm).
findings.current_cost: Self time of get_overlap_cond + condense (profile-it13/summary.txt): scf_caffeine_svp_pbe 0.51 s (5.0% of 10.22 s); b3lyp 0.48 s (4.8%); r2scan 0.51 s (4.3%); camb3lyp 0.37 s (3.4%); tzvp_dfpbe 0.55 s (3.6%); caffeine+ UKS 1.02 s (4.8%); benzene+ UKS r2SCAN 0.30 s (7.3%); c20h42 SVP B3LYP 0.28 s (1.5%); r2SCAN 0.36 s (1.6%); tda_caffeine 0.25 s (1.0%); tddft_benzene 0.13 s (1.6%).
findings.proposal: In nr_rks, nr_uks, nr_rks_fxc, nr_uks_fxc and cache_xc_kernel1, call _fused_xc first, taking nset and nao from the dm shapes. Build _gen_rho_evaluator and pair_mask only when _fused_xc returns None. Store get_overlap_cond on the grids' _GridAOData, which already checks mol by content on every use, and pass it into _rho_setup. In _FusedXC.rho_evaluator, skip the dm_cond/pair_mask computation for dms without mo_coeff, since the dm path is taken regardless. Per call this cuts RKS from 3 get_overlap_cond + 2 condense to 0 + 1, UKS from 5 + 4 to 0 + 2, and fxc from 3 + 2·nset to 0 + 0.
findings.expected_gain: At today's per-call cost: scf_caffeine_svp_b3lyp 0.37 s (3.7%), pbe 0.40 s (3.9%), r2scan 0.39 s (3.3%), tzvp_dfpbe 0.42 s (2.8%), caffeine+ UKS 0.78 s (3.7%), benzene+ UKS r2SCAN 0.23 s (5.6%), c20h42 SVP 0.21-0.28 s (1.1-1.2%), tda_caffeine 0.25 s (1%), tddft_benzene 0.13 s (1.5%). This overlaps with scf-blas-spin: if that fix lands first, these calls cost about 0.1-0.2 ms each, and this change saves only ~10-20 ms per SCF. Its value is that it does not depend on the environment.
findings.exactness_notes: The same ovlp_cond and dm_cond values feed the same rho1/rho2 decisions. Only unused or repeated computations are removed.

findings.title: Grids.build groups points with numpy.unique(axis=0) on structured rows; a scalar box key and one stable argsort give the identical permutation 14x faster
findings.evidence: dft/gen_grid.py:447-469 (arg_group_grids) calls numpy.unique(box_ids, axis=0, return_inverse=True). That views each (bx,by,bz) row as a void struct and sorts it with VOID_compare, which appears in native_grid_caffeine_svp.txt. The function then argsorts the inverse a second time. In profile-it13/summary.txt, '<method argsort of ndarray>' takes 0.171-0.190 s in every caffeine SCF and 0.395-0.413 s in every n-C20H42 SCF; numpy runs it single-threaded. Measured at 1 thread (scratchpad/swarm/scf/grid_build.py): arg_group_grids takes 0.173 s on caffeine/SVP (294,796 points) and 0.430 s on n-C20H42 (694,296 points). The replacement key = ((bx+1)*(ny+2) + (by+1))*(nz+2) + (bz+1), followed by key.argsort(kind='stable'), takes 0.012 s and 0.032 s, and numpy.array_equal(old_idx, new_idx) is True on both molecules.
findings.current_cost: 0.17-0.19 s per caffeine SCF: 1.7% of scf_caffeine_svp_b3lyp (10.03 s), 1.1% of tzvp_dfpbe, 0.8% of the caffeine+ UKS SCF. 0.40-0.41 s per n-C20H42 SCF: 2.1% of SVP B3LYP, 1.8% of r2SCAN, 0.26% of TZVP PBE. ~0.1 s (2.5%) for benzene+ UKS. Paid on every grids.build.
findings.proposal: Replace gen_grid.py:467-469 with the key argsort. Components lie in [-1, boxes], so the lexicographic order of rows equals the order of the key. A stable argsort of the unique-row rank equals a stable argsort of any strictly increasing function of the row, so the permutation is the same; verified on both molecules.
findings.expected_gain: 0.16 s per caffeine-size grid build (1.6% of a caffeine/SVP SCF) and 0.40 s per n-C20H42 grid build (2.1% of the SVP B3LYP SCF). Independent of the threading fixes, because the sort is single-threaded.
findings.exactness_notes: Identical permutation, hence identical coords, weights, non0tab and all downstream results.

findings.title: The Becke-partition kernel VXCgen_grid is 2-wide SSE2; AVX2/AVX-512 builds without FP contraction, with the weight normalization moved into C, are bitwise identical and 1.8-2.7x faster
findings.evidence: lib/dft/grid_basis.c:32-104 is compiled with '-Wall -msse3 -O2' (lib/build/build.ninja), and objdump shows mulpd/subpd, i.e. 2-wide SSE2. The pair loop is O(natm^2·ngrids): in native_scf_c20h42_svp_b3lyp.txt, VXCgen_grid self time is 2.0% (1.85 s of 92.66 s at 1 thread). At 10 threads (summary.txt), gen_grid_partition takes 0.371 s (alkane SVP B3LYP), 0.386 s (r2SCAN), 0.345 s (TZVP PBE) and 0.10-0.12 s on caffeine. In addition, gen_grid.py:409-410 writes pbecke[natm, ngrid_atom] and then reads it back for pbecke.sum(axis=0). I timed a verbatim copy of the kernel at 1 thread (scratchpad/swarm/scf/becke.c, becke_check.py), over all atoms' grids, comparing results with numpy.array_equal against libdft through get_partition. Caffeine: 0.125 s (SSE3), 0.076 s (AVX2), 0.071 s (AVX-512 with -ffp-contract=off); with the weights computed in C, 0.065 s (AVX2) and 0.049 s (AVX-512). n-C20H42: 1.916 s (SSE3), 1.126 s (AVX2), 1.041 s (AVX-512); with the weights in C, 1.053 s and 0.790 s. All of these are bitwise identical. An AVX-512 build that allowed FMA contraction was not, which is why the variants must be built without FMA.
findings.current_cost: 0.37-0.39 s per n-C20H42 SCF at 10 threads (2.0% of SVP B3LYP, 1.7% of r2SCAN, 0.2% of TZVP) and 0.10-0.12 s per caffeine SCF (1.0-1.2%). Grows as natm^3: about 4x the alkane's cost for 100 atoms.
findings.proposal: Add runtime-dispatched AVX2 and AVX-512 copies of the pair loop, as It7 did for nr_direct_batch.c. Use a target attribute without 'fma', or -ffp-contract=off for that file. Add a VXCgen_grid variant that returns the atom's weights vol·P_ia·(1/ΣP) directly, summing rows 0..natm-1 in the same order as numpy's sum(axis=0). get_partition then no longer allocates natm×ngrid_atom arrays or calls pbecke.sum(axis=0). Fuse the g, radii-adjustment and switching-function loops; each element sees the same operations in the same order.
findings.expected_gain: About 2.4x on the partition: ~0.2 s per n-C20H42 SCF (1.1%), ~0.05-0.07 s per caffeine SCF (0.6%), ~0.8 s for a 100-atom molecule.
findings.exactness_notes: The IEEE operations are lane-independent and unchanged. FMA contraction must stay off (verified: the contracted build differs).

findings.title: SCF._eigh uses scipy's default MRRR eigensolver (dsyevr); divide and conquer (driver='evd') is 2.0-2.3x faster on Fock matrices of these sizes
workloads: all scf_* cases (one Fock diagonalization per cycle, two for UKS)
largest share on scf_caffeine_tzvp_dfpbe and n-C20H42 TZVP
findings.evidence: scf/hf.py:1889 calls scipy.linalg.eigh(h, overwrite_a=True) with the default 'evr' driver; also hf.py:1364 (check_linear_dependency) and 1389. 1-thread timings on Fock-like matrices, hcore+0.1·dm transformed by x_orth (scratchpad/swarm/scf/percycle.py): n=246, 5.9 ms to 2.6 ms; caffeine/TZVP n=494, 29.6 to 13.7 ms; C20H42/SVP n=490, 30.4 to 15.0 ms. On random symmetric matrices (eigh_chk.py): n=872, 98 to 75 ms; n=1200, 236 to 179 ms; eigenvalue differences ≤1.4e-13. Profile linalg time: 0.34-0.45 s on caffeine/SVP, 0.83 s on DF-TZVP, 0.49 s on alkane SVP, 1.42 s on alkane TZVP (about 129 ms per Fock diagonalization, n=872). SCF checks at 1 thread (evd_scf.py, evd_uks.py) on benzene B3LYP and r2SCAN, water B3LYP, and benzene+ UKS r2SCAN (the benchmark case): same cycle counts at the default conv_tol, |ΔE| ≤ 6.3e-13, max |ΔD| ≤ 2.2e-11. At tight settings ≤ 1.7e-12 Eh, with cycles 9 vs 10 and 11 vs 10, within the known tight-endpoint jitter. benzene+ UKS PBE (degenerate, partly occupied HOMO) does change path, from 21 to 22 cycles, unconverged in both runs. That case is chaotic under any rounding change: a 1e-15 relative perturbation of the initial guess alone gives 29 cycles.
findings.current_cost: Rate of the Fock diagonalization at 1 thread with evr: ~5.9 ms per cycle on caffeine/SVP; ~30 ms per cycle on caffeine/TZVP and C20H42/SVP; ~100+ ms per cycle on C20H42/TZVP. In the profile this is part of linalg: 0.41 s of 10.03 s (b3lyp), 0.82 s of 14.96 s (DF-TZVP), 1.42 s of 159 s (alkane TZVP); today those times also carry the contention described in scf-blas-spin.
findings.proposal: Use driver='evd' in SCF._eigh (hf.py:1889), in eig for x=None (hf.py:1389), and in check_linear_dependency (hf.py:1364). Combine with scf-blas-spin so the solver runs without competing spinners.
findings.expected_gain: Per SCF at 1-thread rates: 0.05 s on caffeine/SVP (0.5%), 0.27 s on caffeine/TZVP DF-PBE (1.8%), 0.17 s on C20H42/SVP (0.9%), 0.16 s on the caffeine+ UKS SCF (0.8%), 0.3-0.5 s on C20H42/TZVP (0.2-0.3%).
findings.exactness_notes: A different LAPACK algorithm gives eigenvectors that differ at rounding level. Within degenerate subspaces they differ by an arbitrary rotation, which leaves the density unchanged for closed-shell systems. SCF paths that are chaotic under any rounding change (benzene+ UKS PBE) can still change their cycle count.

ruled_out:
All timings below are 1-thread, on caffeine/SVP, caffeine/TZVP and n-C20H42/SVP. Scripts are in /tmp/claude-1000/-home-danny-Chemistry-my-pyscf/3d2aa02f-ca12-40eb-b5fd-b099754f302d/scratchpad/swarm/scf/.

Small enough to ignore:
- Chkfile writes: mf.dump_chk takes 0.47-0.52 ms per cycle and chkfile.save_mol 0.4-0.5 ms once. Users' default chkfile costs nothing measurable; the benchmarks set chkfile=None anyway.
- mol.build: 1.1-2.2 ms.
- Once-per-SCF setup:
  - get_ovlp 0.8-2.3 ms;
  - get_hcore 11, 37 and 69 ms;
  - minao guess 30, 57 and 89 ms, of which re.split on the ANO basis file is 17-27 ms for 4 elements (could be cached, but that is about 0.2%);
  - check_linear_dependency 4-22 ms.
  The ints1e category is 0.02-0.07 s in every SCF profile.
- Per-cycle driver work: make_rdm1 0.1-0.7 ms, get_grad 0.2-1.4 ms, energy einsum ≤0.08 ms, CDIIS update 2.3-17 ms (4 lib.dot GEMMs). Precomputing (S·X)^T would save 1 of the 4 GEMMs (≤0.2 s per SCF, rounding-level), which is not worth it.
- _GridAOData.matches (array_equal on coords and mol arrays per XC call) costs 0.025-0.05 s per SCF. _sparse_enough over block suffixes costs ≤0.009 s.

Excluded by the policy:
- Skipping the conv_check extra cycle, or using a better initial guess: changes the result or the cycle count.
- Screening in-core ERIs below the Schwarz bound (37% of caffeine/SVP's s8 tensor): an approximation.
- Becke weights: Stratmann or screened partitions are approximations. Exact skipping of pairs whose products are already zero needs mu ≥ ~0.993, which occurs only for the innermost radial shells, so it is not worth it.

Left to other areas:
- The in-core ERI build getints4c (0.87-0.99 s per caffeine/SVP SCF) is qcint and J/K. Its fill overhead outside qcint is about 2% at 1 thread.
- Semi-direct setup (_vhf.py SemiDirectERI.__init__ 0.085-1.2 s, semi_direct_eri 0.19-0.78 s) belongs to It9's J/K.
- build_radial (0.04-0.14 s) and nr_rks's Python loop (~0.1 s per SCF) are XC.
- Hessian 1e-derivative calls (get_hcore 300 calls, 0.25 s, plus getints2c 0.22 s in hess_caffeine, 0.3%) and TD einsum transforms are other areas.

Other checks:
- The SCF eigensolver already uses the canonical orthogonalizer x_orth plus a standard eigh, so there is no per-cycle Cholesky of S to precompute.
- Changing the GOMP wait policy (OMP_WAIT_POLICY=passive) would add futex wakeups at every region and barrier in PySCF's kernels; not recommended.
- The evd A/B showed benzene+ UKS PBE is chaotic under any rounding (21 vs 29 cycles from a 1e-15 change to the initial guess). Rounding-level changes elsewhere can move that case too.

Cannot be measured here:
- The scf-blas-spin diagnosis is inferred from code, from 1-thread vs 10-thread per-call costs, from the It3 thread-sweep pattern, and from the SCF vs TDA/Hessian scaling of the XC kernels. Multi-threaded runs were not allowed, so the size of the large-kernel part needs the one A/B run described in that finding.

verdicts.checked: Code: numpy.libs/libscipy_openblas64_ reports 'OpenBLAS 0.3.34.106.0 USE64BITINT DYNAMIC_ARCH NO_AFFINITY' and scipy.libs/libscipy_openblas reports '0.3.31.dev DYNAMIC_ARCH NO_AFFINITY'. Neither has USE_OPENMP, both carry the 'Detect OpenMP Loop' warning, and both read OPENBLAS_THREAD_TIMEOUT. OpenBLAS sources: common.h:393-397 x86_64 YIELDING is 8 nops (commit 07b1c0bc1 'Stop using sched_yield on non-Windows x86_64'); blas_server.c:160-164 sets THREAD_TIMEOUT 28 and :424 the spin-then-cond_wait; the env value is clamped to [4,30] (:572-576); init.c:835-838 gives OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS > GOTO > OMP_NUM_THREADS; ddot.c:174 threads for n>10000; symv.c threads for n>=200. dft/numint.py _FusedXC.nr_rks/nr_uks (1312, 1339-40) and nr_rks (1940) do excsum += numpy.dot(den, exc) per block. Blocks are ~59k points (85 dot calls / 17 nr_rks = 5 blocks), so ddot runs threaded. hf.py _eigh uses ndarray.dot (numpy's pool) and scipy eigh (scipy's pool). bench/common.py worker_env drops OPENBLAS_*. NOTES never tried OPENBLAS_THREAD_TIMEOUT or OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS; It3 only noted 'eigh 0.4 -> 3.0 s from thread-pool contention' at 20 threads. Profile numbers recomputed from summary.txt, all matching: get_overlap_cond 0.261/51 = 5.1 ms, condense 0.218/34 = 6.4 ms, eigh 0.411/32, _dgemm 0.099/57 = 1.7 ms, unpack_tril 0.038/17 = 2.2 ms. My own 1-thread runs: get_overlap_cond 0.13 ms, condense 0.05 ms on caffeine. It3 per-call ranges reproduced from the json: 8 threads 2.4-3.6 ms, 10 threads 3.3-5.7 ms, 20 threads 13-19 ms for get_overlap_cond. A 20-40x excess on 0.05-0.13 ms OpenMP regions, growing with the total thread count, points to scheduler preemption (time slices of several ms) under oversubscription, as the analyst says. Could not test multithreaded here.
verdicts.gain_estimate: Likely 0.5-1.0 s (5-10%) on caffeine/SVP SCFs, 1-1.8 s (5-9%) on the caffeine+ UKS SCF, ~0.5-0.9 s on DF-TZVP, ~0.3-0.5 s (2-3%) on the n-C20H42 SCFs. The 'at least ~1.0 s' is not a hard lower bound. A 10-thread OpenMP region on mixed Zen5/Zen5c cores with futex wakeups costs more than the 1-thread time, and TDA still shows 0.7-0.9 ms per small call. The extra 1-1.7 s from the XC kernels is speculative: VXCfused_dot_wv uses schedule(static,1) on 4 fast + 6 slow cores (an ideal near 6.5x), and the TDA comparison has different per-call work, so the 5.05x vs 7.5x scaling gap is confounded. Needs the proposed A/B.
verdicts.cost_seconds: Excess of small OpenMP and BLAS calls over their 1-thread cost, scf_caffeine_svp_b3lyp: ~1.0 s of 10.03 s (eigh ~0.32, get_overlap_cond 0.25, condense 0.22, partition ~0.1, _dgemm ~0.09, ndarray.dot ~0.05, unpack_tril 0.04). Caffeine+ UKS ~1.8 s of 21.16 s; n-C20H42 SVP ~0.5 s of 18.77 s.
verdicts.comment: The mechanism is verified in code and fits all the profile evidence. The fix (OPENBLAS_THREAD_TIMEOUT=20 in pyscf-env.sh and bench worker_env) is bitwise exact: thread counts and partitioning stay fixed, and only how long idle workers spin changes. It is the cheapest high-value item here, but its size needs the one A/B run. Note that the GOMP threads also spin while the main thread runs numpy/scipy BLAS, so not all contention goes away. Do not set OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS=1 as the default: it changes rounding and makes large numpy GEMMs in user and post-SCF code single-threaded. Of the code-level complements, lib.dot in _eigh/make_rdm1 and a non-BLAS per-block exc sum only change rounding and are fine.

verdicts.checked: Read numint.py: nr_rks calls ni._gen_rho_evaluator -> _rho_setup (3663-3712: get_overlap_cond plus condense_to_shell per dm), then pair_mask = mol.get_overlap_cond() (1945), then _fused_xc (1459) -> _FusedXC.nr_rks -> rho_evaluator -> _rho_setup again (1117). _fused_xc uses neither make_rho nor pair_mask. In the fused path pair_mask from _rho_setup only feeds rho1_rho2_ratio, which is 0 when mo_occ is None, so dm_cond for dms without mo_coeff is wasted. Call counts match: 51 = 3x17 get_overlap_cond and 34 = 2x17 condense (b3lyp); 125 = 5x25 and 100 = 4x25 (caffeine+ UKS); 320 condense in TDA. Costs recomputed, all matching: pbe 0.277+0.237 = 0.514 s, b3lyp 0.479 s, UKS 1.019 s, benzene+ 0.301 s (7.4%), c20h42 0.276 s, TDA 0.252 s. My 1-thread runs: get_overlap_cond 0.13 ms (caffeine), 0.56 ms (alkane); condense 0.05 and 0.16 ms. _GridAOData.matches checks mol arrays by content, so caching ovlp_cond there is safe.
verdicts.gain_estimate: At today's contended per-call cost: 0.37 s (3.7%) on caffeine/SVP B3LYP, 0.78 s (3.7%) on caffeine+ UKS, 0.23 s (5.6%) on benzene+ UKS, ~0.2 s (1.1%) on the alkane, 0.25 s (1%) on caffeine TDA. Some of each removed region's preemption delay may move to the next OpenMP region, so 60-100% of that is realistic. After scf-blas-spin it drops to ~0.01-0.03 s per SCF (<0.3%), so the gains do not add.
verdicts.cost_seconds: get_overlap_cond+condense self time: 0.48-0.51 s (caffeine/SVP RKS), 1.02 s (caffeine+ UKS), 0.30 s (benzene+ UKS), 0.28-0.36 s (alkane SVP), 0.25 s (caffeine TDA).
verdicts.comment: The facts and the bitwise exactness hold. The value depends on scf-blas-spin: do that A/B first. If the timeout fixes the contention, this is a negligible cleanup (still worth it as a small, safe tidy-up of redundant work, e.g. upstream). If it does not, this is a 3-6% item.

verdicts.checked: gen_grid.py:447-469 (same code in pyscf-base) uses numpy.unique(box_ids, axis=0, return_inverse=True), which sorts a structured view; VOID_compare appears in native_grid_caffeine_svp.txt. That is followed by an argsort(kind='stable') of the inverse. My own 1-thread run (scratchpad/swarm/scf_verify/v1.py): caffeine/SVP 294,796 points 0.180 s -> 0.013 s; caffeine at grid level 5 (833,636 points) 0.565 -> 0.039 s; n-C20H42/SVP 694,296 points 0.462 -> 0.032 s. numpy.array_equal of the two permutations is True in all cases, including coords randomly displaced by sigma = 3 bohr (many points clipped at the -1/boxes edges). The argument holds: components lie in [-1, boxes], the key is strictly increasing in lexicographic row order, and the stable argsort of a strictly increasing function of the row equals the stable argsort of the unique rank. Profile: argsort 0.171-0.190 s in caffeine SCFs and 0.395-0.413 s in the alkane SCFs, single-threaded and not affected by contention. NOTES has nothing on it.
verdicts.gain_estimate: ~0.17 s per caffeine-sized grid build (1.5-1.7% of the caffeine/SVP SCFs, 1.1% of DF-TZVP), ~0.43 s per n-C20H42 build (2.3% of SVP B3LYP, 1.9% of SVP r2SCAN, 0.3% of TZVP PBE), ~0.06-0.1 s (1.5-2.5%) on benzene+ UKS. Independent of the threading fixes.
verdicts.cost_seconds: 0.17-0.18 s per caffeine SCF, 0.43-0.46 s per n-C20H42 SCF (1-thread arg_group_grids; the profile argsort shows 0.17-0.19 and 0.40-0.41 s)
verdicts.comment: A 3-line, bitwise-identical change that reaches ~2% on the alkane SVP SCF and pays on every grids.build, including user scripts and other grid levels (it scales with ngrids log ngrids). A good upstream PR candidate.

verdicts.checked: grid_basis.c:32-104 VXCgen_grid: pair loop O(natm^2*ngrids), schedule(static), built with the stock '-msse3 -O2' (NOTES Gotchas: 'PySCF stock: -msse3 -O2 -g'; It3 rejected a global -march=native because J/K got slower, not this per-file dispatch). gen_grid.py:376-410 allocates pbecke[natm,ngrid] per atom and sums it on axis 0. Profile recomputed: native_scf_c20h42 VXCgen_grid 2.0% of 92.66 s = 1.85 s at 1 thread; gen_grid_partition at 10 threads 0.371 s (alkane SVP B3LYP, 2.0% of 18.77), 0.386 s (r2SCAN, 1.7%), 0.345 s (TZVP, 0.2%), 0.10-0.12 s (caffeine, ~1.1%). The bitwise result of a non-FMA AVX2/AVX-512 build is plausible (sqrt and divide are correctly rounded, the operations are lane-independent), and the analyst checked it with array_equal.
verdicts.gain_estimate: ~2.4x on the partition: ~0.2 s per n-C20H42 SCF (1.1-1.2%), ~0.06 s per caffeine SCF (0.6%), ~0.03% on alkane TZVP. Below 2% on every target workload.
verdicts.cost_seconds: 0.37-0.39 s per n-C20H42 SCF and 0.10-0.12 s per caffeine SCF at 10 threads
verdicts.comment: Exact and real, but the saving is ~1% at most on the benchmark workloads, and it needs M effort: runtime dispatch, a new C entry point, CMake flags. It grows as natm^3, but so does the rest of the SCF, so it stays ~1% for 100-atom molecules. Low priority; it could be revisited together with scf-grid-sort if grid builds become a larger share.

verdicts.checked: hf.py SCF._eigh calls scipy.linalg.eigh(h, overwrite_a=True) with the default evr driver; eig() and check_linear_dependency also call scipy eigh. My 1-thread runs on x^T h x matrices: n=246 evr 5.2 ms vs evd 3.0 ms; n=490 (C20H42/SVP) 31.9 vs 16.2 ms, in line with the analyst's numbers. Profile eigh counts: 32-34 calls per caffeine SCF, about half of them Fock diagonalizations; the other half are the DIIS B-matrix eigh in lib/diis.py:254. Nothing on evd in NOTES. The change is rounding-level; it can move degenerate or chaotic SCF paths, and the policy requires identical cycle counts.
verdicts.gain_estimate: ~0.035 s (0.35%) on caffeine/SVP, ~0.27 s (~1.8%) on caffeine/TZVP DF-PBE, ~0.16 s (0.8%) on n-C20H42/SVP, ~0.3 s (0.2%) on alkane TZVP, at 1-thread rates. Under 10-thread contention the absolute times are larger, but how evd behaves under threading is unmeasured.
verdicts.cost_seconds: Fock eigh at 1 thread: ~5 ms/cycle (caffeine/SVP), ~30 ms/cycle (n~490), ~100 ms/cycle (n=872). Profile linalg 0.34-0.83 s per caffeine SCF, inflated by contention.
verdicts.comment: The speedup is real, but the SCF saving is below 2% on every workload (DF-TZVP is the closest at ~1.8%). It also adds a small risk of cycle-count changes in near-degenerate cases, which the policy forbids, so the benchmark cases would all need cycle-count checks. Not worth it on its own; at most a one-line add-on to test in the same A/B as scf-blas-spin for TZVP-size systems.

title: Libraries, build flags and runtime configuration

findings.title: Compile libdft and libcgto's grid files with -O3 -march=x86-64-v3 -ffp-contract=off (bitwise-identical): 1.09-1.20x on fused XC calls at 1 thread
findings.evidence:

findings.title: LIBXC_eval_xc gets ~1-1.9x from 10 threads in the fused SCF: one parallel region with dynamic point chunks (bitwise exact)
findings.evidence:
libxc per full-grid nr_rks on caffeine/SVP (294,800 points, MO dm), 1 thread, my measurement (cProfile tottime of libxc.py:1077 _eval_xc; /tmp/claude-1000/-home-danny-Chemistry-my-pyscf/3d2aa02f-ca12-40eb-b5fd-b099754f302d/scratchpad/swarm/sys/nrrks_1t.py): B3LYP 45 ms, PBE 50 ms, r2SCAN 123 ms (151-417 ns/pt).

The same at 10 threads in profile-it13/summary.txt (_eval_xc tottime / number of nr_rks calls):
- B3LYP: 0.672/17 = 39.5 ms, 1.14x over 1 thread
- PBE: 0.879/18 = 48.8 ms, 1.02x
- r2SCAN: 1.050/16 = 65.6 ms, 1.87x

On identical inputs at 1 thread, libxc inside nr_rks equals standalone (ratio 1.03 PBE, 1.04 B3LYP; libxc_context.py), so the loss is parallel, not per-thread.

It11 A/B (results/20261029-091520_it11-medium.json, same 90 calls), libxc unfused vs fused:
- PBE: 0.235-0.241 vs 0.78-0.79 s
- r2SCAN: 0.43-0.46 vs 0.98-1.01 s
- UKS B3LYP: 0.87-0.89 vs 1.66-1.76 s
The fused path tripled the libxc time.

Code, pyscf/lib/dft/libxc_itrf.c:968-1029:
- static equal split (blksize = np/nthreads, :983)
- 2 + 2*nfn fork/join regions per call: rho copy, then per functional the eval and merge_xc's parallel for (:874/:931); 6 barriers for PBE
- serial first merge loop
- per-call malloc of np*outlen

With equal-speed cores the static split is balanced: per-range cost max/mean 1.02-1.05 measured on real blocks (libxc_split.py). So the loss comes from slow or late threads: Zen 5c is 1.37x slower per core (measured), and any delayed thread stalls each barrier.
findings.current_cost:
libxc category (profile-it13/summary.txt):
- scf_caffeine_svp_pbe: 0.88 s (8.6%)
- b3lyp: 0.67 (6.7%)
- r2scan: 1.05 (9.0%)
- camb3lyp: 0.60 (5.6%)
- caffeine+ UKS B3LYP: 1.52 (7.2%)
- benzene+ UKS r2SCAN: 1.08 of 4.09 s (26%)
- DF-PBE TZVP: 0.51 (3.4%)
- c20h42 B3LYP: 0.49 (2.6%)
- c20h42 r2SCAN: 1.10 (4.8%)
- grid: 0.15 (4%)
findings.proposal:
Rewrite LIBXC_eval_xc as one omp parallel region with #pragma omp for schedule(dynamic,1) over chunks of 1024-2048 points. Each thread keeps private chunk buffers: the rho copy (_eval_rho on the chunk) and ebuf[outlen*chunk].

Per chunk, evaluate the functionals in order i = 0..nfn-1 and merge each into the output chunk with fac[i], with output strides np and chunk strides n. This removes the serial merge loop, the per-call np*outlen malloc and 5 of the 6 barriers, and it balances Zen 5 against Zen 5c and late-starting threads.
findings.expected_gain:
At ~6x over 1 thread, libxc per nr_rks falls to ~8-20 ms:
- caffeine/SVP PBE SCF: -0.7 s (7%)
- B3LYP: -0.5 s (5%)
- r2SCAN: -0.7 s (6%)
- UKS B3LYP: about -1.2 s (5.5%)
- benzene+ UKS r2SCAN: about -0.85 s (20%)
- alkane r2SCAN: -0.5 s (2.3%); alkane B3LYP: -0.3 s
- DF-PBE TZVP: -0.35 s (2.4%)

Partly overlaps sys-blas-pools: if that config removes most of the interference, this keeps roughly the heterogeneity and barrier share (15-30% of libxc time).
findings.exactness_notes: libxc evaluation is pointwise. The per-point output keeps the same order of functional contributions (zeroed output, += fac[i]*e_i for i in order), so the output is bitwise identical however points are chunked or scheduled.

findings.title: numpy/scipy bundled OpenBLAS pools (9 threads each) busy-spin 134 ms after every threaded call and compete with libgomp; set OPENBLAS_THREAD_TIMEOUT=4 (or OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS=1)
findings.evidence:
Both bundled libraries are pthread builds sized by OMP_NUM_THREADS=10 (openblas_get_config):
- numpy.libs/libscipy_openblas64_ is OpenBLAS 0.3.34.106
- scipy.libs/libscipy_openblas is 0.3.31.dev

The harness drops OPENBLAS_* (bench/common.py:46) and sets only OMP_NUM_THREADS (:50); scripts/pyscf-env.sh sets no OPENBLAS_*. So no benchmark ever changed these pools.

Disassembly of both blas_thread_server idle loops: rdtsc + 8 nop, with no sched_yield, until 2^28 TSC ticks (THREAD_TIMEOUT 28; TSC 2.0 GHz from bogomips 3992), i.e. 134 ms. Both .so read OPENBLAS_THREAD_TIMEOUT and OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS (strings).

Triggers:
- numpy.dot(den, exc) runs once per XC block (pyscf/dft/numint.py:1312, 1339-1340, 1940, 2069-2070) with n up to 67,200, above the 10,000 threading threshold (OpenBLAS kernel/x86_64/ddot.c:174). It costs 8.4-9.5 us single-threaded (measured) and wakes 9 spinners about every 60 ms during the XC phase.
- scipy eigh (scf/hf.py:1384) wakes scipy's 9 spinners every cycle, so up to 10 libgomp + 18 spinning threads share 20 hardware threads.

Measured symptoms:
- eigh(h, s) n=246: 12.8 ms/call in the 10-thread caffeine/SVP SCF (0.411 s/32) vs 4.7 ms single-threaded, so threading is 2.7x slower. n~490: 21.8-24.5 vs 26.2 ms.
- Kernels run 1.46-1.8x slower inside the SCF than isolated at 10 threads: in-core J+K 82 ms/call (1.392 s/17) vs 56 ms (It7 E); fused nr_rks 0.351-0.374 s/call vs about 0.20-0.24 s (It10 B and It11 tables). The isolated runs had numpy's pool but no scipy eigh.
- It3: eigh 0.4 -> 3.0 s at 20 threads from pool contention.
findings.current_cost:
Directly measured: scipy eigh 0.34-0.45 s per caffeine/SVP SCF (linalg category), of which about 0.26 s is threading overhead.

Indirect: the 1.5-1.8x SCF-context penalty on the XC kernels (xc_kernels 5-7 s per caffeine SCF) and on in-core J/K (1.0-1.4 s), if spinners cause it.
findings.proposal:
Add OPENBLAS_THREAD_TIMEOUT=4 to scripts/pyscf-env.sh and to the bench configs, e.g. N=pyscf:PYSCF_MAX_MEMORY=20000,OPENBLAS_THREAD_TIMEOUT=4. The bundled pools then sleep 16 TSC ticks after each call. Our USE_OPENMP OpenBLAS has no pool and ignores OPENBLAS_* thread settings (NOTES Gotchas).

Also A/B OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS=1: no pools at all, eigh 12.8 -> 4.7 ms. It makes large numpy GEMMs in user scripts single-threaded, so prefer TIMEOUT as the default.

Code-level complement: replace numpy.dot(den, exc) at the lines above with a reduction that does not wake a BLAS pool, e.g. numpy.einsum('i,i->', den, exc) (rounding-level change).

Test on scf_caffeine_svp_*, tda_caffeine_svp_b3lyp, hess_benzene_svp_b3lyp and scf_benzene+_svp_r2scan_uks, comparing the xc_kernels, libxc, jk and linalg categories.
findings.expected_gain:
Measured part: about -0.26 s per caffeine/SVP SCF from eigh with NUM_THREADS=1 (2.6%).

Speculative part: if most of the 1.5-1.8x SCF-context penalty is spinner interference, XC-heavy SCF/TD runs could save 10-30% of wall time (e.g. caffeine B3LYP SCF 10.0 -> about 7.5-8.5 s).

Realistic expectation: 3-15%.
findings.exactness_notes: OPENBLAS_THREAD_TIMEOUT changes only how idle pool threads wait. The OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS=1 variant changes numpy's ddot/dgemm partial-sum order: rounding only, about 1e-15 relative in E_xc. The einsum replacement is also rounding-level.

findings.title: GEMM_NBLK 4 -> 2 halves the fused kernels' per-thread working set and is 3-5% faster at 1 thread
findings.evidence:
Measured AO counts per 224-point group (/tmp/claude-1000/-home-danny-Chemistry-my-pyscf/3d2aa02f-ca12-40eb-b5fd-b099754f302d/scratchpad/swarm/sys/libxc_split.py ns):
- benzene/SVP: mean 96
- caffeine/SVP: mean 154, p90 200, max 231
- caffeine/TZVP: mean 301, p90 396, max 439
- C20H42/SVP: mean 159, max 196

Per-thread hot working set per group (nr_numint_fused.c:286, 549):
- AO buffer 4*ns*224*8 B = 1.2 MB at ns=170 and 2.2 MB at ns=300 (GGA)
- plus opbuf, cbuf and the private nao^2 matrix: about 2.2-3.3 MB per thread
- L2 is 1 MB per core; the 6 Zen 5c cores share 8 MB of L3

Measured, 1 thread: libdft rebuilt in scratch with GEMM_NBLK=2 (nr_numint_gemm.h:29), interleaved, caffeine/SVP level-3 grid, MO dm (libdft/nblk_bench.py, nblk_bench2.py):
- nr_rks B3LYP: 0.834 -> 0.794 s (1.050x); repeated 0.849 -> 0.810 (1.049x)
- nr_rks r2SCAN: 1.497 -> 1.451 s (1.032x)
- nr_rks_fxc, 8 dms (level-1 grid): 1.954 -> 1.940 s (1.007x)
- GEMM_NBLK=1: nr_rks 1.061x, but fxc 0.925x, so 2 is the sweet spot

Differences vs GEMM_NBLK=4: exc identical; Vxc max relative 5.6e-16 (B3LYP) and 6.6e-16 (r2SCAN).

It6's finding that group size 2/4/8 made no difference was for the unfused gather kernels, which read AO values from memory.
findings.current_cost:
Fused kernels (dot + _rho_kernel, plus rho_lowrank + dot_ao_mo) at 10 threads (profile-it13/summary.txt):
- caffeine/SVP SCFs: 5.2-7.0 s
- DF-PBE TZVP: 10.9 s
- caffeine TZVP B3LYP: 9.6 s
- caffeine TDA: 18.0 s
- alkane PBE TDA: 25.1 s
- caffeine Hessian CPHF: 36.2 s
findings.proposal: Change #define GEMM_NBLK from 4 to 2 in pyscf/lib/dft/nr_numint_gemm.h:29. The blkmask bits and group code are generic. Rebuild, run kernels.py and validate.py FULL+SPARSE, then A/B at 10 threads. The gain there may exceed the 1-thread 3-5%, because the per-thread AO buffer drops to about 0.6 MB (fits L2) and the Zen 5c CCX L3 stops overflowing (6 x ~1.1 MB instead of 6 x ~2.2 MB in 8 MB).
findings.expected_gain: Measured at 1 thread: 3-5% of nr_rks-type kernel time and about 1% on multi-dm fxc. At 10 threads (unmeasured), at least: caffeine SCF -0.15 to 0.3 s (2-3%), DF-PBE TZVP -0.4 s, alkane SCFs -0.3 to 0.6 s. Plausibly 2-3x that if L3 pressure is part of the poor 10-thread scaling (see sys-xc-scaling).
findings.exactness_notes: Group boundaries change which grid points share a GEMM. The XC matrix is summed in a different association: measured 5.6-6.6e-16 relative in Vxc, energies identical at printed precision.

findings.title: Equal static partitions on 4 Zen 5 + 6 Zen 5c cores idle the fast cores; balance them deterministically (NPdgemm chunks, XC-matrix accumulator slots)
findings.evidence:
Per-core throughput measured with /tmp/claude-1000/-home-danny-Chemistry-my-pyscf/3d2aa02f-ca12-40eb-b5fd-b099754f302d/scratchpad/swarm/sys/gemmbench.c (out_core*.txt; FMA peak 73.8 vs 53.0 GFLOP/s): Zen 5c (CPU 12) is 1.36-1.40x slower than Zen 5 (CPU 3) on every fused-kernel dgemm and dsyrk shape (NT 224 x ns x ns, TN ns x ns x 224/448, NT 224 x nocc x ns, NPdgemm chunk). Under load the profile-it13 clocks are Zen 5 4.38-4.55 GHz and Zen 5c 3.24-3.30 GHz.

An equal static partition finishes at the Zen 5c pace. That loses up to 1 - 10/(4*1.38+6) = 13% of the region.

Static loops on hot paths:
- VXCfused_dot_wv nr_numint_fused.c:562, dot_terms :824, dot_ao_mo :1097: schedule(static,1)
- NPdgemm equal m/n splits: np_helper/npdot.c:112, :130
- the libxc split (sys-libxc-dynamic)

Comparing profile-it13 with my 1-thread runs (caffeine/SVP): the dynamic(4) rho kernel scales 2.60-2.78x while the static(1) dot kernel scales 2.37-2.41x (PBE and B3LYP).

It6 measured dynamic 7% faster than static round-robin on the XC-matrix kernel.
findings.current_cost:
VXCfused_dot_wv tottime at 10 threads (profile-it13/summary.txt):
- caffeine SCF: 2.66 (B3LYP), 2.88 (PBE), 4.78 (r2SCAN)
- DF-PBE TZVP: 6.92; TZVP B3LYP: 6.29
- UKS: 5.30

findings.proposal:
(a) NPdgemm (m- or n-split branch): split into fixed chunks (at least 4*nthreads, aligned to 64 rows) under schedule(dynamic,1). Each output element is still produced by one dgemm on a chunk that does not depend on the thread, so the result does not depend on the schedule.

(b) Private-matrix XC kernels: a deterministic slot schedule.
- Groups go to S = 4*nthreads fixed slots (igroup % S); each slot accumulates in its own private matrix in group order.
- Slots are taken with schedule(dynamic,1) and reduced in slot order with NPomp_dsum_reduce_inplace over S buffers.
- Results are reproducible and even independent of the thread count.
- Use it when S*nset*nao^2*8 B fits (SCF: caffeine 19 MB, alkane 77 MB); keep static(1) for large nset (TDA/CPHF), or there use weighted static round-robin (Zen 5 threads weight 1.38) with OMP_PLACES=cores OMP_PROC_BIND=close.

(b) changes the summation association of the XC matrix to rounding (about 1e-16 relative) but stays bitwise reproducible.

findings.title: Fused XC kernels scale only 2.4-3.1x on 10 threads (J/K: 6.3-7.8x); four exact A/B runs to find which fix recovers it
findings.evidence:

10 threads (profile-it13/summary.txt), per nr_rks:

- PBE: (2.879+2.832)/18 = 0.317 s, 2.48x
- r2SCAN: (4.779+2.215)/16 = 0.437 s, 3.13x
- libxc 1.0-1.9x (sys-libxc-dynamic)

Same profiles for comparison:

Candidate causes, each with a separate finding:
- pool spinners (sys-blas-pools)
- per-thread working set 2.2-3.3 MB vs 1 MB L2 and the 8 MB L3 of the 6-core Zen 5c CCX (sys-gemm-nblk)
- static partitions on heterogeneous cores (sys-sched-hetero)
- libxc barriers (sys-libxc-dynamic)
- SMT doubling or migration without binding: NOTES It7 tested binding only on dynamic-scheduled J/K

- (2) OMP_PLACES=cores OMP_PROC_BIND=close. Note the NOTES gotcha: pools created after libgomp init inherit the main thread's mask.
- (3) OPENBLAS_THREAD_TIMEOUT=4.

ruled_out:
All measurements were single-threaded on this machine. Scratch is under /tmp/claude-1000/-home-danny-Chemistry-my-pyscf/3d2aa02f-ca12-40eb-b5fd-b099754f302d/scratchpad/swarm/sys.

(1) OPENBLAS_CORETYPE=Haswell or Zen instead of Cooperlake (gemmbench.c, out_cpu2_*.txt, best of 2 interleaved, Zen 5 core). Faster by 3-7% on the main shapes: NT 224 x ns x ns, TN ns x ns x 224/448, zbuf NN, NPdgemm chunk, dsyrk n=100-160. Slower by 7-11% on dot_ao_mo TN nocc x ns x 448 and 2% on some rho-MO shapes. 1.6x slower on the low-rank benzene shape 224 x 21 x 100, which takes Cooperlake's small-matrix kernel (permit MNK <= 1e6). Net: no global switch worth making.

(2) Another BLAS (BLIS/AOCL; not installed, only system OpenBLAS, jemalloc and mimalloc are). Cooperlake OpenBLAS already reaches 76-83% of the measured FMA peak on the hot NT/TN shapes (dsyrk 57-72%), so the ceiling is about 1.2x on the BLAS share. Not verified.

(3) Batching the dms of a group into one GEMM so the shared AO operand is packed once (batchbench.c): 0.98-1.06x. Packing is cheap here.

(4) PGO or -O3 for the libcvhf semi-direct read kernels. I tested a verbatim copy of _batch_j/_batch_k_body_s with function-pointer dispatch on an n-C20H42/SVP-like stream of 83.6M stored quartets (pgo/drv.c, kernels.h). -O2 runs at 53.5 ns/quartet, matching It9's ~54 ns. -O3 runs at 77 ns (-42%) and default PGO at 76 ns (-42%): they vectorize and unroll the 1-5-trip loops. PGO with vectorization off gives 53-54 ns (no change). This also explains It3's J/K regression under -march=native -ftree-vectorize. Keep libcvhf at -O2; shape-specialized kernels remain the route there (J/K area).

(5) SMT and 20 threads: It3 measured 0.67-0.80x, and grad-threads showed no gain with qcint.

(6) Memory allocation and THP. Per-call C buffers are 1.5-3.3 MB per thread (aobuf) plus nset*nao^2*8 B (vpriv). glibc reuses them from per-thread arenas after the first call. numpy already madvises arrays of 4 MB and up under THP 'madvise' mode. It7 measured MADV_HUGEPAGE on the private sums: 5% on the alkane, 0 on caffeine. vpriv calloc plus reduction is about 2 ms of a 187 ms TDA dot call. jemalloc or mimalloc would not change the page-fault and zeroing cost that dominates large allocations. Only the 186-dm alkane fxc case (6 of 44 s in private matrices, It13) might gain from glibc.malloc.hugetlb=1. Not measured.

(7) libxc -march build. libxc is ISO C99 with contraction off, so it would be bitwise neutral. Single-thread libxc is only 5-8% of nr_rks (45/50/123 ms of 0.84/0.84/1.50 s) and is bound by scalar maple code and libm. Its real problem is parallel scaling (sys-libxc-dynamic). A single-threaded libxc build exceeds the 2-minute limit, so this was not measured.

(8) Static-split imbalance in libxc with equal-speed cores: max/mean 1.02-1.05, small.

(9) In-core J/K static schedule: memory-bound and already scaling 6.3x.

(10) GEMM_NBLK=1: fxc 0.925x.

(11) LTO: It8 found none on qcint. The cross-library gain from compiling the GTO grid files with libdft is already in sys-cflags-libdft (variant C: +4-5% over B).

Profile note: libopenblasp-r0.3.34.so is not stripped (`file` says so). py-spy mis-symbolizes it because the .text segment sits 0x18000 above the first r-x segment. Shifting the reported symbol addresses by +0x18000 (checked against nm) gives:
- 'sgemm_small_kernel_b0_nn_COOPERLAKE' = dgemm_beta + dgemm_kernel_COOPERLAKE
- '..._b0_nt' = the rest of dgemm_kernel plus the d{in,it,on,ot}copy packing
- 'dtrmm_iltncopy/iltucopy' = dgemm_small_kernel_b0_nn/tt
- 'dtrmm_iunncopy' = about dsymm_iutcopy
- 'cblas_stpmv/stbsv' = dgemm_
- 'strsm_RTLU' = dgemm_nt/tn drivers, 'strsm_RTUN' = dgemm_nn

verdicts.checked: Flags confirmed: build.ninja has '-Wall -msse3 -O2 -g -DNDEBUG -std=gnu99 -fPIC -fopenmp' for every libdft object, and dft/CMakeLists.txt has no per-target options. objdump of the shipped libdft.so shows _contract_mo with only 2 mulsd and no packed multiplies, so the kernel is not vectorized. Micro-benchmark results in flags/res_*.txt: the -O3 x86-64-v3 nofma checksums equal the -O2 ones, and only the FMA build differs. I reran the analyst's swap_bench.py at 1 thread on CPU 2 (caffeine/SVP, level-1 grid). Variant C: nr_rks 0.293 -> 0.266 s (1.10x), nr_rks_fxc with 8 dms 1.918 -> 1.770 s (1.08x), dense eval_rho 1.01x, all bitwise equal to the shipped library. The analyst reported 1.14x and 1.11x. I also reran lowrank_bench.py (benzene rks_fxc_mo, 36 dms): 3.853 -> 3.181 s (1.21x), bitwise equal, which confirms 1.20x. Profile costs recomputed from summary.txt match the finding: xc_kernels 5.16/5.71/6.99 s for the caffeine SCFs, 18.05 s for caffeine TDA, and rho_lowrank+dot_ao_mo 36.2 s for the caffeine Hessian. NOTES It3 rejected -march=native for all of PySCF's C code (XC 20-35% faster, J/K 4-6% slower). Limiting the flags to libdft and the GTO grid files, with contraction off, is a new refinement, not a repeat of that experiment.

verdicts.checked:
Code: libxc_itrf.c:968-1029 is as described.
- Regions: a static equal split for the rho copy; per functional one region for _eval_xc and one parallel for per derivative order in merge_xc; then a free region. That is 6 regions for PBE at deriv 1.
- The first merge loop is serial, and ebuf (np*outlen) is malloc'd on every call.

Numbers: I reran nrrks_1t.py at 1 thread. _eval_xc took 45 ms (B3LYP) and 49 ms (PBE) per nr_rks, matching the analyst. In profile-it13, 0.672/17 = 39.5 ms and 0.879/18 = 48.8 ms per nr_rks, so libxc gets roughly 1.0-1.1x from 10 threads.

The proposed cause does not hold. In the It11 ABBA file (20261029-091520_it11-medium.json), the same LIBXC_eval_xc code with the same static split, on the same 90/85/80 calls, took:
- unfused U: PBE 0.235-0.241 s, B3LYP 0.188-0.191, r2SCAN 0.43-0.46
- fused F: 0.78-0.79, 0.50-0.58, 0.98-1.01
So libxc scales about 4x after the unfused kernels and about 1-1.4x after the fused ones. The static split and the Zen 5c speed gap are identical in both paths, and core heterogeneity can cost at most about 1.4x. The 3x loss therefore depends on what runs before libxc, not on how libxc's loops are scheduled. Possible causes include per-call malloc/free of the fused kernels' per-thread buffers (arena trimming, page faults, TLB shootdowns), late or sleeping workers, and BLAS pool spinners. None of these is identified yet.
verdicts.gain_estimate:
If libxc returned to its unfused-path cost (about 11-13 ms per nr_rks):
- caffeine/SVP SCFs: -0.45 to 0.6 s (4.5-5.5%)
- caffeine+ UKS B3LYP: about -1.0 s (5%)
- benzene+ UKS r2SCAN: about -0.6 to 0.8 s (15-20%)
- alkane SCFs: -0.3 to 0.5 s (2%)
The proposed rewrite is not shown to achieve this. If the cause is late or preempted threads, the dynamic single-region design captures most of it; if it is allocator or page-fault churn, it captures little. Expected value is perhaps half of the above.

- caffeine/SVP SCFs: 0.88 (PBE), 0.67 (B3LYP), 1.05 (r2SCAN), 0.60 (CAM-B3LYP)
- caffeine+ UKS: 1.52; benzene+ UKS r2SCAN: 1.08 of 4.09
- DF-PBE: 0.51; alkane B3LYP/r2SCAN: 0.49/1.10

verdicts.comment:
The symptom is real, and larger than the analyst says: the same libxc calls are 3x slower in the fused path than in the unfused path. The diagnosis is wrong, because the static split is identical in both paths and the unfused path scales about 4x. Before rewriting, run one 10-thread diagnostic:
- time LIBXC_eval_xc on a stored rho standalone, and right after a VXCfused_eval_rho_mo call
- then try OMP_WAIT_POLICY=active, MALLOC_TRIM_THRESHOLD_/MALLOC_MMAP_THRESHOLD_ (or MALLOC_ARENA_MAX), and OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS=1
The single-region dynamic rewrite is still bitwise exact and cheap (fewer barriers, no per-call np*outlen malloc), so it is worth doing. Do not expect it to deliver the full gain until the cause is known.

verdicts.checked:
Code and configuration facts all check out:
- bench/common.py:46 drops OPENBLAS_*, and :50 sets only OMP_NUM_THREADS; scripts/pyscf-env.sh sets no OPENBLAS_* variable.
- numpy.libs has OpenBLAS 0.3.34.106 and scipy.libs has 0.3.31.dev. Both are DYNAMIC_ARCH pthread builds that contain the strings OPENBLAS_THREAD_TIMEOUT and OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS. Neither imports sched_yield (only pthread_cond_wait), so the idle loop spins.
- numpy.dot(den, exc) is at numint.py:1312, 1339-1340, 1940 and 2069-2070.

The eigh part is confirmed. My 1-thread scipy.linalg.eigh(h, s) on CPU 2 takes 4.4 ms at n=246 and 23.6 ms at n=490. In the 10-thread profiles it takes 12.8 ms (B3LYP 0.411/32) and 12.6 ms (CAM-B3LYP 0.353/28, a run with no overlap). So about 0.25-0.27 s per caffeine/SVP SCF is threading overhead. There is no gain at n~490, and TDA and Hessian runs have almost no eigh (TDA linalg 0.02 s).

The speculative 1.5-1.8x 'SCF-context penalty' is mostly an artifact:
- From the file timestamps, the 10-thread profile-it13 run started at 18:09:28 while the 1-thread py-spy profile of scf_caffeine was still running (it ended at 18:09:59), so the PBE and B3LYP SCF profiles shared a core.
- In the clean It11 F runs, fused dot+_rho_kernel take 0.267 s per nr_rks (PBE), against about 0.24 s isolated (It10/It11). That is about 1.1x, not 1.5-1.8x.
- The in-core J/K comparison mixes sessions: It7 was measured partly at the 2 GHz clamp.
verdicts.gain_estimate: Measured: OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS=1, or limiting threads around scipy eigh, saves about 0.25-0.3 s per caffeine/SVP-sized SCF (2.5-3%), and about 2x that for UKS (two eighs per cycle). It saves about 0 for the alkane and TZVP SCFs and for post-SCF steps. Interference from the spinning pools on the libgomp kernels is unmeasured. Clean data leaves at most about 10% context penalty to explain, so 0-5% is a realistic range for XC-heavy SCFs, not 10-30%.
verdicts.cost_seconds: scipy eigh: 0.34-0.45 s per caffeine/SVP SCF, of which about 0.26 s is threading overhead. Spinner interference is unquantified; the clean-run upper bound is about 0.3 s per SCF.
verdicts.comment: Lead with OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS=1, or a code-level thread limit around eigh, because that is what the measurement supports. OPENBLAS_THREAD_TIMEOUT=4 does not remove eigh's threading overhead on small matrices and may add wake-up latency to it. Treat it as a secondary A/B. The einsum replacement for numpy.dot(den, exc) is fine and costs little. Rerun the A/B without any concurrent process: profile-it13's first SCF cases overlapped a native profiling run.

verdicts.checked:
Schedules confirmed:
- schedule(static,1) at nr_numint_fused.c:562 (VXCfused_dot_wv), :824 (dot_terms) and :1097 (dot_ao_mo)
- dynamic(4) in the rho kernels (:188, :295, :423, :927)

NOTES It6 measured dynamic 7% faster than static round-robin (17.3-17.6 vs 18.5-18.8 ms) and kept round-robin for reproducibility. Plain dynamic was rejected for that reason; the deterministic slot scheme is new.

Cost check of design (b), with S = 4*nthreads = 40 private matrices per VXCfused_dot_wv call. That call runs once per grid block, not once per SCF:

verdicts.comment: Part (a), the NPdgemm fixed chunks under dynamic, is cheap and reproducible: do it. In part (b), use fewer slots (for example 2*nthreads), or reuse the slot buffers across blocks of one call so they are zeroed and reduced once per nr_rks rather than per block, which overlaps with the 'private matrices' item in NOTES Next iterations. Weighted static round-robin depends on binding and on knowing which thread runs on which core type, which is fragile. Expect about 1-2% per workload. That is borderline against the 2% threshold, which is why this is adjusted rather than confirmed.

verdicts.comment:
The A/B plan is cheap and environment-only, so it is worth running. Corrections to the plan:
1. Run it on an otherwise idle machine. profile-it13's first cases and all native profiles had concurrent load.
2. Pin variant (1) to CPUs 0-7 (taskset), so that 4 threads really are the Zen 5 cores.
3. Add OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS=1, OMP_WAIT_POLICY=active, and a glibc malloc tuning variant (MALLOC_TRIM_THRESHOLD_/MALLOC_MMAP_THRESHOLD_ or MALLOC_ARENA_MAX). The It11 libxc data (the same calls 3x slower after the fused kernels than after the unfused ones) points to a context effect, such as per-call buffer churn or late threads, rather than heterogeneity alone.
4. Drop the J/K scaling numbers taken from the native profiles.
